stories.Headline: Tencent reports slower revenue growth as AI demand boosts cloud unit
stories.Summary:
China's Tencent reported an eight per cent climb in third quarter revenue on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, in Beijing. This growth was weaker than expectations and results from the previous quarter because gaming business growth cooled. The company reported revenue of 207.3 billion yuan, which is equal to 31.1 billion US dollars, for September. This figure was slightly below an LSEG consensus estimate of 210.8 billion yuan, while the previous quarter grew 11 per cent. Net profit edged up 0.8 per cent to 63.61 billion yuan, beating analyst expectations of 59.46 billion yuan.

Fintech and business services, including the cloud unit, rose 9 per cent to 63.7 billion yuan due to AI demand. Value added services, including gaming, rose 3 per cent to 98.3 billion yuan, with domestic games growing 11 per cent. International games revenue slid 9 per cent, while capital expenditure in the September quarter was 81.4 billion yuan. This spending was higher than the 52.8 billion yuan spent in the June quarter for the same company. Tencent spent 84.7 billion yuan in the first half of the year, exceeding the 79 billion yuan spent in 2025.

Chief executive officer Pony Ma said cloud revenue growth increased because of WorkBuddy and more compute for GPU rental. He noted that the company allocated more compute to Model as a Service to drive the growth of cloud services. CEO Ma Huateng stated that the company is making substantial progress toward building a new, AI empowered Tencent. He mentioned this progress is happening in terms of intelligence, applications, and infrastructure for the large Chinese tech firm. These leaders are managing heavy AI spending to see if it pays off or if it is squeezing margins.

Investors are monitoring the spending, and shares in Chinese cloud service providers, including Tencent, slid on Tuesday. These investors are concerned about whether the heavy spending on artificial intelligence is starting to pay off for the firm. Other affected parties include Chinese tech giants who have struggled to obtain advanced Nvidia chips because of US export restrictions. Washington announced new rules this week that restrict remote access to advanced US AI chips through overseas data centres. These restrictions have put Chinese companies on the back foot compared to their competitors in the United States.

Tencent said a year ago that chip shortages were constraining its cloud growth as it prioritised internal AI chip use. The company prioritised using these chips internally over renting computing power to external clients during that specific time period. The articles mention that CXMT has overtaken Tencent as the most valuable Chinese firm amid a general AI frenzy. Tencent also released an AI image model to compete with other companies like ByteDance and the firm Alibaba. Reports indicate that Tencent leases 100,000 chips from Oracle to accelerate its push into the artificial intelligence field.

The company will continue to monitor if its heavy AI spending is paying off or if it is squeezing margins. It remains to be seen how enterprises will navigate power constraints and sustainability targets while using these cloud services. The articles leave open how the new Washington rules on remote chip access will impact long term growth for Tencent. It is unclear if the company can overcome the struggle to obtain advanced Nvidia chips due to US export restrictions. Future results will show if the AI image model successfully catches competitors like ByteDance and the firm Alibaba.

stories.Headline: Shopify builds Remote Dev to let AI agents run iOS and Android builds in parallel
stories.Summary:
Shopify built Remote Dev, a remote mobile development environment, so AI agents can independently build, test and maintain iOS and Android applications in parallel, InfoQ reported on November 17, 2026. Shopify engineers said running agentic workflows in parallel quickly hogs all resources available on development machines. They said three or four workflows were enough to max out a laptop, on top of resources already consumed by compilers, simulators and emulators. They said that if someone accidentally closed a laptop lid, the work stopped. Shopify had previously built River for web and backend development, but River is a Linux-based solution and could not be used for building iOS apps.

Remote Dev uses a fleet of remote Macs running Shopify's development environment and iOS simulators, accessible via SSH. Android emulators run on separate Linux VMs, and the architecture lets developers build and test both iOS and Android builds through the same SSH session. Each River session gets its own environment, so one agent can debug on Android, another can work on an iOS feature and another can test a PR, all in parallel. Agents can be accessed through a Slack channel backed by River. Remote Dev can implement changes, build the app, run tests, interact with the simulators, collect screenshots and create a PR, and if something fails it can inspect the logs, fix the issue and try again.

Shopify says that with Remote Dev it is no longer limited by how many builds and simulators its laptops can handle. Shopify promoted internal adoption through demonstrations and storytelling, and River's share of merged PRs increased from 6% to 61%. Shopify says the platform supports automated workflows, including overnight runs that identify bugs, implement fixes and submit PRs. Shopify says agents can verify a build is functional by navigating through the app, interacting with its UI, reproducing bugs, recording current behavior, implementing fixes and running the same interaction to verify the fix. Shopify says it plans to expand the platform with continuous application health monitoring, automated crash detection and fixes, and PR generation for identified issues, among other capabilities.

Raiyan Jugbhery, in charge of software infrastructure and founder at SpendMe, argued on LinkedIn that the key advantage of Remote Dev is its Xcode and iOS Simulator integration. He noted that a PR you still have to pull and verify on a Mac isn't really autonomous. He pointed out that the article does not explain how Shopify keeps builds from queuing when several agents ask for a Mac at once, which he identified as a key concern. Junaid Raza, solutions architect at Hoboetech, raised another concern, saying that allowing agents to run the simulator could lead to unreliable test results. Raza said that if you give an agent a red test and enough retries, it will sometimes rewrite the test until it passes, and he suggests prohibiting runner agents from modifying the tests they execute.

Tether's QVAC is built on the premise of running AI models directly on the user's device, Network World reported on November 18, 2026. With QVAC, data never leaves the hardware, there are no per-request costs, no rate limits, and no need for an internet connection once a model is downloaded. Open-source tools and standards like llama.cpp, GGML and ONNX have made local AI much more accessible in recent years, but the edge AI ecosystem remains fragmented. In 2026, Tether released a software development kit that pulls together the best open tooling from across different domains of machine learning. The centerpiece of Tether's QVAC SDK is Fabric, which is built on llama.cpp and expands the engine to enable on-device fine tuning and additional AI capabilities.

Building on GGML's modular framework, QVAC Fabric is primarily oriented toward three backends: Vulkan, which covers most consumer-grade desktop and mobile chips; Metal and Core ML for Apple Silicon; and CUDA for higher-end NVIDIA GPU setups. The QVAC SDK gives developers a unified interface for building multiplatform AI apps that run on-device. RAG requires a second embedding model and a vector index alongside the core language model's inference, and these vector indexes can be huge, often much larger than the plain text files they represent and easily surpassing the RAM capacity of consumer hardware. As a result, most RAG operations are offloaded to the cloud, along with the user's personal information. In September 2026, the QVAC SDK integrated TurboVec, an open-source vector index that shrinks embedding memory usage by up to 8 times (4-bit quantized).

Frontier-scale systems typically need data-center GPUs and hundreds of gigabytes of memory, so the QVAC SDK integrates quantized versions of common open-source models, and Tether has also developed its own lightweight models designed to run on a phone or personal computer, distributed peer-to-peer via its registry. QVAC Psy is a family of specialized low-weight models that run on the QVAC SDK, and each model is trained with specially curated training data to perform specific tasks at the same or a higher level than much larger AI platforms. Despite weighing in at just 800 million parameters, the smallest variant of Tether's translation model for African languages outperformed Google's 27 billion parameter TranslateGemma on key benchmarks. Processing sensitive information directly on local hardware addresses privacy concerns and can help ease compliance with regulations like GDPR and HIPAA, opening the door for secure AI apps in the healthcare, legal and financial sectors. Without recurring API costs or expensive cloud hosting, independent creators and smaller studios can implement AI features that previously required enterprise-scale budgets.

stories.Headline: OpenAI funds $255,000 Effingham schools grant as students design projects
stories.Summary:
Three Effingham County residents sued OpenAI, local officials and others in November, alleging that plans for Project Camellia were kept secret until key decisions had been made, and the allegations have not been proven in court. OpenAI is the artificial intelligence company behind the ChatGPT platform. Project Camellia is OpenAI’s proposed $20 billion artificial intelligence data center campus at the Savannah Gateway Industrial Hub near Rincon. The proposal has drawn opposition from residents who raised concerns about transparency, electricity demand, water use, traffic and noise. County commissioners postponed a decision on the project’s preliminary site plan on Nov. 3 and were expected to revisit it Tuesday.

The District Innovation Challenge provides up to $15,000 for each of the Effingham County School District’s 17 schools, backed by $255,000 from OpenAI. Students and educators will work together on proposals that could address technology, STEM, artificial intelligence literacy, sustainability or other school and community needs. Following Tuesday’s districtwide kickoff, students and staff will develop project ideas, itemized budgets and presentations, and the district’s curriculum and technology departments will host presentations and question-and-answer sessions. In January, each school will review proposals and select a group of projects totaling up to $15,000 to represent it at the district level. Finalist student teams will present their ideas to a district panel in February.

Superintendent Yancy Ford said public education thrives when students are given real ownership over their learning and the resources to bring bold ideas to life. Ford said that through this partnership with OpenAI, students are not just learning about the future but are actively designing it for their classrooms, their schools and the Effingham County community. The panel will include Ford, school board representatives, district curriculum and technology leaders, and representatives from the data center and AI industries. Rather than serving as a high-stakes elimination contest, the panel will offer feedback and formally award funding to participating projects, the district said. OpenAI said it would continue working with county officials to address outstanding questions.

Supporters point to potential tax revenue and opportunities for local businesses from Project Camellia. OpenAI has pledged at least $80 million for community priorities tied to Project Camellia. The company also provided a $4.8 million grant to cover Effingham County students’ school breakfast and lunch costs for the 2026-27 school year. In October, OpenAI announced a $2 million grant for the first phase of Atlas Park, a planned recreation area at a former sand mine.

Students across Effingham County will have a chance to turn their ideas for improving their schools into reality through the new grant program. The Pike County Board of Commissioners will hold a special meeting on Wednesday, Nov. 18, to discuss and potentially approve a non-binding term sheet from SoftBank Energy and OpenAI for the PORTS-Pike data center project in Piketon. The special meeting will occur at 10:30 a.m. at the Pike County Administration Building, located at 230 Waverly Plaza in Waverly.

The county said the purpose is to consider, discuss and possibly act on the proposed non-binding term sheet, with possible actions including a resolution approving the term sheet and authorizing its execution and any related matters. The notice said the elected county board could also enter into a private executive session to discuss matters related to the data center deal. An agenda with more details has not yet been published for the special AI data center meeting. Japan’s SoftBank and OpenAI want to redevelop the U.S. Department of Energy Portsmouth Gaseous Diffusion Plant into a new data center.

The 3,700-acre U.S. government plant previously enriched uranium for nuclear weapons and later for nuclear energy plants, and it operated from 1957 to 2001. The plant property is owned by the U.S. Department of Energy, and adjacent privately owned properties have also been acquired as part of the planned AI data center development. At full buildout, there could be as many as 18 data center buildings at the southeastern Ohio site, and the AI development is projected to create 35,000 construction jobs and 2,500 permanent, operational jobs, according to the companies. AI chipmaker NVIDIA will provide the AI infrastructure at the data center, and the development also entails significant electricity infrastructure investments and upgrades.

stories.Headline: Marian Kamenistak builds a 123-automation AI executive assistant that saves an estimated 361 hours a month
stories.Summary:
Marian Kamenistak, VP of Engineering at Mews, published on hackernoon.com on 18 November 2026 an account of the AI executive assistant he built. He made an inventory of his automations on 25 October 2026 and found one job that had reported success for 48 days while its access key was being rejected. Another job sent LinkedIn messages on a Sunday because its schedule was off by one day, and a group of other jobs succeeded about 60% of the time and never alerted him. In late October 2026 he saw about 70% of his jobs failing on a dashboard he had built that weekend. He dropped meetings that were not critical and started fixing things, and found the root cause was that most jobs ran from his local PC, which was not plugged in.

The assistant is 123 scheduled automations, a set of AI skills and one dashboard he calls the Control Room, with 1,506 steps and 948 connections between them as captured on 15 November 2026. It saves an estimated 361 hours of work a month, about 4,330 hours a year, equal to 2.3 extra people at 160 hours a person a month. People cost avoided is €14,428 a month and €173,141 a year, or 352,415 and 4,228,980 Czech crowns, while the cost of running the automations is €464 a month and €5,569 a year, or 11,335 and 136,020 crowns, leaving €13,964 a month and €167,573 a year saved after costs. Euros are converted at the Czech National Bank fixing of 13 November 2026, 24.425 CZK per EUR, and 176 of the 361 hours are work he would otherwise have hired for, an SDR or a virtual assistant, about 1.1 people. With the tools he would pay for anyway the bill is about €811 a month, every subscription he pays is about €1,204, and none of the three totals includes his build time, which was one weekend for the dashboard and another 3 weeks to a month for the full monthly cycle.

He kept his personal human EA, Lucie, and calls it the best decision he could do, because she keeps him accountable and resolves everything on the spot. He says she was very persistent about making sure he invested his time into the right decisions and urges him to pay attention to non-business things, which go into relationships with his teammates. In invoicing the AI reads the bank lines and matches each one to a document, and Lucie finds the documents the AI can't, in Drive first, then Gmail, then the supplier portals. From July to October 2026, 79 of 248 bank lines were waiting for a document. He says the AI does the recurring work and Lucie does the part where somebody has to go and find the thing and decide on the spot.

ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini all answer "hybrid" when asked whether to replace an executive assistant with AI, and he agrees with hybrid and pays for it every month. Perplexity, asked on 15 November 2026, put an assistant stack at $20 to $200 a month and its upkeep at 2 to 8 hours a month, and ChatGPT leaned on vendor price pages such as Lindy's and cited a Forrester study commissioned by Microsoft for Copilot Studio where one customer says an agent saved 4 hours per user a month. He says those numbers are fair for one tool on one desk, while his bill is for a whole back office. The assistant serves five business streams: the Engineering Leaders Community, the ELC Conference, the Academy, hiring through Marian's List, and his mentoring at marian.coach. Tereza is Head of Community, and they have two recurring meetings, weekly preparation for the next week and checking the Control Room on the web, and monthly review of past KPIs and setting KPIs for the next month.

He spent 20+ years in software development and was VP of Engineering at Mews, where engineering grew from 8 to 80 teams, which is why he could build it himself. The plumbing needed an engineer, but writing down his niche, his ideal customer and his KPIs didn't, and that is the part that made the AI useful. The automations ran before the AI knew what business it was working for, and the fix was setting the niche, ICP and KPIs so the AI knows the context. Every stream must have a niche and a mission, one sentence each, max 160 characters, and concrete as to who, what and which geography, and his mentoring niche starts with one-to-one leadership mentoring for engineering and product leaders in Czechia and Central Europe. The ICP has 1 to 4 segments with consumers and companies kept separate, each saying who they are, what they buy and where that comes from, and one thing the company segment of his mentoring stream buys is a Mentor in Residence.

A watchdog now runs every hour in the cloud, off the Mac, and expects a heartbeat from each job, so a job silent past its schedule counts as failed and an unplugged computer can't hide. The AI may not fix outreach senders, finance and logins on its own, because a wrong fix on a sender goes out to real people, and there is a limit of at most 5 fixes a day and 1 per job per 7 days. A test on 15 November went from approved to fixed in 2 minutes, and he refurbished his 7-year-old MacBook Pro to run the local jobs. On 15 November 2026 the coverage page showed 140 jobs OK, 4 failing and 30 stale, the home page read "4 of 5 goals on track" with 1 goal behind, qualified mentoring leads, and 9 things wait for a person and 136 of 167 automations working. The 123 in the post is the count in the savings model of 14 November 2026, each page counts a different set of jobs and the set changes daily, and the system refuses to publish a stream missing its niche, ICP or KPIs, showing a target without a source as unsourced.

stories.Headline: DistroKid gives UMG and Sony data on AI music in Suno lawsuit
stories.Summary:
DistroKid provided data about AI-generated music on its platform to Universal Music Group and Sony Music after initially refusing, according to a Monday November 16 court filing obtained by Billboard. The subpoena sought numbers on how much music passing through the DIY distributor is thought to be made with Suno and other AI generators. UMG and Sony say the data is key to proving Suno-generated music eats into their market share and royalty distributions. DistroKid is not a party to the Suno suit. The filing withdrew the subpoena petition after the distributor produced responsive documents.

The subpoena sought numbers regarding how much of the music passing through the leading DIY digital distributor is thought to be made with Suno and other AI generators. Competition between AI songs and human music is a key part of the fair use inquiry, the test a judge will use to decide whether Suno infringed the majors' copyrights by training on millions of unlicensed tracks. DistroKid initially refused to provide AI data, leading the labels to initiate a legal action last month seeking to force compliance. The distributor has since changed its tune and produced responsive documents, according to Monday's filing. Reps for DistroKid and Sony declined to comment on Tuesday November 17, and reps for UMG did not return a request for comment.

A DistroKid spokesperson said the company takes copyright protection, fraud prevention and the integrity of the music ecosystem seriously and works closely with digital streaming platforms, rightsholders and other industry partners. The spokesperson said DistroKid strongly disagrees with UMG's allegations and is disappointed UMG chose litigation rather than established industry processes. The spokesperson said DistroKid is confident in its practices and intends to defend DistroKid vigorously. UMG alleges DistroKid is to blame for a surge in AI music on streaming services like Spotify. That case, filed in September, alleges deceptive business practices and copyright violations by flooding streamers with what UMG called mass AI-generated, SEO-optimized, and copyright-infringing slop.

Universal and Sony are fighting Suno's attempt to put their second copyright lawsuit entirely on hold, arguing in papers filed in Boston federal court last Friday November 13 that a full pause could keep the case frozen into 2028. Under Suno's plan, its 2025 and 2026 models and business conduct, including v6 launched in September, would be examined nowhere until at least 2028, the labels claim in the 17-page filing. Suno asked Judge F. Dennis Saylor IV on October 30 to pause the second case until he rules on summary judgment in the first lawsuit, filed in June 2024. Suno's main defense is fair use, arguing training its AI on copyrighted recordings is lawful without a license. Suno also said that if Saylor rules in its favor on fair use, or on the labels' separate claim that it stream-ripped recordings from YouTube, the first case could foreclose the labels' theories in the second.

The labels agree the fair use ruling will shape the second case and have offered to postpone proving ownership of the more than 60,000 recordings at issue until Saylor rules. In the first case, fact discovery on the infringement claims has largely closed, while discovery on the stream-ripping claim runs until this Friday November 20, and summary judgment motions are due by June 22, 2027. The second lawsuit, filed September 18, accuses Suno of copying 60,202 of the labels' recordings without a license, and US copyright law caps statutory damages for willful infringement at USD $150,000 per work, a theoretical maximum of just over USD $9 billion. The labels also ask the court to order Suno to stop further use of their recordings. The dispute began in June 2024, when Universal, Sony and Warner Music Group sued Suno, and Warner settled and struck a licensing deal in November 2025, leaving the case covering 560 of Universal and Sony's recordings.

In May this year Universal and Sony asked to add 61,026 more recordings to the original case after tracing them inside Suno's training data, and the second suit asserts slightly fewer, 60,202. Saylor refused on August 18, saying adding them will have obvious consequences of complexity and delay, and steered the labels toward a separate lawsuit, writing that evidence-gathering in any new case could proceed on a different schedule, or indeed be stayed pending resolution of the fair use issue. Suno says that means the court has already contemplated a stay, while the labels counter that a stay was only one of several options Saylor listed and point out he also said the new case could also be potentially consolidated, in whole or in part, with the first. Suno launched its v6 models on September 9, nine days before the second suit was filed, saying they were built in partnership with Warner, BMG and Believe. In the first case, called Suno I in the filing, the labels say Suno's document handover largely stops at February 2025 and no witness has been put forward to explain how v6 was trained.

The labels say Suno has taken the position in Suno I that the full picture of its 2025 and 2026 models and licensing conduct are outside that case's scope, and now asks the Court to stay the only action in which that conduct can be examined. The labels warn the danger is concrete, saying that by the time discovery into v6 could begin under Suno's proposal the engineers who built the models may have moved on and their recollections faded. The labels say they recently learned the engineer responsible for Suno's data scraping and training data acquisition has left the company. Suno said in its motion it is retaining relevant data in accordance with its legal preservation obligations and that the first case's record will preserve testimony from past years, while the labels reply this covers documents, not what engineers know. Instead of a full pause the labels proposed a partial stay with three parts: putting off proving ownership of the 60,000-plus recordings, letting evidence-gathering go ahead now on Suno's later models including how v6 was trained, its licensing efforts, its funding rounds and investor pitches and its recent finances, and letting everything handed over in the first case count in the second.

stories.Headline: Anthropic's Claude Code team writes and reviews about 90% of its code with Claude
stories.Summary:
On the Claude Code team at Anthropic, roughly 90% of code is written and reviewed by Claude, Addy Osmani wrote in a claude.dev blog post published November 16, 2026. Verification loops let the team run dozens or hundreds of Claudes in parallel instead of only one or two at a time. In internal testing around structured file generation, a separate grader checking Claude's work against a rubric improved task success by up to 10 points over a standard prompting loop. The largest gains came on the hardest problems. The team uses end-to-end, property and differential tests to verify work with evidence.

The team's reliability checklist has 39 items, each with a trigger readable from a diff, a check, and the incidents or PRs behind it. Claude reads the diff and checks only the items whose trigger matches, usually 3 to 10. If a check is still failing after three rounds, Claude stops and brings in a human. Code Review reads the REVIEW.md file from the base or default branch, never from the pull request's changes. A commit gate can block a commit if the session did not contain /code-review or /verify, with off, observe and enforce modes, and if commits have been blocked twice in the session the next one is allowed through.

Code owners write their own checks and refine them until they flag what the owner would flag, and a check that pulls in a reviewer should say why. The team does not stack a second, more expensive reviewer on top of the primary one, preferring to tune the primary and point each pass at context from earlier rounds and past failures. The team stamps each commit with how it was verified, including "none" so commits that weren't verified can be queried. Observe mode logs what would have been blocked so false positives can be reviewed. The team tracks how many merged changes were reverted, how many changes a maintainer rejected before merging, and a size-matched subset of changes that have stayed clean.

Code Review tags findings as Important, Nit or Pre-existing, the last meaning the reviewer shouldn't hold the author responsible for something that was already a bug. The Code Review team recreates the repo to the state at the time of review for each example and provides a one-sentence answer key to what the bug was, and only findings that correctly describe the bug get points. They use merged and stable changes as a control to prevent over-flagging, and their tuning set is split out from the fixed test set. They evaluated recall separately for raw findings, post-verification and final review. The team tunes recall up to the point where the next improvement would be overfitting to the eval rather than actually catching bugs.

The article says the team has previously written about how code review works at Anthropic, and this article aims to go deeper on how the team verifies its work. It says what was once expensive to verify, such as tests, benchmarks, specs and real end-to-end runs, is now cheap to request from an agent. It warns that flaky tests train the agent to run them again rather than fixing the failing code, and slow tests mean the agent does fewer tests across batches. It says property libraries keep agents honest by using edge cases not created with the same bias as the agent that created the original code, and are helpful for rewrites when the spec has drifted from production behavior. It says differential tests are particularly effective for large-scale migration use cases where functionality is expected to remain the same.

The article says Claude can test the whole app the way a human or QA engineer would, using the Claude Chrome extension for web changes, an iOS or Android MCP for mobile, computer use for desktop, or running the service locally for backend work. It says to create a skill called verify in a .claude/skills/ folder in the repo, as close to the relevant code as possible, and Claude knows to use it before committing changes. It says this is how nearly all changes are tested at Anthropic. It says the team has two methods of turning missed cases into rules, the first being extracting patterns in human code review comments and PR reverts, which must occur in at least two PRs and be identifiable from a diff. It says three agents will try to do something, and the text stops there.

stories.Headline: Google raises Gemini chat retention to about two months even with history off
stories.Summary:
Google updated the Gemini privacy policy on Monday, November 17, 2026, raising the conversation retention period from 72 hours to around two months, as reported by Gizmodo, IBTimes and TechCrunch. The change was made by Google for its flagship AI tool Gemini, according to Gizmodo. Gizmodo reporter AJ Dellinger published his story on November 17, 2026 at 5:00 pm ET. The updated Gemini Apps Privacy Hub page carried a notice that future chats will still be saved for around 2 months even if Gemini History is turned off. An archived version of the Gemini Apps Privacy Hub had a last update date of October 13, 2026, according to Gizmodo.

The retention period rises from 72 hours to around two months, and Temporary Chats will also be kept for around two months, according to Google's updated privacy documentation cited by IBTimes. Gemini History defaults to 18 months and can be changed to three months, 36 months or indefinite, and saved chats can be deleted at any time, Gizmodo reported. The Gemini History option in user settings still describes the retention period as 72 hours, Gizmodo said. Google's new settings let users keep their Gemini chat history while opting out of generative AI model training, and the new training controls are off by default, according to IBTimes. Conversations reviewed by human reviewers and associated information can be retained for up to three years even if users later delete their history, and feedback can lead to a conversation, attachments and other relevant information being reviewed and retained for up to three years, IBTimes reported.

Google declined to provide a comment to Gizmodo and instead directed it to a blog post titled "We're updating controls in the Gemini app." In that post Google said it was giving users more control over when Gemini chat history is used to train generative AI models. Google said the longer retention period was intended to strengthen safety and security protections as AI systems become increasingly capable, according to IBTimes. Google said retained information may be used to respond to requests, process feedback and protect the company, its users and the public. Google's updated Gemini Apps Privacy Hub also cites potential system failures as a reason for retaining chats and says temporary conversations are not used to train AI models, TechCrunch reported.

OpenAI claims it holds onto temporary chats for up to 30 days, and Anthropic says conversations with Claude are held for 30 days by default, with both noting they may hold certain chat logs longer if necessary, according to Gizmodo. TechCrunch said OpenAI may keep temporary ChatGPT chats for up to 30 days and Anthropic retains incognito Claude chats for 30 days by default, though companies may keep some data longer for legal or safety reasons or to investigate policy violations. The Register reported Tuesday that archived versions of Google's privacy documentation confirmed the earlier three-day limit, IBTimes said. Under the updated policy, conversations may remain associated with a user's Google Account during the temporary retention period even though they do not appear in the user's visible Gemini History, according to IBTimes. Google says conversations sent to service providers for review are disconnected from users' accounts, IBTimes reported.

Until now, chat history and AI training were tied to a single "Keep Activity" setting, TechCrunch reported. Previously, retaining Gemini conversation history was more closely tied to allowing Google to use those interactions to improve its AI systems, according to IBTimes. Google's documentation states that future chat content will not be used to train generative AI models when the training setting is disabled, except in certain circumstances including when users voluntarily submit feedback, IBTimes said. Temporary Chats are also excluded from generative AI model training, although Google still retains them temporarily for operational and safety purposes, according to IBTimes. Google warns that deleting Gemini history does not necessarily remove information saved through connected Google services, which may follow their own privacy and retention policies, and advises users not to enter confidential information they would not want a reviewer to see, IBTimes reported.

The updates will begin rolling out globally over the coming weeks, according to IBTimes. Google did not answer TechCrunch's questions about what prompted the change and whether it would affect how conversations are accessed or reviewed. Gizmodo said the Gemini History option in user settings will presumably update when the change goes into effect. Users who want to review their choices can open Gemini, go to Settings and select History, and can also manage retention preferences through Gemini History, according to IBTimes. Individual users may see different options while the global rollout is underway, and for users who leave chat history enabled the default automatic deletion period remains 18 months, IBTimes reported.

stories.Headline: Anthropic sets $83 share price for Nasdaq debut under ticker ANT
stories.Summary:
Anthropic set the share price for its US stock market debut at $83 on Wednesday, positioning the artificial intelligence company for one of the biggest initial public offerings in history. The firm is slated to begin trading on Thursday under the ticker symbol ANT. CEO Dario Amodei and other co-founders will ring the bell to open the Nasdaq exchange. The pricing is above Anthropic’s earlier estimates. Last week the San Francisco-based company, founded in 2021, set its preliminary share price at $70 to $78.

With all shares counted, those prices put Anthropic’s initial public offering from $1.26tn to $1.41tn. Elon Musk’s SpaceX debuted on Wall Street in June with the biggest market offering ever at $1.77tn. With Anthropic setting its share price at $83, it could now surpass SpaceX. Amodei is planning to sell about $260m worth of shares with the IPO, as are his six fellow co-founders. At the top of the price range, the co-founders’ stakes will be worth more than $18bn each.

When Anthropic filed for its IPO last month, the company detailed rapidly rising revenue in its prospectus: $41m in 2023, $386m in 2024, $4.585bn in 2025, an increase of more than 1,000%, then $16.286bn in the first six months of 2026 alone. The company disclosed that, as of the end of June, it had raised $141.1bn. Despite the increasing revenue, Anthropic disclosed a net loss of $80bn for the first half of 2026. Anthropic’s main expenditure listed in its investor prospectus is computing power from datacenters. The company has compute purchase commitments and lease agreements of more than $70bn over the next 12 months and more than $450bn by 2030, with a further $450bn due by 2045.

Anthropic is the first company at the forefront of the generative AI boom to go public, and its performance is likely to affect investors’ enthusiasm. Its competitor OpenAI was slated to hit Wall Street later this year, but CEO Sam Altman has said that the company opted to delay its IPO until it can overcome safety concerns. Anthropic’s IPO comes during a volatile time for AI and the stock market. Last month, the industry saw a broader slowdown, with share prices dropping at several companies amid growing concern about the technology. Then, last week, Nvidia, which designs the chips AI companies use to power their chatbots, was racked with a scandal that led to CEO Jensen Huang resigning after reports of multiple extramarital affairs.

FP Markets, a Forex and CFD broker, will add Anthropic (ANT.xnas) to its Share CFD offering, with Anthropic trading going live on 19 November 2026 for clients worldwide. Anthropic will be available to trade on the FP Markets MetaTrader 5, cTrader, and TradingView. The new addition will match the standard trading hours of other US-listed Share CFDs on FP Markets, with competitive commission rates applied across all transactions. FP Markets Chief Market Analyst Aaron Hill commented that the debut of Anthropic is a defining moment in the AI trade. FP Markets is a global, multi-regulated, award-winning broker established in Sydney, Australia in 2005.

Anthropic is set to become by far the most valuable company on the stock market with the legal designation of a public benefit corporation, or P.B.C. That status requires Anthropic to prioritize its corporate mission, to develop safe A.I. systems “for the long-term benefit of humanity,” in addition to the customary sole focus on value for stockholders. The company’s public benefit mandate is guarded partly by a five-member “long-term benefit trust,” which includes Ben Bernanke, the former Federal Reserve chair. Todd Underwood, a former Anthropic engineering leader, said the company “will choose to do things in favor of safety rather than in favor of making money.” He added that he agreed with that focus but thought it might turn off some investors.

stories.Headline: Teletrac Navman launches AI driver monitoring sensor to detect fatigue earlier
stories.Summary:
Teletrac Navman launched its new Driver Monitoring Sensor on 19 November 2026, announcing it from Sydney through PR Newswire. The company described the device as an AI-powered driver-facing visual sensor that tracks micro eye movements to identify early signs of driver drowsiness and fatigue. It is available within Smart Dashcam Quad, which Teletrac Navman calls the latest addition to its Smart Dashcam ecosystem. Smart Dashcam Quad combines four HD cameras with AI-powered video analytics to identify risky behaviours, deliver real-time coaching and provide actionable driver insights. Teletrac Navman said the sensor is designed to help safety-conscious fleet operators intervene sooner and reduce the risk of fatigue-related incidents.

DMS is a purpose-built visual sensor mounted on the vehicle's dashboard with a clear view of the driver's eyes, face and head. It measures blink patterns, eye closure percentage and head movements, and warning signs such as slow or excessive blinking help flag tiredness early. It can identify microsleeps and extended eye closures, including nodding off, and its infrared capability lets it operate in low and harsh light. It can detect drowsiness through many non-polarised sunglasses and high-visibility gear, and it generates compound alerts by combining indicators with advanced driver assistance system data such as lane deviation. Smart Dashcam Quad launches in Australia and New Zealand on 19 November, and DMS works alongside it.

Ricardo Buranello, CEO of Teletrac Navman, said the most effective way to manage fatigue risk is to stop incidents before they occur. He said DMS is designed to detect early signs of fatigue, which can help prevent events and incidents and support a safer environment. He said fatigue management is about creating a proactive safety culture, not simply responding to incidents after they occur. He said that by combining scientifically recognised fatigue indicators with real-time alerts and reporting, DMS helps businesses build stronger safety programs while supporting their duty-of-care obligations. Teletrac Navman said its goal is to empower industries that transform and sustain futures with simple and intelligent solutions.

IT Brief Australia reported that the product is aimed at transport, logistics and heavy vehicle operators, where fatigue management remains a core safety issue. It reported that businesses in these sectors face ongoing pressure to show they are taking practical steps to reduce fatigue-related incidents and meet duty-of-care requirements. It reported that operators are increasingly adopting such systems as insurers, regulators and corporate safety teams demand more detailed evidence of driver risk controls. It reported that the launch adds to a growing market for driver monitoring tools that combine AI analysis with in-vehicle hardware and fleet management software. It reported that Teletrac Navman already offers drowsiness detection across its wider safety products.

Teletrac Navman said drowsiness detection is already available across its safety solutions, but DMS takes detection a step further by tracking micro eye movements rather than relying solely on late-stage visual cues. The company said this is designed to enable earlier identification of fatigue and help further reduce the risk of incidents. IT Brief Australia reported that the new sensor extends that approach by focusing on micro eye movements rather than relying only on visible fatigue cues. It reported that the company says this should allow earlier intervention before a fatigue event escalates. Teletrac Navman operates globally, with offices worldwide and headquarters in Anaheim, CA.

When DMS detects drowsiness, the driver receives multiple audio alerts in the vehicle along with haptic feedback through seat vibration where fitted. The back-office team receives real-time, severity-based notifications so they can act sooner, and alerts weigh multiple signals to determine severity. A dedicated management dashboard helps safety teams prioritise risk with historical reporting that reveals recurring behaviours and supports more targeted coaching. Automated drowsiness detection and severity classification help businesses with limited time to review events, and DMS records interventions and follow-up actions, creating an audit trail. The articles leave open what the sensor costs, when it will reach markets beyond Australia and New Zealand, and how many fleets have adopted it.

stories.Headline: KPMG runs first full parallel AI audit of a FTSE 250 company
stories.Summary:
KPMG ran a full AI-powered parallel audit of a FTSE 250 company for the first time this year, according to a Financial Times report. The Big Four firm deployed more than 100 AI agents that worked through every phase of the annual audit alongside the conventional one. The official audit opinion was based on the regular audit. The experiment is called "Project Exponential" inside KPMG. The agents independently collected, analyzed, and documented data and drafted audit conclusions.

KPMG is rolling out KPMG Clara intelligence, or KCi, in the United States, announced November 17, embedding specialized AI agents into audit workflows. The deployment extends the existing KPMG Clara platform across risk assessment, transaction analysis, engagement coordination, and testing support. KCi has been rolling out to more than 125 U.S. teams and 500 teams globally following use during 2026. The next objective is deployment across all private company audits in 2027, with a separate, phased rollout planned for public company audits. Automated data pipelines can analyze complete transaction populations in selected audit areas, identifying unusual items, trends, and anomalies for targeted investigation.

In several cases "AI was able to go so much deeper" than the regular audit team, said Cath Burnet, KPMG's UK head of audit. In some situations, she said, the technology asked "better questions" than the firm's own auditors. Christian Peo, vice chair of Audit and Assurance at KPMG U.S., framed the opportunity as giving auditors more time to understand information and challenge what does not make sense, rather than automating their judgment. "Whatever technology a firm uses, the auditor remains accountable," said Mark Babington, the FRC's executive director of regulatory standards. Auditors must be able to explain how they used AI, challenge its results, and stand behind the evidence, he said.

The UK's accounting regulator, the FRC, published guidance just days ago that applies existing independence rules to the use of AI. The core question is when auditors may share findings from AI-powered audits with their clients without compromising independence. Under certain circumstances, the FRC says, sharing those findings could pose a "distinct threat" to auditor independence. Certain findings, such as major weaknesses in internal controls, still must be reported to clients, and the FRC says these mandatory disclosures don't count as non-audit services. KPMG says human involvement remained "critical," with staff setting goals for the agents, providing context, reviewing work periodically, and challenging conclusions before the audit opinion was finalized.

Two partners and a director worked alongside senior managers and junior staff. In one area a human had to intervene because an AI agent couldn't correctly match a set of regulations against company documents. KPMG plans to expand the project to as many as 20 larger audits, though the technology isn't yet available at the scale needed for thousands of audits, Burnet said. Few companies currently have clean enough data for AI agents to work with reliably, she said. KPMG says the system offers "full visibility and full traceability," recording agent interactions with documents down to individual characters and timestamps.

After construction and outsourcing group Carillion collapsed in 2018, a parliamentary inquiry found that KPMG, as the company's longtime auditor, had failed to challenge management's "increasingly fantastical figures" for 19 years. Two KPMG entities were fined a total of £21 million as a result. Rival PwC has already run several "parallel audit" projects of its own. An internal town hall at rival Deloitte in May showed the same pressure and upset the firm's own consultants, according to the Wall Street Journal, with management presenting a chart showing the share of hourly consulting revenue shrinking to a thin sliver of the growing overall market by 2035. One Deloitte consultant summed up the message, saying, "They heavily implied our model is toast. We're basically getting replaced by robots."

KPMG sees "clear time-saving opportunities," according to the FT, but won't say whether that would lead to lower fees. KPMG International has already negotiated lower fees with its own auditor, according to an FT report, arguing that AI makes the work cheaper. KPMG reports that, on some engagements, the KCi approach shortened timelines by as much as three and a half weeks and removed the need for clients to retrieve large volumes of individual supporting documents manually. The announcement does not present that result as an average across all engagements. The technology foundation combines proprietary KPMG capabilities with enterprise technologies available through relationships with Anthropic, Google Cloud, Microsoft, and OpenAI, and the announcement does not specify which provider powers each individual KCi function.

stories.Headline: NTT DATA and IIT Jammu launch an AI centre of excellence for climate resilience
stories.Summary:
The Indian Institute of Technology Jammu and NTT DATA announced on 13 November 2026 a strategic collaboration to establish an Artificial Intelligence Centre of Excellence at IIT Jammu. NTT DATA is described as a global technology services provider and a global leader in digital business and technology services. The announcement was datelined Jammu, India, and dignitaries from both organisations exchanged MoU documents during a function in Jammu. Daily Excelsior reported the announcement on 14 November 2026, CASRAI published its editorial on 15 November 2026 and ETEducation published on 17 November 2026. The centre is intended to promote AI research, develop regional talent and address local challenges in Jammu and Kashmir.

The AI-CoE will focus on four areas: secure and responsible AI innovation, digital twins, physical AI, and research commercialisation and startup development. Secure and responsible AI covers small and large language models, agentic AI, AI governance and AI for Indian languages, with Dogri named as a target for making digital services more accessible. Potential applications include flood monitoring and early-warning systems for the Tawi and Chenab river basins and sensor-based approaches to landslide and flood risk. Physical AI combines AI with robotics, computer vision, IoT and edge computing for infrastructure monitoring, autonomous systems, situational awareness and public safety. A talent programme offers students, researchers and faculty industry projects, faculty engagement, fellowships, hackathons and hands-on training in AI, high-performance computing and edge computing.

NTT DATA will connect IIT Jammu's research capabilities with industry requirements through its global network of Innovation Centres. Avinash Joshi, Executive Managing Director for India at NTT DATA, said that AI's greatest impact happens when it helps solve real problems for people and communities. Professor Manoj Gaur, Director of IIT Jammu, said the aim is to create an environment where ideas can move from research to real-world application. Gaur said the collaboration will strengthen efforts towards research commercialisation, technology entrepreneurship and a strong deep-tech ecosystem in the region. Joshi and Gaur said the collaboration aims to translate research into practical solutions for regional challenges, with potential applications across India.

The announcement lists potential applications rather than committed projects, and adds that use cases elsewhere in the Jammu and Kashmir region are to be explored. Successful approaches could be adapted across India, and Gaur said innovations could have wider applications across India. Jammu and Kashmir's mountainous terrain and river systems present complex challenges related to floods, landslides, infrastructure planning and emergency response. The partnership will also support intellectual property development, product innovation and deep-tech startups in the region. Students, researchers and faculty are affected, along with deep-tech startups in Jammu and Kashmir and communities facing flood and landslide risks.

CASRAI describes the arrangement as an industry-hosted AI centre on a university campus combining research, student training and commercialisation. CASRAI notes that research offices weighing a similar arrangement typically need to settle the form of the sponsored research agreement, background and foreground IP, publication rights and data handling. The inclusion of AI governance in the stated scope connects to wider policy work such as India's AI governance guidelines and general principles of responsible AI. CASRAI states that membership-style models are another route to industry engagement, referring to its industry affiliates program entry. CASRAI adds that the stated emphasis on fellowships, hackathons and industry projects suggests student and faculty participation routes.

The announcement does not give financial terms, funding amounts, a duration or a governance structure for the centre. Questions such as who owns resulting intellectual property, how data is shared and how the centre will be staffed are not addressed in it. The announcement gives no eligibility rules or application process for the talent programme. CASRAI published its editorial reading of the announcement, not a statement from either organisation, and cites NTT DATA's announcement of 13 November 2026, checked 2026-11-15. CASRAI states that everything it publishes stays open to read, with no account and no card.

stories.Headline: Microsoft adopts Intel Foundry advanced packaging technology for Azure custom silicon
stories.Summary:
Microsoft announced on November 18, 2026, that it will adopt Intel Foundry's advanced packaging technology. The company will use the Embedded Multi-die Interconnect Bridge for custom silicon used in Azure. This decision involves using the EMIB-T variant to support vertical power delivery for 3D silicon modules. Microsoft will package next-generation versions of its custom silicon projects at the Intel Foundry. These projects include the Maia 200 accelerators and the Cobalt 200 CPUs for agentic workloads.

The plan requires using through-silicon vias to enable power delivery across multiple stacked chips in the package. Microsoft will use Intel Xeon processors and the upcoming Diamond Rapids Xeon 7 CPUs for Azure infrastructure. They will integrate Xeons on Compute Express Link to improve memory efficiency and system control in data centers. The company will also utilize Intel Trust Domain Extensions for confidential computing and Intel QuickAssist for operations. These optimizations have already provided a 2.5x performance increase for specific workloads like SQL backups.

Naga Chandrasekaran is the EVP, Chief Technology and Operations Officer and General Manager of Intel Foundry. He stated that Microsoft and Intel share a clear view regarding the future of AI infrastructure. He noted that these systems are increasingly complex and require co-optimization of silicon, packaging, memory and software. Chandrasekaran believes that EMIB allows the flexibility of heterogeneous integration with the manufacturing scale needed for AI. This collaboration aims to provide Azure customers with new levels of performance and economics.

Azure customers are affected by these changes as they gain better performance through advanced silicon packaging. Other industry players include Suregiant Technology, which provides release film to the top five semiconductor manufacturers. Suregiant's release film is used in 2.5D, 3D and panel-level fan-out packaging processes to prevent contamination. Chairman Yang Yun-pin stated that AI is in early growth stages with diverse applications like automotive. He noted that Suregiant does not rely on one customer but covers almost all major AI chip orders.

Suregiant entered the semiconductor field in 2014 and has supplied grinding tape to top packaging plants for 12 years. Their release film entered mass production for 2.5D packaging in 2024 and FOPLP processes in 2025. The company's release film will advance to 3D advanced packaging in 2026 to increase high-end material penetration. Yole Group statistics estimate the global advanced packaging market will grow to 79.4 billion dollars by 2030. This represents a compound annual growth rate of about 9.5 percent starting from 46.1 billion dollars in 2024.

Suregiant's Taoyuan Plant 2 will start mass production in December 2026 with 2.5 to 3 times the capacity of Plant 1. The company expects a full-year capacity contribution period in 2027 and a mid-December OTC market listing. A new thick-type grinding product was sent for first-tier verification in the fourth quarter of 2026. Official samples for hydrolyzable tape are expected in mid-2027 with a gradual ramp-up occurring in 2028. The articles leave open whether Taiwanese manufacturers can continue capturing market share from dominant Japanese material suppliers.

stories.Headline: Nigeria's electoral commission removes 1.6 million AI generated profiles from voter register
stories.Summary:
Artificial intelligence has recently begun to interfere with election discourse, creating new risks for the outcomes of future national voting processes. The Independent National Electoral Commission, known as INEC, discovered that AI was used to manipulate its official voter register. This discovery occurred around November 2026, as reported by journalist Zinab Suleiman Okino in two separate news articles. INEC responded by removing 1.6 million AI generated voters and sanctioning the staff members who were indicted for the breach. These events have heightened public suspicion regarding the potential for more sophisticated disruptions before the upcoming 2027 general elections.

The manipulated register saw voter numbers inflate from 93 million to 103 million, though INEC only flagged 268 specific irregularities. This situation requires a transparent forensic audit of databases to address the remaining 8 million profiles that may be AI generated. The 2027 election will be sensitive, and the Senate previously repealed the Electoral Act of 2022 in February 2026. That repeal rejected real time uploads to the IReV portal and upheld physical Form EC8A as the primary collation source. These changes follow previous controversies involving the Smart Card Reader during the 2015 elections in places like Rivers State.

INEC Chairman Professor Joash Amupitan spoke at a national summit titled Beyond the Ballot regarding AI, FIMI, and electoral information integrity. He stated that elections can be undermined before the first ballot is cast and that INEC cannot police the truth alone. Amupitan called for institutionalised fact checking channels and clear inter agency escalation procedures to prepare for potential AI driven information crises. The summit was held in partnership with the European Union, DAI, CEMESO, and the IPC, with all INEC commissioners attending. He emphasized the need for practical simulation exercises to help stakeholders manage the risks posed by these new technologies.

Opposition members and social media users first raised alarms after INEC published a preliminary voter register online for public scrutiny. Journalists also flagged the database for duplicate profiles, and Nigerians are now united in demanding a full forensic audit. Politicians are affected because they may use AI to their advantage but blame others if they lose the election. The public remains distrustful because a technical glitch occurred during the presidential election involving the IReV and BVAS systems. This failure broke the trust between the democratic institution and the citizens who relied on technology for transparency.

Before the AI threat, Nigerians hoped the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System and the IReV portal would guarantee free and fair elections. These tools provided real time viewing of results after authentication through facial recognition and fingerprinting, following an electoral law amendment. This shift happened after the Supreme Court ruled that the 2015 card reader was a supplement to, not a replacement for, registers. The court reversed a previous annulment of the Rivers State governorship race between Dakuku Peterside and Nyesom Wike. This legal reasoning made the later introduction of BVAS and IReV both legitimate and legal under Nigerian law.

INEC must now continue to clean its database and deploy available tools to fight electoral malpractices and bridge the credibility gap. The nation needs to strengthen digital infrastructure and seek partnerships through MoUs with Facebook, Instagram, X, and TikTok. Digital literacy is required to ensure that incorrect political communication does not go unnoticed by citizens who are not discerning. The articles leave open whether the data breach was an intentional effort to rig elections or a simple system failure. It remains unclear if the remaining millions of fake profiles will be removed before the 2027 elections begin.

stories.Headline: IBM and Confluent launch time-series foundation models for real-time forecasting
stories.Summary:
IBM and Confluent launched time-series foundation models on November 18, 2026, to provide real-time forecasting and anomaly detection. These models allow businesses to turn continuous records of change into decisions while the signals still matter for outcomes. The system uses Apache Flink to apply semantic intelligence to streaming data, making outputs available to responsible people. This technology extends the concept of foundation models from text and images to numerical data by learning general patterns. These tools help organizations avoid training separate models for every single data series by providing a common starting point.

The models run natively on CPUs in the cloud and on premises using Confluent Cloud or Confluent Platform. They have achieved more than 50 million downloads and include a family of four different foundation models. The Streamhouse architecture uses five capabilities, which are connect, stream, process, govern, and query, to serve business context. Lightning Tables provide low-latency access to current states, while Flink prepares data and invokes the forecasting and anomaly functions. These tools operate across manufacturing, retail, banking, and airlines to keep production lines in spec and detect unusual activity.

IBM and Confluent stated that their models reduce the need for dedicated GPU infrastructure by running on standard CPUs. They explained that pretrained models scale development by reducing the need to maintain separate models for each individual series. The providers noted that forecasts can incorporate recent observations as part of a streaming workflow based on pipeline configurations. They claimed that routing signals closer to decisions allows teams to combine them with business context and human judgment. These capabilities help businesses avoid making decisions based on outdated or inconsistent information from periodic batch processes.

Retail teams are affected as AI_DETECT_ANOMALIES compares sales readings with expected ranges to identify causes for low stock. Category planners use AI_FORECAST to produce 28-day forecasts with P10 to P90 ranges to calculate product reorder points. Bank fraud teams use time-series signals to compare payments with a card's recent history to request additional authentication. Execution desks use PatchTST-FM to forecast trading volume for the next 30 minutes to pace large 100,000-share orders. Reliability engineers use TSPulse to produce representations of time-series windows to search for similar historical patterns across equipment.

The articles explain that businesses generate continuous records through machine readings, payments, sales, orders, and changes in inventory. In ice cream production, engineers currently rely on QA lab measurements taken after tubs are already filled. This delay means hours of production may need rework if a warm day changes the process before results appear. The Streamhouse addresses this by continuously capturing and governing current business context to support applications and AI agents. This background shows that traditional systems often update at different times, leading to risks when acting on old data.

Next, the TTM model will read SCADA telemetry every 10 minutes to forecast product quality four hours ahead. Operators can then approve recommended freezer draw temperature and airflow setpoints to reduce rework and lower energy use. The system can be applied to other industrial equipment like ovens, dryers, kilns, and mills for proactive processes. The articles leave open how these models will integrate with other large language models and specialized machine learning systems. They do not specify the exact costs for enterprises to implement these native functions in the Confluent Cloud.

stories.Headline: Micron and Nvidia shares fall as investors weigh AI infrastructure risks despite strong Nvidia earnings
stories.Summary:
Micron Technology shares fell about 0.88 percent during early trading on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, as investors remained cautious about Nvidia. The decline occurred at 10:06 AM ET, following a period where the stock had gained in after-hours trading on Tuesday. This weakness reflected lingering concerns across the artificial intelligence trade, which also caused peer Sandisk to fall in early trading. Nvidia shares also traded lower on Wednesday despite reporting strong quarterly results and forecasting fourth-quarter revenue of 130 billion dollars. The market reaction suggested that strong demand forecasts alone were not enough to ease risks surrounding the AI infrastructure buildout.

Nvidia reported third-quarter sales of 115.8 billion dollars and net income of 65.3 billion dollars, with data center revenue reaching 108 billion dollars. The company increased supply commitments to 390 billion dollars from 279 billion dollars, primarily for multi-year procurement of memory supply. Vera Rubin delivered nearly 20 billion dollars in its first production quarter, while networking revenue topped 21 billion dollars for the period. Nvidia reported a GAAP gross margin of 74.8 percent, though it guides the fourth quarter to a range of 71 to 72 percent. Basic EPS rose to 2.71 dollars from 1.31 dollars, and the trailing net profit margin is now 62.5 percent.

Nvidia's board rejected a proposal from former CEO Jensen Huang to return to his role if it served the company's best interest. The board stated it would proceed with a search for a permanent successor to lead the company through this leadership transition. RBC Capital Markets analyst Srini Pajjuri reiterated a Buy rating and a 1,500 dollar price target for Micron on Tuesday. Pajjuri highlighted Micron's positioning in high-bandwidth memory, firmer pricing, and tighter industry supply-demand conditions as factors that could support earnings growth. Google Finance data showed 28 Buy ratings and one Hold among 29 analysts, with an average price target of 1,624 dollars.

Bearish analysts on Simply Wall St argue that rising component costs and supply chain burdens may reduce operating leverage for Nvidia. These analysts suggest that richer system content may not fully offset inflation, especially as export controls tighten and China is excluded. Investors are questioning whether AI-related capital spending can maintain its pace amid various regulatory, political, and financing concerns in the market. Micron is one of the key suppliers seeking to benefit from rising demand for specialized high-bandwidth memory products for AI infrastructure. These HBM chips are critical components that enable processors to access large volumes of data at very high speeds.

Nvidia's revenue grew from 57.0 billion dollars in the third quarter of 2026 to 115.8 billion dollars in the third quarter of 2027. The company is shifting from individual chips to a full AI factory stack to increase revenue opportunity per deployed gigawatt. Revenue opportunity per gigawatt is rising from about 18 billion dollars on Hopper to roughly 40 billion dollars on Vera Rubin. Micron has recently traded around 700 dollars, while its high-bandwidth memory and storage are treated as critical AI data center infrastructure. The broader market backdrop has remained challenging for semiconductor stocks as traders focus on near term concerns and leadership headlines.

Micron's next earnings report, expected in December, should provide a clearer picture of demand for its memory products and pricing trends. Investors will watch if the leadership transition at Nvidia affects its strategy regarding aggressive investment and financing for AI infrastructure customers. The stock could remain sensitive to developments surrounding Nvidia and broader sentiment toward investment in artificial intelligence until the December report. The articles leave open whether the gap between Nvidia's strong fundamentals and its share price will narrow in the coming quarters. It remains unclear if Micron can fully capitalize on AI infrastructure spending despite the current pressure on its stock price.

stories.Headline: Tencent misses third quarter sales estimates as AI infrastructure spending rises
stories.Summary:
Tencent released its third quarter earnings report on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, showing that sales missed analyst estimates. The company disclosed that its WorkBuddy AI product surpassed 10 million daily users during this specific reporting period. ByteDance also reported that its Doubao Work AI tool exceeded 8 million daily active users on November 18. Tencent stated that WorkBuddy revenue over seven days implied an annualized run rate of more than 500 million dollars. ByteDance reported that Doubao Work annual recurring revenue from enterprise customers exceeded 2 billion yuan, or 300 million dollars.

Tencent revenue rose 8 percent to 207.34 billion yuan, falling below the Dim Sum Daily analyst forecast of 210.2 billion yuan. Operating profit fell 7 percent to 59.15 billion yuan, missing the Newsquawk analyst expectation of 66.6 billion yuan. Capital spending hit 81.4 billion yuan, which was far above the 55.4 billion yuan that analysts had originally expected. Free cash flow fell to minus 69.1 billion yuan, while general and administrative expenses climbed 29 percent to 44.08 billion yuan. Shares in Hong Kong closed down 0.85 percent at 372.80 Hong Kong dollars on turnover of nearly 8 billion.

Tencent stated that 90 percent of its engineers use the CodeBuddy programming tool, which is built on the Hunyuan model. The company reported that Hunyuan Image 3.0, launched in September, beat Google DeepMind's Nano Banana on a leading image generation ranking. Newsquawk suggested that heavy AI spending, rather than weak demand, is the main pressure on the company's current margins. The founder, Pony Ma, is taking the AI race seriously, as evidenced by the massive increase in capital expenditure. Tencent noted that marketing services revenue rose 19 percent to 43 billion yuan due to AI driven ad targeting.

Investors are now looking at what the company is spending to fix the revenue miss and the negative cash flow. Newsquawk flagged international games as a weak spot, as revenue stayed flat at 18.9 billion yuan during the quarter. Domestic games brought in 47.6 billion yuan, while value added services rose only 3 percent to 98.3 billion yuan. WeChat monthly active users reached 1.45 billion, which was ahead of the 1.43 billion forecast reported by Newsquawk. Fintech and business services, including cloud, grew 9 percent to 63.7 billion yuan, while cloud services grew 35 percent.

Tencent previously stated that a shortage of AI chips under US export curbs was holding back its cloud growth last year. In the second quarter, revenue rose 11 percent to 204.8 billion yuan, but net profit grew just 0.7 percent. Second quarter free cash flow was already negative at minus 13.8 billion yuan, as reported by The Next Web. Capital expenditure payments reached 65.1 billion yuan in the third quarter, up from 52.8 billion in the previous quarter. Tencent recently leased 100,000 Nvidia class chips from Oracle for roughly 7 billion dollars over a five year period.

Tencent is moving to raise 5 billion dollars in bonds, following a 4.66 billion dollar raise in June of 2026. Investors will likely ask Alibaba and Baidu how much of their AI spending turns into cloud revenue and when. The market is waiting for a date from Tencent regarding when the current heavy spending will finally begin to ease. It remains open whether AI spending in China's tech sector is paying off yet for companies like Tencent and Alibaba. Future earnings calls will be judged on free cash flow first and product launches second until AI revenue grows faster.

stories.Headline: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw says AI can cut drug development from five to seven years to one or two
stories.Summary:
Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw, Executive Chairperson of Biocon Ltd, said on Tuesday that Artificial Intelligence has the potential to drastically cut the time required to take a drug molecule from the lab to patients, compressing the current five-to-seven-year timeline into just one or two years. She spoke on the role of AI in life sciences on the first day of the Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026. She noted that accelerating this journey from lab to clinic will unlock major opportunities in precision and personalised medicine. She said the process of drug development does not end in the labs and has to be validated in clinical trials. She asked how to pick the right patients and conduct trials in a way that gives early readouts.

She said AI is going to be used for these purposes in the future. She said it currently takes almost five to seven years to get a molecule from the lab all the way to the patients, and asked whether that can be compressed into a year or two. She called that the most fascinating outcome and impact. She said it is not about making incremental change but about reimagining how to do discovery, development and drug innovation. She said that is the real opportunity AI gives and it should not be lost.

Shaw emphasised that scientific models must ultimately be validated in clinical trials, including picking the right patients and generating early readouts. She said autonomous wet labs are already conducting high-throughput screening and real-time analytics using AI. She said science and biology are currently done one target at a time, which is not going to move the needle. She said that when you understand where that target functions and how it functions using AI, you will be able to develop next generation drugs, next generation diagnostics and next generation technologies. She stressed that regulations must keep pace with accelerated discovery and development.

She highlighted that Karnataka can take a lead in this space. She noted that discussions are underway on how to create a regulatory sandbox to validate proof of concepts much faster. She described biology as the most important frontier for AI to be deployed. She said AI will help simplify complex biological systems and allow scientists to connect the dots rather than studying one target at a time. According to Shaw, converging genomics, chemical pathways and neural networks through AI will enable next-generation drugs, next-generation diagnostics such as detecting the first cancer cell to overcome late-stage diagnosis, as well as advancements in agriculture and bioenergy.

On a broader note, she said AI is about accelerating intelligence and is the greatest assistant that has become embedded in daily life and business. She said it helps people prioritise tasks, improve efficiency and get back time. Global leaders, innovators, founders, entrepreneurs, investors and thinkers from different industries are participating in the three-day Bengaluru Tech Summit, which started on Tuesday. The summit began on the first day of the week, when Shaw spoke. The articles were published on November 17, 2026, by PTI and carried by moneycontrol.com and rediff.com.

The articles do not state what specific regulatory changes, if any, have been proposed or approved. They do not name the participants of the Bengaluru Tech Summit or give the venue beyond the city. They do not say when the regulatory sandbox discussions began or who is involved in them. They do not give any timeline for when AI-enabled drug development might reach one or two years. They leave open whether the one-to-two-year compression has been demonstrated or remains a goal.
