stories.Headline: Malaysia regulator seeks details from Anthropic on alleged AI influence operation
stories.Summary:
Malaysia's communications regulator is seeking more information from the artificial intelligence company Anthropic about an alleged foreign-linked operation that used AI to manipulate political influence among users in Malaysia, the Communications Ministry told Parliament in a written reply dated Nov 17. According to the ministry, Anthropic alleged that its Claude AI technology was used by an overseas entity to build several parts of the operation, including targeting systems, fake social media accounts and fabricated news websites. Anthropic also linked the operation to BBS Bilisim Teknolojileri, a technology company based in Istanbul, Türkiye, the ministry said. The ministry said Anthropic reported that the Claude accounts it identified had been terminated and that mitigation measures had been put in place.

The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission will decide on appropriate follow-up action based on the information and evidence it obtains, within its jurisdiction and under the relevant legal provisions, the ministry said. That action could include cooperation with enforcement and security agencies, digital platform providers and other relevant parties where necessary, according to the ministry. Any regulatory or enforcement action would be carried out under the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998, the Online Safety Act 2025 and other applicable laws, it said. The ministry also said the Digital Ministry is drafting an Artificial Intelligence Governance Bill to strengthen the country's AI governance framework, covering accountability, risk management and the responsibilities of parties that develop and deploy AI systems.

The ministry was answering a question from Datuk Seri Dr Ronald Kiandee of PN-Beluran, who asked whether MCMC investigations had identified those responsible for the alleged operation and what action had been taken against the network of fake accounts and fabricated news portals involved. In its reply, the ministry said MCMC is seeking further information and clarification from Anthropic about the report so that any assessment and follow-up action rest on sufficient information and evidence. The government said it would keep strengthening monitoring of potential AI misuse and work with technology providers, digital platforms and relevant agencies to address online harm and ensure a safe, transparent and trusted digital environment. The articles do not say what happens next beyond MCMC's request for details and the drafting of the AI Governance Bill.

stories.Headline: Chinese AI firms shift to domestic chips as Nvidia halts H200 shipments to China
stories.Summary:
Nvidia founder Jensen Huang resigned from his role as chief executive officer on November 12, causing shock waves through global AI supply chains. The company has since stopped shipping licensed Hopper data center products, including H200 chips, to customers located within the country of China. Interim CEO Colette Kress disclosed this shipping halt during an earnings call held on Tuesday of the current US time. The board of directors has unanimously accepted the resignation and does not intend to reinstate Huang as the company leader. Huang stated on his X account on Tuesday that he would return to the company if he were invited back.

The US Commerce Department released a rule requiring licenses for advanced semiconductors sold to Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand. This new regulation also requires licenses when overseas data centers provide substantial remote computing capacity to companies based in restricted jurisdictions like China. Nvidia created a standing committee on national security and export controls to oversee compliance and report directly to the board. The company reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of 115.8 billion dollars, with data center revenue reaching 107.6 billion dollars during that period. Nvidia forecast fourth-quarter revenue of 130 billion dollars, assuming no data center computing revenue would be generated from the Chinese market.

Nvidia Chair Harvey Jones stated that the board will not restore Huang, who linked demand-side financing to supply-side execution for the firm. Roger Sheng of Gartner said the leadership vacuum has immediate ramifications for Chinese companies embedded in the world's most valuable chip company. A spokesperson for China's Ministry of Commerce said the US is overstretching national security and meddling in normal trade cooperation. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun stated that China has repeatedly made its principled position clear regarding US chip exports to China. The Chinese Commerce Ministry expressed firm opposition, stating the US approach undermines market rules and the international economic trade order.

Analyst Chen Haijin said reliance on a single foreign hardware vendor carries unacceptable geopolitical and operational risks for Chinese AI enterprises. Domestic buyers are now diversifying procurement portfolios by testing homegrown AI accelerators from Moore Threads, Cambricon, and the Huawei Ascend line. Analyst Chen Jing noted that domestic chips can already handle many inference tasks, which limits the impact of the H200 halt. Ma Jihua said the gap between Chinese alternatives and the H200 is narrowing, though some firms must rethink their models. Zhang Xiaorong warned that self-imposed restrictions could cause Nvidia to lose its competitive edge despite appearing to be a safer company.

Nvidia's share of the Chinese data center AI chip market fell to 34 percent in the first half of 2026 from near-monopoly. Huawei's market share rose to 28 percent, and nine of eleven domestic chip makers posted year-on-year growth in their total shipments. In June, China Mobile Hubei and Huawei tested an AI inference system using Ascend hardware on a live telecom network. Huawei announced in September that its Ascend software platform, known as CANN, had moved to community-driven open-source development for users. The US government claims a loophole allowed Chinese firms to bypass restrictions on advanced AI chips through various third countries.

Chinese cloud service companies are expected to increase procurement of domestic AI chips to grab larger shares of the local market. Experts warned that the software ecosystem remains the biggest bottleneck because Nvidia's CUDA platform has a dominant moat among developers. The current leadership disruption offers a window for the domestic software ecosystem to mature as users adapt to non-CUDA architectures. Future orders will depend on whether customers earn returns from AI applications once their data center facilities are fully running. The articles leave open whether Nvidia can sustain growth if spending slows or if US export restrictions are eventually eased.

stories.Headline: Marvell moves the HBM memory controller to a custom base die to free XPU compute area and cut interface power
stories.Summary:
Marvell has described a custom high-bandwidth memory layout that moves the memory controller off an accelerator's compute die and into a custom base die beneath each DRAM stack, as reported by NeoTeo on November 18, 2026. In the standard arrangement Marvell describes, the memory controller and the HBM interface sit on the XPU compute die, which is the accelerator's compute chip. In Marvell's custom layout, each DRAM stack sits above a base die that contains the controller, and a narrower die-to-die physical interface connects that base die to the XPU. The change shifts memory-control logic away from the XPU's edge and its compute area, and Marvell presents the design as a way to free compute area and lower interface power.

Marvell estimates that, compared with standard HBM, the architecture could provide up to 25% more compute area, room for up to 33% more HBM stacks and up to 70% lower memory-interface power, depending on the XPU design. The company says those figures describe potential design gains rather than a guaranteed increase in AI workload speed, because more compute area helps most when computation is the constraint. Marvell also describes adaptive power management for the die-to-die interface, which it says can reduce interface power by up to 75% under normal workloads and up to 42% at peak traffic compared with an interface without that feature. Those are separate comparisons from the broader estimate of up to 70% lower memory-interface power versus standard HBM.

Marvell identifies the die-to-die physical interface in the base die as the hottest spot and argues that the stack, base die, package and cooling need to be designed together. The company cites a Samsung thermal study of a 2.5D package in which internal thermal resistance accounted for 57% of the HBM stack's total and 13% of the adjacent ASIC's total, with those percentages referring to each component's total rather than to its temperature. For next-generation HBM running above 28 Gbps, Marvell expects heat flux to exceed 2.0 W/mm², and it discusses silicon heat paths near the interface, copper-to-copper hybrid bonding and coolant channels etched into silicon. Marvell relays a projection that internal temperatures in 16-high HBM stacks will exceed the thermal budget by 2028.

IBM Technology's Kaoutar El Maghraoui explains the memory wall, arithmetic intensity and the roofline model as general ways to understand why some workloads are limited by memory bandwidth rather than computing capacity. Arithmetic intensity measures floating-point operations per byte of memory accessed, and the roofline model uses it to distinguish work constrained by memory bandwidth from work constrained by compute. When data movement is the bottleneck, adding compute alone may not speed up the task, so the practical value of Marvell's potential bandwidth and power gains depends partly on what limits a given workload. The articles do not say when the custom HBM layout will reach products or which customers will adopt it.

stories.Headline: Suno launches Visuals tool to turn AI songs into short video clips
stories.Summary:
Suno launched a new tool called Visuals on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, to create short video clips. This product allows users to turn AI songs from their libraries into lyric videos, album art, and clips. The company moved from making songs to creating the visual content that users post alongside their music. These new video clips can be up to 15 seconds long and are available on the web. Mobile versions for iOS and Android are promised to arrive within the next few weeks.

The tool uses H3 Move, a model derived from MiniMax's H3, and requires a separate credit system. A new Platinum plan costs $120 a month, which is four times the price of the Premier plan. Free users are limited to one five second video before they must pay for more credits. The system is designed to follow song structure, lyrics, and beats rather than treating video as separate. This technology comes from MiniMax, which Disney, Universal, and Warner Bros.

Discovery sued in California in 2025. Chief product officer Jack Brody said Suno is a creative entertainment company that now goes beyond music. He stated that everyone is creative and the right tools help people bring their original ideas to life. Brody noted that video generation was previously too slow and expensive for anyone but large enterprises to use. He believes a new generation of models now opens video generation up to creative entertainment for everyone.

The company says the model is optimized for how the Suno community will use the product. Universal Music Group and Sony Music are still suing Suno, alongside the Elvis Presley estate and Jason Isbell. Eminem's publisher has also filed a lawsuit, while a class action group alleges violations of voice and likeness. The Elvis Presley estate claims Suno's assertions about not mimicking real voices are unequivocally false in court.

Independent artists are affected by the high cost of the Platinum plan and the separate credit pool. These creators must pay for experiments since many generated clips will not be keepers. Suno launched Speech last month for poems and meditations, and it launched Hooks in 2025 for user videos. The company was valued at $5.4 billion in June and signed licensed deals with Warner and BMG in September.

A Munich court ruled on July 31, 2026, that Suno broke copyright law by training on GEMA songs. Sony and Universal filed another lawsuit on September 18, 2026, naming 60,202 recordings in the new v6 model. ByteDance added similar likeness guardrails to its Seedance tool in March 2026 to compete in the market. Suno will implement hidden watermarks on videos shared outside the app, though these are currently described as planned.

The company will use filters to block prompts for public figures, specific artists, and copyrighted characters or intellectual property. Users must confirm they hold the rights to any files they upload before the tool can be used. It remains an open question whether the $120 plan is worth the cost for the average user. The first month of Platinum signups will determine if the product's specific music alignment is a success.

stories.Headline: Google spends heavily on AI and rebuilds search as rivals challenge its dominance
stories.Summary:
In late October, Alphabet released its most recent earnings report, and the company's stock price plummeted more than 12% the next day, the biggest single-day percentage decline since Google went public in 2004. The Planet Money newsletter asked whether Google had been caught in the innovator's dilemma. Google became one of the most valuable companies in the world by revolutionizing how humanity finds information, and a new generation of AI rivals is now challenging its dominance and pushing Google to spend a fortune to secure its future. Former Google executive Marissa Mayer remembers when the company was a scrappy startup working out of a small office above a bike shop in Palo Alto, Calif. She joined Google in 1999, fresh out of nearby Stanford with a master's in computer science, and became its 20th employee.

When Mayer interviewed at Google there were just seven people there, and by the time she got hired, a month or two later, she became its 20th employee. That year, Google brought in just over $200,000 in annual revenue, and by 2022, the eve of the AI boom, the company, by then reorganized under a parent company called Alphabet, was generating more than $280 billion, a more than millionfold increase. Google made its fortune selling ads next to its search results, monopolized internet searches so thoroughly that its name became a verb, and its search business became like an unstoppable money machine. In 2012, Mayer left and became the CEO of Yahoo, trying to revive a competitor that Google had blown out of the water, but neither Yahoo nor any other rival managed to dethrone King Google. Its share of the U.S. search-engine market grew from 80% in 2009 to nearly 90% in 2020.

Google plowed the profits from its search business into research and development of AI, and in 2017 a team of eight Google employees developed the transformer, a breakthrough technology that made today's AI chatbots possible. Mayer, now CEO of the AI startup Dazzle and a Google shareholder, sees Google's pioneering AI work as a reason for optimism, saying this is not a technology that's happening to Google and that they helped invent this new technology. Today Google is spending enormous amounts to build its AI capabilities and fend off rivals, and it is overhauling its search business, using AI to answer questions directly instead of just providing links. The late Harvard Business School professor Clayton Christensen developed the innovator's dilemma theory in his 1997 book, The Innovator's Dilemma: When New Technologies Cause Great Firms to Fail. Christensen theorized that the very thing that makes a business wildly successful can lead to its downfall in the face of a disruptive technology, and he helped put disruption in Silicon Valley's vocabulary long before it became a cliché.

Google's researchers made computers translate languages, recognize speech and images, drive cars autonomously, and even beat one of the world's best players at the game Go, and the company developed an internal chatbot called Meena that employees played with years before AI chatbots became a sensation, but they didn't release it. On Nov. 30, 2022, OpenAI released ChatGPT and offered a completely new way to find information and a glimpse of a future where people didn't need to go to Google to find answers anymore, and Google scrambled to respond, reportedly declaring a "code red" as ChatGPT captivated the masses. Last year, Google's chief scientist, Jeff Dean, told podcaster Dwarkesh Patel that they looked at their existing chatbots through the lens of their search business, saying that from a search perspective you want to get the right answer 100% of the time and that these models were not near that bar. Dean acknowledged that Google had underestimated how useful chatbots could be for things people wouldn't necessarily turn to a search engine for, like drafting a note or summarizing text. Mayer questions whether releasing a chatbot first would have gone as well for Google as it did for OpenAI, saying the standards for an established company like Google in terms of what users expect, in terms of quality, how good the search is, how great the product is, are fundamentally different than for an upstart or a newcomer.

Benedict Evans, a widely read technology analyst previously a partner at the Silicon Valley venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, says that every 10 or 15 years or so a revolutionary platform shift shakes up the tech industry, giving newcomers a chance to challenge dominant companies, and that it happened with personal computers, then the internet, then smartphones, and now with AI. Evans says the whole table gets reset and the things that meant that they had won and you couldn't take them on suddenly don't matter anymore. The process toward monopolization began with Google building a better search engine than rivals, and then, Evans says, its success became self-reinforcing: more users gave Google more data to improve its results, helping it attract still more users, which economists call a network effect. Google also paid to make its search engine the default in browsers and on devices, deals that a federal judge ruled in 2024 had illegally helped maintain its search monopoly. Google runs the operating system on many of our phones, we use free Google services to send emails, write documents, find directions, and watch a stranger explain how to fix our washing machine, and many of us keep going back to Google search out of sheer habit or because we keep getting nudged to go there.

Google has fought back with its own chatbot, now called Gemini, and by putting AI-generated answers directly onto its search page, even at the risk of undermining the advertising business that made it rich. The question now is whether all this will leave Google as dominant and as profitable in the AI age as it was in the age of old-school web search. Christensen warned in The Innovator's Dilemma that companies that keep disruptive technologies bottled up in their labs risk losing out to rivals willing to run with them, however imperfect they may be. The articles leave open what would have happened if Google had released a chatbot first, whether a Google chatbot would have taken off in the same way and given Google a first-mover advantage, or whether its flaws would have created big headaches for a company with an established reputation to protect. The articles also leave open whether rival AI systems will borrow from Google's playbook and work to intertwine themselves into our lives.

stories.Headline: Bank of Korea reports 66.5% of South Korean workers use generative AI but sees limited productivity gains
stories.Summary:
The Bank of Korea published a report on Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026, saying generative AI tools have spread rapidly among South Korean workers in recent years but have had a limited impact on improving productivity. The report said 66.5 percent of employees surveyed said they were using one of the available generative AI tools, including ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude, this year. That figure was up from 51.8 percent a year earlier, citing surveys of more than 16,000 people in 2025 and 2026. The BOK report showed that the 2026 figure of 66.5 percent was higher than the corresponding rates in the United States (43 percent) and Germany (31.5 percent), citing separate research. The report found limited productivity gains and improvements in work quality resulting from the time saved through AI use.

Their weekly AI usage rose to 8 hours from 5.9 hours over the one-year period, while 28.4 percent of AI users subscribed to paid AI services, spending an average of 49,000 won (US$37) per month this year. Respondents said AI tools helped them reduce the time spent on work tasks by 9.2 percent in 2026, compared with 3.8 percent in 2025, with stronger time-saving effects among higher-educated workers. A BOK survey of 16,342 workers found 66.5 percent of employed adults aged 18 to 64 used generative AI at least once for work this year, up from 51.8 percent last year, while the corresponding figures were 43 percent in the United States and an average of 33.7 percent in six European countries. The share of Korean workers who regularly use generative AI rose from 17.1 percent to 30.6 percent, and AI users in Korea saved an average of 9.2 percent of their working hours this year, up from 3.8 percent a year earlier. That amounts to 3.7 hours saved in a 40-hour workweek, compared with just 1.5 hours last year, and the central bank put the economic value of AI-related time savings at 61.1 trillion won.

The calculation applied the average time-saving rate of 4.8 percent across all workers, including those who do not use AI, to last year's total employee compensation of 1.27 quadrillion won. Assuming all the time saved was redirected toward productive work, the potential increase in economic output rose from 1 percent last year to 2.6 percent this year. Some 28.4 percent of those who rely on AI at work subscribed to paid services themselves and spent an average of 49,000 won per month, and Korean workers are estimated to spend a combined 2.8 trillion won a year out of their own pockets on AI services. Those who paid for their own subscriptions saved an average of 11.4 percent of their working hours, while employees whose companies covered the cost saved 11.6 percent, and both figures exceeded the 8.3 percent recorded among users who did not pay for AI themselves. Oh Sam-il, head of employment research at the BOK, said AI cannot reach its full potential unless companies also rethink how they reward employees and organize their workplaces.

The correlation between time saved and increased work output was just 0.08, while the figure for improvements in work quality stood at 0.09, and on a scale from zero to one, values closer to zero indicate a weaker relationship. Some 33.8 percent said they had devoted the extra time primarily to their core duties, while 29.3 percent said they had used it to handle additional assignments, and a mere 2.3 percent opted to leave the office early. The adoption rate stood at 86 percent for licensed professionals, 84 percent for managers and 81.3 percent for clerical workers, but workers were less likely to use AI as the proportion of core tasks in their jobs increased. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh said on Monday that productivity gains remained resilient but had yet to translate into a fundamental shift in the economy's productive capacity. The BOK said companies should redesign their working practices and organizational operations to embed AI in core functions and redirect the resulting time savings toward activities that create greater value.

The BOK report said the latest findings showed that although many respondents indicated that they used the saved time to focus on core tasks or handle additional work, no clear correlation was found between the rate of time savings and the rates of increase in work volume or quality improvement. The report said AI's much-anticipated productivity revolution remains in its early stages, and generative AI has become a workplace staple in Korea at a pace unmatched globally. The BOK said that rather than pursuing higher adoption rates or longer usage times as ends in themselves, businesses must assess whether AI delivers measurable improvements in job performance. The gap between actual usage and theoretical potential remained substantial, and for most workers, the hours saved through AI meant more time for work, not less. The report was published by the Bank of Korea, whose headquarters is in central Seoul.

The BOK said companies should redesign their working practices and organizational operations to embed AI in core functions and redirect the resulting time savings toward activities that create greater value. The report said businesses must assess whether AI delivers measurable improvements in job performance rather than pursuing higher adoption rates or longer usage times as ends in themselves. The articles leave open whether the correlation between time saved and work output or quality will strengthen, and they give no date for when AI might reach its full potential. The articles do not say how the surveys of more than 16,000 people in 2025 and 2026 were conducted beyond the BOK survey of 16,342 workers. The articles do not say what the six European countries with an average of 33.7 percent are, nor do they name the separate research behind the U.S. and German figures.

stories.Headline: ASEAN signs binding digital economy pact as MetaComp marks a year of its agentic payment network
stories.Summary:
On 14 November 2026 ASEAN member states signed the ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement, the bloc's first standalone, legally binding digital economy agreement, during the 49th ASEAN Summit. MetaComp Pte. Ltd., a Singapore-headquartered Web2.5 payments provider licensed by the Monetary Authority of Singapore as a Major Payment Institution, marked the first anniversary of its StableX Agentic Network at an industry forum in Singapore on 17 November 2026. The forum, titled "Agents Are Moving Money. Are You Ready?", drew close to 200 guests from banks, financial institutions and payment service providers. Mr Tan Kiat How, Senior Minister of State, Ministry of Digital Development and Information, was Guest of Honour. The forum was held on the eve of Singapore FinTech Festival 2026.

DEFA sets common rules for digital trade, cross-border data flows and electronic payments, and is expected to enter into force in early 2027. Google, Temasek and Bain & Company project that Southeast Asia's digital economy will reach US$368 billion in gross merchandise value this year, up 17%. ASEAN's merchandise trade reached US$2.1 trillion in the first half of 2025, up 16.4% year on year, according to the ASEAN Secretariat. The StableX Agentic Network grew in its first year to more than 1,000 members reaching over 100,000 users. Over local rails and SWIFT, institutions can pay out in local currency in six ASEAN markets: Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia, Vietnam, the Philippines and Thailand, and can collect local currency in Singapore, the Philippines and Indonesia, with Vietnam to follow.

Tin Pei Ling, Co-President of MetaComp, said ASEAN has set a clear ambition for integrated payments and that policy only becomes trade when payments can move between markets. She said MetaComp is building an interoperable agentic payment infrastructure for the region, now with more than 1,000 members on the StableX Agentic Network. She said that as more payments are initiated by AI agents, MetaComp takes AI governance and safety seriously, which is why the StableX KYA framework is a key feature of its infrastructure, so that every agent permitted into the network is verified, bounded and accountable. She said a payment network is only as useful as the trust behind it. Dr Bo Bai, Executive Chairman and Co-founder of Alpha Ladder Group, parent group of MetaComp, said Southeast Asia is where many of its clients' businesses are growing.

Dr Bo Bai said that when the StableX Network launched a year ago, the aim was payment infrastructure that institutions could rely on across markets, not only in Singapore. He said that with new investment behind the group, it can take the network into more of the region's markets and connect businesses from North Asia and beyond to them. Key thought leaders from banking, payments, digital assets and academia discussed what agentic payments must demonstrate to earn the trust of institutions and the businesses that depend on them, including Prof Hahn Jungpil, Provost's Chair Professor at the School of Computing at the National University of Singapore, and representatives from Tether and PwC. Businesses that pay across Southeast Asia still deal with different rails, currencies and rules in each market. The network's members include payment service providers whose clients are expanding into Southeast Asia, including exporters from North Asia.

The StableX Agentic Network is built to connect fiat and stablecoin rails in one place and routes each payment across available pathways by rate. If one corridor is slow or unavailable, a payment can take another. In April MetaComp announced it would adopt Solana as a preferred blockchain for settlement within the network, adding a route alongside fiat rails. The StableX Know Your Agent Framework acts as the network's gatekeeper, and every agent on the network must be verified, bounded and accountable. Each agent is registered to a verified owner, works only within the permissions it has been given, and can be traced back to whoever is responsible for it.

StableX KYA, launched in April 2026, decides which agents can join the network and be active on it, and what each one is authorised to do, and has since been productised and taken live. It oversees agents across their full lifecycle, and its monitoring framework sets out more than 30 measures across six governance objectives to track how agents behave over time, with results shown on a live dashboard. VisionX, MetaComp's compliance intelligence engine, screens transactions as they happen, across fiat and on-chain activity. At the forum VisionX AI, a standalone RegTech company within Alpha Ladder Group, unveiled AEGIS, its proprietary Large Graph Model for financial crime detection, and launched TraceX, a blockchain investigation platform. The StableX Agentic Network was named Outstanding Use of AI for Cross-Border Payments at The Digital Banker's Global AI Innovation Awards 2026, and VisionX won Best Compliance-First Innovation (Transaction Monitoring) at The Digital Banker's Digital Assets Awards 2026.

MetaComp was named to the CB Insights 2026 Fintech 100 and listed among Tech in Asia and Statista's Singapore's Top Fintech Companies 2027, and is a finalist in the Regulatory Leader category of the Singapore FinTech Festival FinTech Excellence Awards 2026. Visitors can see the StableX Agentic Network and VisionX at the Alpha Ladder booth, 6A13, Hall 6, Singapore EXPO, from 18 to 20 November. MetaComp connects fiat and stablecoin rails through a compliant Web2.5 architecture, enabling institutions and businesses to move, convert and manage capital across borders. Through its agentic financial solution, AI agents can access MetaComp's regulated payment capabilities directly, supported by StableX KYA for agent governance and VisionX for integrated fiat and on-chain compliance intelligence. The articles do not state the terms DEFA sets beyond digital trade, cross-border data flows and electronic payments, or which member states have ratified it.

stories.Headline: Ravi Menon says employers choose whether AI lifts or removes junior workers
stories.Summary:
Speakers at the Singapore FinTech Festival discussed the ongoing impact of artificial intelligence on jobs on Wednesday, November 18, 2026. These experts examined how automation and augmentation affect the workforce during a period of significant technological change. They focused on whether AI would lift or remove junior workers from their roles. The event featured panels on statecraft and the employment equation. These discussions highlighted the tension between productivity gains and job displacement.

The event included a panel titled Geoeconomics 2.0: Statecraft in the Age of Intelligence and another called The AI and Employment Equation. Ravi Menon, former managing director of the Monetary Authority of Singapore, spoke about the need for a social licence. Dr Michael Spence, a professor at Stanford University, discussed the current age of uncertainty. Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong, also the minister for energy, trade and industry, gave a keynote. These leaders addressed the specific challenges facing the small nation of Singapore.

Ravi Menon stated that AI needs a social licence based on the balance between wages and jobs. He argued that AI can either displace jobs through automation or raise productivity and wages through augmentation. Menon warned that failing to share gains could lead to a populist backlash similar to that of globalisation. He noted that the choice to lift or remove junior workers rests with the employers. He believes that entry level roles are where the pressure from AI shows first.

Dr Michael Spence said that displacement of young people is already appearing in the financial sector and professional services. He noted that investment banks must invent new models to bring in talent if AI does the beginner work. He cautioned that the period ahead looks disruptive and will change the scope of virtually every job. Many Singaporeans are anxious about these shifts, according to Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong. Gan stated that while some jobs will change, the government intends to protect every worker.

The articles explain that the AI landscape consists of frontier work, including infrastructure investment, and diffusion across the economy. Dr Spence noted that it is too soon to know the ultimate effects on productivity. Gan Kim Yong mentioned that the world is currently short of AI talent. He emphasized that trust between government and industry is key to building and testing AI applications. The background suggests that AI may change lifestyles and jobs faster than people can adjust.

Singapore will keep its doors open to welcome global talent to strengthen its position in the AI ecosystem. The government aims to give workers skills that allow them to take advantage of new opportunities. Gan Kim Yong believes that anxiety about the pace of change is healthy for the workforce. He warned that ignoring the impact of AI would lead to trouble for everyone. The articles leave open exactly how the new talent models for investment banks will be invented.

stories.Headline: South Korea deploys 75,000 proctors and bans smart devices as 551,864 students take college entrance exam
stories.Summary:
More than half a million students took the 2027 College Scholastic Ability Test across South Korea on Thursday, November 19, 2026. The national exam began at 8:40 a.m. and concluded at 5:45 p.m. at 1,312 different test centers. Authorities deployed 75,000 proctors and 8,400 additional staff members to prevent cheating during the event. A total of 551,864 people applied for this year's academic test to determine their university placements.

The government implemented strict security measures including checking all eyeglasses for hidden cameras and using stickers to cover clothing buttons. All electronic devices were banned from the rooms, and officials sent two loud disaster alert messages to find hidden mobile phones. Those caught cheating face a 10 year ban from the exam, while reporters of misconduct can receive 100 million won. To ensure silence during the English listening section, aircraft landings and takeoffs were suspended from 1:05 p.m. to 1:40 p.m. Additionally, Seoul increased subway services by 27 runs and delayed stock market hours by one hour to reduce traffic.

These heightened security protocols were triggered after the top scorer of a certified tax accountant exam admitted to using artificial intelligence and digital devices. Government officials stated that they are making all out efforts to crack down on cheating involving smart devices and AI. They believe these measures are necessary because the university a student attends can heavily influence their future career prospects. The administration aims to maintain the integrity of the test following the public outcry over recent academic scandals.

The College Scholastic Ability Test is considered a major life event and the culmination of years of grueling study for students. Because the stakes are so high, the government coordinates various national services to accommodate the needs of the test takers. Air traffic control required aircraft in flight to remain at an altitude of 3 kilometers or higher during the exam. These wide ranging efforts reflect the immense pressure placed on students during this single day of testing.

stories.Headline: Dubai crown prince approves City AI Agent initiative for government services
stories.Summary:
Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence of the UAE, approved the ‘City AI Agent’ initiative on Wednesday at the AI Retreat during the opening of Dubai Future Week 2026. The event, organised by the Dubai Future Foundation (DFF) at Emirates Towers and the Museum of the Future, runs until November 21 under the theme ‘For the Human of the Future’. The initiative will have AI agents understand people’s needs, execute tasks and coordinate procedures across Dubai government entities through a single, seamless experience. Drawing on advances in agentic AI, it marks a step towards an AI-native government that goes beyond improving services and speeding up procedures. It lays the foundations for a phase in which intelligent systems become integral to government operations, helping Dubai anticipate and respond to people’s needs.

Sheikh Hamdan also launched the Government Resources AI Agents ecosystem and NxtBI, an AI-powered decision-making platform, and reviewed Dubai Nexus, three systems that support the development of the City AI Agent. The Government Resources AI Agents ecosystem comprises 93 specialised agents covering human resources, finance and procurement within the shared Government Resource Planning (GRP) system. The agents are expected to execute more than 34 million tasks annually, save over 812,000 working hours and cut costs by more than Dh151 million across 85 government entities. Sheikh Hamdan attended the AI Grandmaster challenge, where 20 contestants from around the world compete for a Dh1 million prize through live, timed challenges using advanced AI tools. The 2025 edition drew more than 3,800 applications from 125 countries.

Sheikh Hamdan said that, guided by the vision of Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President and Prime Minister of the UAE and Ruler of Dubai, Dubai has established itself among the world’s leading cities in anticipating the future and harnessing technology to serve people. He said Dubai is entering a new phase with the ambition of building a world-leading government model in which AI becomes an integral part of how government operates and responds to people’s needs. He said the approval marks the transition from a government that harnesses AI to enhance its services to one that fundamentally redesigns the way it operates around AI capabilities. Hamad Obaid Al Mansoori, Director General of Digital Dubai, called the approval a strategic milestone and said AI will become an integral part of the government’s infrastructure and operating mechanisms. He said this will enable the government to understand people’s needs, address them comprehensively and proactively, and coordinate everything required across different entities and systems.

Sheikh Hamdan visited the Science, Technology, Arts and Research Summit (STARS), which features more than 20 panel discussions, 10 tech art installations and 30 interactive research posters. STARS hosts the Annual Meeting of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology’s (MIT) Senseable Open Lab for the first time in the region, where experts, academics and government officials will explore AI-powered smart cities, infrastructure, data systems and intelligent mobility. STARS is the first initiative in a year-round programme designed to strengthen Dubai’s Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) ecosystem. Sheikh Hamdan met alumni of The Knowledge Society (TKS) Dubai, a programme that prepares students aged 13 to 17 and has graduated 250 students from schools across Dubai and the UAE, 90 in its first cohort and 160 in its second.

They have joined a global network of more than 5,500 students and alumni across hundreds of cities. Sheikh Hamdan attended the graduation of the sixth cohort of the Dubai Future Experts Programme, jointly developed by DFF and The Executive Council of Dubai and delivered by Dubai Future Academy. The six-month programme brought together 48 mid- and senior-level officials from Dubai government entities to build foresight expertise and strengthen future readiness. He also attended the graduation of the third cohort of ‘FEEL: A Disruptive Futures Program’, the region’s first international programme of its kind, organised by Dubai Future Academy.

This year’s cohort comprised 18 participants from nine countries, selected from 265 applicants representing 49 countries. Sheikh Hamdan also launched the ‘Seed of Hope’ campaign to raise Dh325 million for the Cancer Patients Endowment. The ‘Seed of Hope’ campaign is organised by Dubai Health and led by Al Jalila Foundation, running until April 2027 to raise AED325 million for the Cancer Patients Endowment. Dr. Raja Easa Al Gurg, Member of the Board of Directors of Dubai Health and Chairperson of the Board of Directors of Al Jalila Foundation, said the campaign reflects a commitment to turning community giving into lasting support for patients through the Cancer Patients Endowment.

Dr. Amer Sharif, CEO of Dubai Health, said the campaign reflects Dubai’s vision of building a sustainable, people-first healthcare system and noted that giving is central to Dubai Health’s integrated academic health system. Sheikh Hamdan was accompanied on the tour by Mohammad Abdullah Al Gergawi, Minister of Cabinet Affairs, Vice Chairman of the Board of Trustees and Managing Director of DFF. He was also accompanied by Omar Sultan Al Olama, Minister of State for Artificial Intelligence, Digital Economy and Remote Work Applications, and Khalfan Belhoul, CEO of DFF. More to follow.

stories.Headline: KAYAK adds 28 AI travel features that pair chat planning with live prices
stories.Summary:
KAYAK introduced 28 new and enhanced AI-powered travel features on November 17, 2026, according to a November 17 update. The features include a search tool that helps travelers identify the cheapest dates to fly without choosing departure dates in advance. The update brings conversational trip planning together with live flight, hotel and rental car prices. Users can describe the vacation they want while comparing actual booking options alongside AI-generated recommendations. Travelers can ask when a particular trip will be cheapest and receive results based on live, bookable fares rather than relying solely on historical estimates.

The expanded Ask AI system allows travelers to describe a destination, budget or preferred type of holiday without first completing a conventional search form. Users can ask KAYAK to identify more affordable travel periods instead of selecting specific dates and repeatedly changing them to compare fares. The system combines conversational answers with search results that can be filtered and compared using the platform’s existing tools. KAYAK is also expanding AI-assisted itinerary creation, helping users organize activities and accommodation into travel plans while considering prices and options for selected destinations. Travelers can search for hotels with characteristics such as quiet rooms or rooftop swimming pools rather than relying entirely on predefined property filters.

Another addition allows users to identify flights offering Starlink satellite Wi-Fi, a feature that has become increasingly important as airlines compete to provide faster onboard internet connections. Some of the 28 announced features are enhancements to existing functionality rather than entirely new products, and availability may differ by market and rollout stage. Peer Bueller, CEO of KAYAK, said AI is great at suggesting where to go but can sound confident even when it is out of date. He said KAYAK’s AI is tied to live prices so travelers can verify what it suggests before they book. He said travelers should not have to jump between an AI conversation and multiple travel sites to check what is accurate.

KAYAK says users who engage with Ask AI are approximately 2.5 times as likely to make a booking as other visitors to its platform. The figure is company-reported and does not establish that AI itself causes higher booking rates. Since Ask AI launched earlier this year, 30% of sampled conversations included flexible or open-ended requests, such as finding the cheapest weekend to fly to Rome in January. KAYAK is the first travel tool to answer that kind of question with real-time prices and bookable results. The new features build on KAYAK’s earlier AI Mode launch rather than representing the company’s first entry into conversational travel search.

AI travel assistants have become increasingly common, but one of their persistent limitations has been the difference between an attractive suggested itinerary and the prices travelers actually find when attempting to book it. KAYAK’s latest development is intended to narrow that gap by placing real-time travel search results directly alongside conversational planning. The distinction is particularly relevant during periods of high demand, when airfare and hotel rates can change quickly and an itinerary assembled from estimated prices may no longer fit a traveler’s budget. KAYAK is part of Booking Holdings (NASDAQ: BKNG) and describes itself as a leading travel search engine with billions of queries across its platforms. The KAYAK app is available on iOS and Android, and KAYAK also supports business travelers with a corporate travel solution.

KAYAK uses the technology and data behind its Buy vs. Wait recommendations to find promising dates, then checks live prices so users can see what is available and what it actually costs. Users can build a personalized, day-by-day itinerary and refine it through conversation while live flight, hotel and rental car results and prices update alongside it. Users can set Price Alerts directly through Ask AI to track prices while plans take shape, and Ask AI is now available on iOS and Android. Ask AI helps users understand what is included in a fare and weigh details before booking, and a route’s on-time record feature is coming soon. Ask AI will remember preferences such as nonstop flights or morning departures to personalize future recommendations, a feature also listed as coming soon.

stories.Headline: APEC member nations reach consensus on safe and responsible AI deployment
stories.Summary:
Member nations of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation focused on the responsible application and safe deployment of artificial intelligence on Tuesday, November 17, 2026. Chen Xu, who served as the ambassador for China to the United Nations until last year, led these discussions as the chair of the APEC Senior Officials' Meeting. The participants engaged in detailed conversations regarding various digital technology issues to reach an important consensus on the future of AI. These meetings took place in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, during the broader APEC summit.

The discussions required member states to examine the role of data in driving the growth of artificial intelligence for the first time. This diplomatic effort occurs while the United States and China compete for global leadership in AI technology amidst increasingly strained ties. On Monday, November 16, the United States implemented tighter restrictions to stop Chinese firms from using overseas data centers to get advanced AI chips. Washington claims these measures are necessary to close a loophole that allows companies to bypass existing export controls.

Chen Xu explained during a press conference that the parties involved held in-depth discussions on a wide range of digital technology topics. He emphasized that the primary goal of these talks was to ensure that the deployment of AI remains safe and responsible across the region. The former envoy highlighted that the member nations successfully reached a significant agreement on these critical AI-related issues. He noted that the dialogue focused heavily on the intersection of data usage and technological advancement.

stories.Headline: Nigeria wins global privacy accountability award in Brussels after beating over 145 jurisdictions
stories.Summary:
Nigeria won the Excellence in Accountability Award at the 48th Annual Global Privacy Assembly held in Brussels, Belgium, on November 19, 2026. The Nigeria Data Protection Commission received this international honor for strengthening accountability in personal data processing and promoting regulatory transparency and governance. This achievement occurred after Nigeria beat out other jurisdictions from a total of more than 145 countries represented at the global forum. The award recognizes the country for its leadership commitment to privacy and its exemplary compliance frameworks and governance within the regulatory system. Nigeria also reached the finals in two other competitive categories, which were Innovation and Education and Public Awareness, during the assembly.

The regulatory framework requires a public-private partnership approach that has led to the licensing of 367 Data Protection Compliance Organisations across the country. This specific model aims to promote accountability among more than 500,000 data controllers and processors of major importance operating within Nigeria. The system is designed to extend the regulatory reach of the Commission and strengthen the monitoring of compliance for various institutions. These efforts follow the signing of the Nigeria Data Protection Act into law by President Bola Tinubu less than four years ago. The Global Privacy Assembly is a leading international forum that brings together privacy authorities from more than 145 jurisdictions worldwide.

Dr Vincent Olatunji, the National Commissioner and Chief Executive Officer of the NDPC, stated that accountability is fundamental to effective data protection. He explained that this principle is essential for building public confidence in the expanding digital economy and earning trust from citizens. Olatunji noted that the award reflects the commitment of the Federal Government to building a sustainable and trusted digital ecosystem. He believes that upholding these standards positions Nigeria as a destination of choice for investors seeking a secure digital environment. The commemorative citation praised the Commission for its leadership commitment to privacy and its transparency in managing personal data processing.

The award affects over 230 million data subjects in Nigeria who rely on the protection of their personal information from misuse. Financial institutions, technology firms, telecommunications companies, and public institutions are all affected as they handle increasing volumes of sensitive consumer data. Other foreign data protection authorities are now studying the Nigerian model to see if it can expand their own regulatory capacity. These authorities are interested in how private sector participation can be encouraged to improve the enforcement of data protection laws. The recognition comes as global concerns grow regarding identity theft, unauthorized access to information, and various large scale data breaches.

The articles state that the rapid adoption of artificial intelligence and digital financial services has increased concerns over the security of information. The 48th annual conference focused on emerging challenges like privacy enhancing technologies, digital governance, and the protection of data belonging to children. Nigeria's framework was developed to address the risks associated with the collection and processing of personal information by various entities. The broader discussions at the assembly aimed to strengthen cross border cooperation and develop common approaches to protecting personal information globally. This background highlights the critical need for effective enforcement of regulations to build confidence in the national digital economy.

The award is expected to boost the visibility of Nigeria within the field of international privacy governance and regulatory leadership. Future progress will be measured by sustained enforcement, public awareness, and the accountability of organisations that handle personal information. The articles leave open how the licensed compliance organisations will continue to monitor the thousands of data controllers in Nigeria. It remains unclear how the government will address the ongoing threats of identity theft and unauthorized access to sensitive consumer data. The text does not specify the exact timeline for implementing the innovative compliance mechanisms mentioned in the competition finals.

stories.Headline: Kansas State proposes a master's degree in AI systems as the board of regents weighs it
stories.Summary:
Kansas State University is proposing a new master's degree in artificial intelligence systems and their applications, which would be part of the Department of Computer Science in the College of Engineering. The Kansas Board of Regents is considering the proposal this week, according to reports from News Radio KMAN published on November 18, 2026. The proposal states that demand for AI-related jobs is growing rapidly and that the new degree would help students compete in a changing job market. A market analysis by Veritone, itself an AI company, showed an increase of 25.2% in AI jobs in the first quarter of 2025 compared to the first quarter of 2024. Another company reported that jobs such as AI engineer have shown growth of nearly 150%.

The proposal ties the degree to that job growth, saying the credential would help students compete in a changing market. The articles give no further details on curriculum, tuition, enrollment targets or a start date. The Board of Regents is the body considering the degree, and the proposal comes from the Department of Computer Science in the College of Engineering at K-State. The reporting is by Megan Moser, and the articles direct readers to the Mercury.com for the full article. No university officials are quoted in the articles, and no one is named beyond the author and the companies cited.

The context given is the rapid growth in AI-related jobs, supported by the Veritone analysis and the figure of nearly 150% growth for roles such as AI engineer. What happens next depends on the Kansas Board of Regents, which is considering the proposal this week. The articles do not say when the board will decide or when the degree could launch. stories.Headline: Calif researchers use GPT-6 Cyber to find a critical Java flaw and build a working exploit for under $200
stories.Summary:
Researchers at the cybersecurity startup Calif, with help from OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber model, discovered a memory corruption bug in Java that can be used to take over computer systems, according to Engadget. On some machines, feeding Java's base64 decoder a string of 64 "A" characters followed by an equals sign triggers a memory error that usually causes a crash but can be finessed to gain full unauthorized access. Calif showed the bug could be used to hack into Keycloak, a widely used login system protecting organizations like CERN and NASA. The Record reports that CISA issued a notice on Tuesday night about CVE-2026-114938, which researchers are calling "Java4Shell," warning that attackers could crash the critical Java Virtual Machine and conduct unauthenticated remote code execution. Oracle released a patch for the bug in its November Patch Tuesday release, writing that it carries a severity score of 8.1, and credited Quang Luong and Albert Yang of Calif with discovering the vulnerability.

Java is the world's third most popular programming language and powers about 90 percent of Fortune 500 companies, according to Calif, which said banking, aviation, telecommunications and nearly every critical sector runs on it, including national security systems. Calif said it took Luong an hour to discover the vulnerability and two more hours to develop the first working exploit, at a total token cost of less than $200. The company explained that there is no universal exploit and each system may require different steps to exploit, and Luong noted he found the bug while developing a 0-click exploit on a certain phone vendor. Calif said it is holding back on releasing application-specific exploits and weaponized chains for individual products until everyone has had a chance to upgrade. Several other companies confirmed Calif's findings and urged organizations to patch the bug immediately.

CISA urged organizations to review their software inventories for affected Java installations, including those bundled within third-party applications, and to prioritize internet-facing systems. Calif says the bug isn't easy to weaponize, which should give defenders some breathing room, but Engadget notes that some systems will inevitably go unpatched and Calif estimates the bug could linger for five to 10 years. Calif also discovered the highly publicized vulnerabilities impacting PHP last month and used AI to find this bug, as it did with PHP2Shell. Although officials' public statements haven't linked the past week's outages at Microsoft, the FAA, banks and Apple to AI, Engadget describes the events as a picture of aging digital infrastructure unprepared for what comes next.

stories.Headline: Florida House Speaker Sam Garrison warns lawmakers about AI risks and creates a technology oversight committee
stories.Summary:
The Florida Legislature officially began a new term Tuesday, with new legislative leaders pledging to work on affordability issues and guard against the unwieldy ramifications of the evolution of artificial intelligence. New House Speaker Sam Garrison, R-Fleming Island, encouraged the chamber to have a sense of urgency about the perils of the new technology. Garrison raised the prospect of AI that improves itself so quickly that humans will lose the ability to understand or control it. Garrison said this is not science fiction but a sober reality that many in the tech community predict will arrive as early this year or next. Garrison asked lawmakers to think about that and then ask themselves what they are doing and whether they are AI's tool or it is theirs.

Garrison set up a new panel, the Advanced Technology & Digital Security Committee, to look into AI and other new technologies to oversee state technology services. Garrison said the state faces an estimated $12 billion loss to local governments as the homestead exemption increases from $50,000 to $150,000 in 2027 and to $250,000 in 2028. Garrison said the measure will save money for homestead owners but presents the biggest fiscal challenge Florida has faced in a generation. Garrison cited his creation of the House Public Integrity Committee to investigate public corruption and hold public officials to account. The next regular session for the Legislature is set to begin March 2.

New Senate President Jim Boyd, R-Bradenton, cited cost-of-living issues as among his top priorities but gave few clues about what his policy prescriptions will be to address them. Boyd said it is imperative to tackle affordability and asked what good a beacon of opportunity is if you cannot build a good life here. Boyd said it is challenging to build a good life when folks are struggling to make ends meet. Boyd said that while we cannot change the national or global economy, we do have an important role to play in keeping Florida affordable. Boyd said families have made hard adjustments and they expect government to do the same.

House Democratic Leader Christine Hunschofsky of Parkland said Democrats are ready to listen, find common ground, build relationships and work with every member who shares a commitment to making Florida better. Hunschofsky, armed with a 50-member-strong Democratic caucus, the largest for the party in decades, warned her caucus will speak up if the Republican majority shuts them out of discussions affecting their districts. Rep. Gallop Franklin, D-Tallahassee, spoke out against proposed changes to the House rules, which include earlier deadlines to file bills and allow bills to be rewritten and passed on the same day. Franklin said constituents' needs do not follow the legislative calendar and that members of the public deserve to read bills before we vote. Franklin welcomed other changes, such as requiring lobbyists to disclose whether they also act as a political consultant or receive any other payment from a member's political committee.

Florida has been at the forefront of AI skepticism, led by Gov. Ron DeSantis, who urged lawmakers to pass an AI Bill of Rights to protect consumers. Garrison's predecessor as Speaker, Daniel Perez, preferred to let the federal government and President Donald Trump take the lead on regulating the new technology, so the measure didn't advance in the House this year. Boyd's remarks came in the wake of the midterm elections, in which Republicans narrowly held onto the governor's mansion, the Cabinet and a U.S. Senate seat, but Democrats flipped several seats while emphasizing the rising cost of living. Some Republicans have pointed to Amendment 3, the property tax cut measure approved by more than 60 percent of voters, as one way they're reducing costs for residents. The amendment faced fierce resistance from a wide range of organizations, including firefighters, police, health care workers, local government officials and some GOP leaders, who argued the property tax cut would be too drastic for rural counties to absorb without affecting essential services.

The new rules were passed on a voice vote, over the objections of Democrats shouting no. The articles do not say what the Advanced Technology & Digital Security Committee will do first or when it will meet. The articles do not say what specific affordability proposals Boyd will put forward. The articles do not say how Garrison's House Public Integrity Committee will be structured or staffed. The articles do not say whether the AI Bill of Rights will be revived in the new term.

stories.Headline: Microsoft claims MAI Code 2 matches 96% of Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost
stories.Summary:
Microsoft unveiled a new lineup of specialized AI models at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, making a direct run at Anthropic and OpenAI in coding, cybersecurity and image generation. The company pitched models trained to do particular jobs at substantially lower cost instead of one chatbot that beats everyone at everything. The biggest claim involves MAI Code 2, which Microsoft says delivers 96% of Claude Opus 5.5's performance on common enterprise coding tasks for just 5% of the cost. Microsoft also claims 98% of GPT-6.1 Sol's performance at 40% of the price. OpenAI also released GPT-6.2 on Tuesday, so Microsoft's Sol comparison already concerns an older generation.

Those figures average results from four evaluations focused on practical software development, including fixing code and completing multi-file changes. Microsoft ran three of the tests on its own evaluation platform, used outside results for the fourth, and calculated MAI Code 2's costs using a 50% promotional discount. A lighter Code 2 Flash model targets routine fixes and quick edits, with Microsoft claiming performance comparable to Claude Haiku 5.5 at 20% of the price. Microsoft says MAI Cyber 2 Flash succeeded on 92.3% of CyberGym-E2E's evaluated vulnerability-discovery tasks, compared with 91.5% for GPT-6 Astra, at less than 2% of the cost per task. Microsoft excluded 92 of 905 tasks after identifying overlap between their source material and its training data.

Microsoft has not yet published a direct comparison against OpenAI's restricted GPT-6 Cyber model. Its security system will begin replacing an older MAI model for eligible MDASH customers in mid-December, building on the vulnerability-scanning approach Decrypt previously covered. Microsoft's own documentation says Code 2 is not yet optimized for fundamental scientific research or very long-running autonomous assignments. Microsoft quotes about $35 per 1,000 images for MAI Image 2.7 and $10 for its Flash version, versus roughly $211 for GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst at maximum quality in Artificial Analysis's comparison. Microsoft is also offering selected business customers the ability to customize and run its models' licensed weights inside Azure, reducing reliance on outside vendors without making the technology open source.

On Artificial Analysis's image-editing test, which asks people to choose between anonymously generated edits and turns those preferences into an Elo rating, MAI Image 2.7 currently leads with 1,215 points against GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst's 1,211. The four-point gap is small enough that their reported uncertainty ranges overlap, and the separate text-to-image generation ranking puts Microsoft in fourth place. Google's Nano Banana 2.1 is about $34 per 1,000 images there, while Nano Banana Pro is about $134, and actual bills depend on the provider, resolution and settings. Both coding models are already in GitHub Copilot, putting Microsoft's in-house technology directly into a product that has relied heavily on outside AI suppliers. Microsoft also announced MAI Work Flash, which it describes as having been derived from Code 2 Flash and which can help generate formulas in Excel, work with documents and instructions in Word, and track decisions and extract useful information from Teams.

Microsoft famously has a multi-billion-dollar investment in OpenAI dating back to 2023 and has built many of its products and services around OpenAI intellectual property. Anthropic competes in the cheaper end of the market with Haiku, not just its premium Opus models, so Microsoft is entering a race its rivals already understand. OpenAI has taken a related approach with its Mini and Nano models, letting cheaper workers handle routine tasks while larger systems tackle the exceptions. Our earlier testing of MAI Image 2 found excellent realism but frustrating limits on editing and output formats, and the newer release adds interactive editing through Microsoft's Canvas workspace, transparent backgrounds and broader access through Foundry. Microsoft says the numbers it is reporting use a 50% introductory discount, and the benchmarks are all Microsoft-provided.

For the next test of its specialist strategy, Code 2 is already available in GitHub Copilot, and the Cyber 2 Flash rollout is scheduled to start in mid-December. Microsoft is touting that it is integrating these new models as optional choices for GitHub Copilot, Microsoft 365 and Fabric. The company has not yet published a direct comparison against OpenAI's restricted GPT-6 Cyber model. Performance numbers may well differ once the models undergo independent performance tests, and benchmark selection could be cherry-picking. The company also described clearly that these new models are not designed to handle the most challenging agentic and research workloads.

stories.Headline: KAIST professor Jaeseung Jeong unveils his own AI-era assessment system on tvN show
stories.Summary:
The 369th episode of tvN’s You Quiz on the Block, airing on the 18th, features Remco Breuker, a Dutch scholar of Korean studies who completed an English translation of the Samguk Yusa, Professor Jaeseung Jeong, a neuroscientist who looks to the future of AI, and actor Kim Myung-min. The episode arrives as cases of cheating using artificial intelligence come to light, raising concerns about its misuse in the 2027 College Scholastic Ability Test, which is just a day away. Professor Jaeseung Jeong, a professor in KAIST’s Department of Brain and Cognitive Sciences, will share his views on assessment methods in the age of AI and the future of technology. Making his first appearance on You Quiz, Professor Jeong will have a warm meeting with Yoo Jae-suk, who reacts as though he looks familiar, asking whether he has been on before. It will turn out that Professor Jeong has made more indirect appearances on You Quiz than anyone else, adding to the interest.

On the show, Professor Jeong will share his experience of feeling a chill while talking with AI, as well as a scientist’s insights into the age of AI. As reports of exam cheating using high-tech devices such as AI glasses raise concerns about the misuse of AI, attention is turning to Professor Jeong’s views on the issue ahead of the CSAT. He is expected to unveil a novel assessment system for the AI era that he developed himself at KAIST and discuss the potential of new approaches to assessment. Viewers will also hear the life story of Professor Jeong, who once dreamed of becoming an astrophysicist before pursuing neuroscience. From how he asked Dr. Stephen Hawking a question in person at Hawking’s first lecture in Korea when Jeong was in high school to what sparked his interest in neuroscience, the program will look at the scientific life of a pioneer who has had a major influence on popularizing science.

Viewers will also hear the fascinating idea that the brains of people in love are on a different level, as well as a neuroscientist’s perspective on love. The story behind the creation of the emotion-tracking watch featured in Park Hae-young’s drama We Are All Trying Here will also be revealed for the first time on You Quiz. Marking the 10th anniversary of the historic match between AlphaGo and Lee Sedol, the program will also revisit behind-the-scenes stories from the match, which Professor Jeong watched as a commentator, and explore the future AI will transform. Viewers can hear the stories of Professor Jeong, who even captivated Yoo Jae-suk, on the show. Professor Jeong became a familiar face to the public through tvN’s variety show Encyclopedia of Useless Facts, and through books including Science Concert and Twelve Footsteps he has steadily engaged with the public, offering lively explanations of neuroscience, human behavior and social phenomena.

The top scorer on South Korea’s tax accountant certification exam, who admitted Sunday to using AI to cheat, reportedly turned over a miniature camera, a laptop and a phone to police, and no smart glasses were among the devices submitted. He first drew attention after boasting that he had scored 397.5 out of 400 on the first stage of the exam, well above the average. Affiliates of Samsung, SK, Hyundai Motor and LG, along with shipbuilders and defense contractors, said that as of Tuesday they restrict smart glasses or require prior approval to bring them onto their premises. Companies are stepping up employee training and asking workers to report unauthorized devices, and some facilities are adding visual inspections to existing entry checks. Smart glasses can conceal cameras, microphones and wireless transmitters in ordinary-looking frames, and the security risk extends to everyday objects such as shirt buttons and pens, which can also house miniature cameras.

The stakes are particularly high at semiconductor and defense facilities that handle technologies protected under South Korea’s industrial and defense security rules, because the same kind of device that can capture an exam question could also record a chipmaking process, a vehicle prototype or a confidential document. An industry official said companies were already struggling with AI-related hacking threats, that tiny wearables like smart glasses add to their security worries, that a leak can change a company’s fortunes, and that businesses need targeted government support and clearer rules. Samsung Electronics generally prohibits on-site photography with smart devices and requires camera-blocking stickers on smart glasses brought onto its premises. SK hynix bars smart glasses and reminded employees Monday to leave them in lockers before entering company buildings and to report anyone using similar devices inside. South Korea protects key semiconductor manufacturing processes under laws governing national core technologies and national advanced strategic technologies.

The National Police Agency’s National Office of Investigation recorded 179 technology leak cases last year and apprehended 378 people, with semiconductors accounting for five overseas leak cases, the most of any sector. Hyundai Motor has required visitors to its Seoul headquarters to declare smart glasses and other AI wearables and get approval before bringing them in since June, and has reportedly extended the policy to its domestic research centers and factories. It has added AI-based battery detection to its X-ray equipment and uses visual checks to spot wearables. LG Group bars unauthorized smart devices and requires cameras to be covered on smart glasses that cannot run its security software, while HD Hyundai has restricted some smart devices at major sites and updated its confidentiality agreements and employee training. Hanwha Aerospace has added visual inspections to existing security checks and metal detection at research facilities that handle sensitive technology.

As scrutiny grows, smart glasses makers are highlighting safeguards: Samsung Electronics said its upcoming glasses will feature an external LED that lights up when in photo or video mode and the camera will be disabled if the light is blocked or malfunctions, and Meta said its models sold in South Korea rely on spoken commands and audible replies, making them unlikely to be used for cheating. President Lee Jae Myung on Tuesday ordered additional measures to curb AI-assisted cheating during Thursday’s college entrance exam, a proposed reward of at least 100 million won, or $75,000, for tips. stories.Headline: Pinewood.AI adds ChatGPT as an advertising channel to its Boost marketing tool for automotive retailers
stories.Summary:
Pinewood.AI expanded its Boost performance marketing tool by adding ChatGPT as a new advertising channel on November 18, 2026. This update allows automotive retailers and dealer groups to reach potential car buyers through AI powered conversations. The company announced this development from Fort Lauderdale, Florida, to help dealers engage with active vehicle researchers. Pinewood.AI provides cloud based technology services to automotive retailers and original equipment manufacturers across the globe. The Boost tool was originally developed by Seez, an automotive AI company that Pinewood.AI acquired in 2025.

The Boost tool now manages ChatGPT ads alongside existing paid media channels including Meta, Google, TikTok, and Snapchat. Dealers can currently run the Sponsored Card format, which presents an advertisement alongside a response generated by ChatGPT. OpenAI has also selected Aleph as the exclusive reseller for ChatGPT Ads in 44 different countries. These markets include 14 in Latin America, 16 in Europe and Central Asia, and 10 in Middle East and Africa. Aleph provides local invoicing and support in countries like Argentina, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and the United Arab Emirates.

Jad Naamani, the Director of Marketing at Seez, stated that adding ChatGPT is an important development for their dealers. He explained that car buyers increasingly use AI conversations to research vehicles, compare different models, and understand their options. Naamani noted that dealers must be present when buyers ask AI assistants or they will not make the shortlist. He said that integrating ChatGPT into Boost provides dealers with one strategy and one view of reporting for activity. The tool uses the retailer's own data to connect advertising spend to actual dealership outcomes like leads and sales.

Over one hundred thousand marketers have already advertised on ChatGPT, which now has more than one billion weekly users. Research from Invoca found that 60 percent of UK car buyers used generative AI tools for research in 2026. This figure is an increase from 47 percent the previous year, showing explosive growth in using AI assistants for purchases. Automotive retailers are affected because ChatGPT Ads are contextual, appearing in relevant conversations rather than relying on behavioral signals. These ads target users who are exploring options, comparing models, or asking for specific recommendations for their next vehicle.

Pinewood Technologies Group Ltd was established in 1981 and serves a global user base spanning over 36 different countries. The company has long standing partnerships with over 50 OEM brands and maintains headquarters in North America and the UK. Seez was founded in 2016, is headquartered in Dubai with an office in Copenhagen, and operates in 25 countries. In October 2026, Ridgeview Partners completed an acquisition of Pinewood Technologies Group PLC, which took the company private. Seez offers various SaaS products, including AI powered chat solutions, predictive pricing models, and omnichannel retail platforms.

Pinewood.AI and Seez will continue to evolve Boost capabilities as OpenAI makes new advertising formats and opportunities available. OpenAI plans to develop further optimization tools, measurement solutions, and new formats while broadening access to its AI. Aleph will continue offering local contracting and training for brands and agencies in the 44 designated reseller markets.
