stories.Headline: House lawmakers introduce bipartisan bill to create federal cyber and AI review board
stories.Summary:
House lawmakers introduced a bipartisan bill on Wednesday to create a federal board. This board would investigate major cyberattacks, artificial intelligence incidents, and technology failures. Rep. Morgan Luttrell of Texas introduced the ROOT CAUSE Act with Rep. Ritchie Torres. The proposal follows outages that disrupted air travel, workplace software, and National Security Agency operations. These disruptive events occurred over the last week before the bill was introduced.

The ROOT CAUSE Act creates a National Cyber and AI Investigations Board in CISA. This board would examine serious disruptions from faulty updates, configuration errors, or AI failures. The AI INSIGHT Act by Rep. Matt Van Epps addresses AI agents on civilian networks. Rep. Andy Ogles of Tennessee introduced the SECURE IT Act on Wednesday for IT security. These measures exclude national security systems, defense systems, and intelligence community systems from their authority.

Rep. Luttrell stated that action is critical because adversaries are becoming increasingly sophisticated in this space. Rep. Van Epps said every agent on a federal network is a potential target for adversaries. Rep. Ogles noted that recent outages exposed American dependence on shared IT infrastructure. He stated that stronger coordination between government and industry is needed as cyber threats grow. The bills aim to prevent the executive branch from abolishing the board without Congressional acts.

Sens. Maria Cantwell and Mike Rounds urged Jay Clayton to coordinate a national response to AI threats. They wrote that the digital economy cannot rely on individual companies to solve these problems. The senators cited AI's role in uncovering flaws in PHP software used to run websites. They noted that banks cannot always distinguish authorized AI agents from rogue actors accessing customer accounts. The proposed SECURE IT Act would keep company participation in its coordination efforts entirely voluntary.

The board proposal comes nearly two years after the Trump administration emptied the Cyber Safety Review Board. That previous board had faulted Microsoft for security failures that allowed Chinese hackers to access emails. Recent disruptions include a Friday FAA ground stop that delayed more than 10,000 flights. A Microsoft outage disrupted workplace tools, and maintenance caused a Tuesday outage of the classified NSANet. The Trump administration emptied the previous board during an investigation of China's Salt Typhoon telecom intrusions.

Democrats will take control of Congress in January with Rep. Bennie Thompson chairing the homeland panel. CISA would establish supporting capabilities for AI agent tracking within one year of the act's enactment. The legislation would prevent outside officials from altering or suppressing the findings of the new board. The articles leave open whether the proposed bills will pass under the new Congressional leadership. They do not state if the current administration supports these three specific legislative proposals.

Articles.Title: Bipartisan bill would create cyber and AI review board amid series of tech outages

stories.headline_source: Bipartisan bill would create cyber and AI review board amid series of tech outages

stories.Headline: AAIB probe report into AI 171 crash at ‘fag end’, Centre tells Supreme Court
stories.Summary:
The Centre told the Supreme Court on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, that the final Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau report on the Air India Flight 171 crash is at the fag end, and it asked for two or three weeks more for publication. The crash at Ahmedabad Airport killed 12 crew members and 229 passengers on June 12, 2025. On July 28, the court was told the report would be published anytime between the middle of September, with a buffer till the end of October. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Union government and the Directorate General of Civil Aviation, said the report was nearly complete.

Advocates Prashant Bhushan and Pranav Sachdeva, appearing for petitioner NGO Safety Matters Foundation, said the authorities have repeatedly sought adjournments in the case. Mehta denied any attempt to deliberately delay the report. In July, the apex court put on hold the petitioners' plea for a Court of Inquiry or a fair, transparent and technically sound investigation, in order to wait for the report. One petitioner is 91-year-old Pushkar Raj Sabharwal, father of Commander Sumeet Sabharwal, one of the pilots on the ill-fated aircraft. The court had clarified that the trajectory of the litigation would depend on whether the AAIB report would be well-merited and accepted.

The petitions, including one by a pilots' body, argued that an investigation of such magnitude ought to have gone to an independent agency under international protocols to which India is a signatory. The court opted to wait for the report, reasoning that the AAIB probe had substantially progressed. On Wednesday, Bhushan submitted that the probe had been on for a year and a half, and he had earlier alleged a conflict of interest, saying three of the five members of the investigation team were from the DGCA. He said AAIB rules mandated a permanent body without DGCA members.

Mehta had earlier explained that experts from the countries to which some of the passengers belonged were involved in the investigation. He said the investigation took time because each component of the aircraft had to be sent to the manufacturers, wherever they were located, for checking. The court is awaiting the report before deciding how the petitions proceed.

Articles.Title: AAIB probe report into AI 171 crash at ‘fag end’, Centre tells Supreme Court

stories.Headline: Democrats prepare to take Congress and press Trump on AI rules and data center costs
stories.Summary:
Democrats are preparing to take control of Congress in January, setting up a possible confrontation with President Donald Trump over artificial intelligence, data centers and how much responsibility technology companies should bear when AI causes harm, according to azfamily.com. Polling showed AI was a significant issue for many voters in the midterms. An NBC News exit poll found that 56% of voters considered AI and data centers a crucial or major factor in their congressional vote, while 76% of respondents opposed construction of a new data center in their community. In both cases, those respondents favored Democrats by about 30 percentage points. Caroline Lynch, a former congressional committee counsel and founder of the lobbying firm Copper Hill Strategies, said the election could mark a turning point.

Lynch said one of the most promising areas for compromise is who should pay for the enormous electricity demands of AI data centers. She pointed to the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, a Senate proposal that would require data centers to pay for the additional electricity infrastructure needed to serve them rather than passing those costs to other customers. That proposal goes further than the Ratepayer Protection Act, which passed the Republican-controlled House 417-3 in September and required states to consider adopting protections for electricity customers but did not require them to implement those protections. Lynch said there is currently no comprehensive federal requirement governing how much of those costs data center operators must absorb. Democrats are also exploring ways to hold AI developers responsible when their technology causes harm, including situations in which autonomous AI systems commit fraud, breach computer networks or expose sensitive information.

Lynch, a former prosecutor, said existing criminal laws generally require prosecutors to identify a responsible person or corporation, and applying those laws when an AI system acts beyond its instructions presents unresolved legal questions. She said Congress may eventually have to address whether AI developers should receive protections similar to Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act, which shields online platforms for content created by third parties. Rep. Yassamin Ansari has called for a pause on advanced AI development and a ban on superintelligence, while Sen. Mark Kelly has proposed taxing certain AI-related windfall profits to help fund worker retraining. Lynch believes narrower regulations have a better chance of attracting support than sweeping restrictions on advanced AI.

Lynch predicted Democrats may advance AI bills in a bid to call the president's bluff, forcing Trump to decide whether to block measures addressing concerns about the technology. Lawmakers could also try attaching AI provisions to larger spending bills, making a veto politically more complicated, she said. Democrats will gain control of congressional committees and the ability to summon technology executives for oversight hearings, and Texas Rep. Greg Casar has discussed calling AI executives to testify under oath. Lynch cautioned that such hearings can produce more political theater than substantive results, but she noted that several leading AI companies have publicly supported some form of federal regulation, which could make the hearings less confrontational than previous congressional investigations of social media companies.

Articles.Title: What’s next for AI regulation once Democrats control Congress?

stories.headline_source: What’s next for AI regulation once Democrats control Congress?

stories.Headline: KB Securities invests 2 billion won in UNIST Holdings regional tourism AI fund
stories.Summary:
KB Securities announced on November 19 that it invested 2 billion won into a specialized venture investment association. This specific fund focuses on deep tech and artificial intelligence for regional tourism and is managed by UNIST Holdings. The investment was made through Npay Startup, which is a venture capital platform that connects various investors with emerging companies. This transaction represents the first time a financial firm has committed capital using this particular digital investment platform.

The total value of the fund is 15.4 billion won, which includes 10 billion won from the Korea Venture Investment Corp. fund of funds. UNIST Holdings will use these resources to identify regional startups that utilize AI technology in the tourism sector to provide them with growth capital. The Npay Startup platform was launched in July with official support from the Ministry of SMEs and Startups and the Financial Supervisory Service. This initiative aims to shift the flow of venture capital away from the greater Seoul area toward promising local companies.

A representative from KB Securities stated that this move is meaningful because it expands the supply of venture capital to regional areas. The official added that the firm intends to continue contributing to balanced growth and the revitalization of regional economies through productive finance. This action follows a meeting on the 12th of this month where the Financial Supervisory Service urged financial firms to diversify their channels for supplying capital. The regulator specifically cited the review of this funding proposal as a positive example for other comprehensive financial investment business operators.

stories.Headline: Vasudha Gadhiraju grounds Normal's AI rollout in cross-agency data work
stories.Summary:
The 57 cities recognized in this year's survey from the Center for Digital Government are prioritizing AI while modernizing core systems and upgrading data infrastructure, GovTech reported on Nov. 16, 2026. Leading cities are putting guardrails in place, launching AI-driven applications and adopting agentic workflows. At the same time, they're exploring new cybersecurity strategies, upgrading legacy systems and elevating the health of their data pipelines. In the face of lean budgets and rapid changes in technology, IT leaders are positioning themselves as strategic partners with city agencies. They're driving innovation while continuously improving both constituent engagement and employee experiences.

In Normal, Ill., Director of Innovation and Technology Vasudha Gadhiraju follows two guiding principles: make digital transformation a cross-agency effort, and ground the work in data. Grounded in the What Works Cities framework from Bloomberg Philanthropies, the approach now includes a cross-departmental Data Innovation Team that is helping build data governance and literacy. The town is leveraging training from InnovateUS, and it has begun to onboard AI applications, with an immediate focus on upgrading from a machine-learning-based chatbot to a true AI interface. The IT team has implemented the "Normal Forum," a platform used to document project updates and solicit constituent feedback around road safety. The town shares its public rights-of-way with Illinois State University, so safety for pedestrians, cyclists, motorists and transit users is of the utmost importance.

In Schaumburg, Ill., Director of Information Technology Peter Schaak said he was eager to embrace AI, but early on the village wanted to put some guardrails around it and to structure its approach. That has meant putting in place a high-level administrative protocol that instructs employees in effect to do good things, don't do bad things, with AI. From there he implemented a standard operating procedure, and the village did some training around both those documents to introduce and encourage the use of AI in the organization. The immediate impact of that effort has included adoption of Microsoft Copilot as the preferred internal AI tool, and the village also launched an external AI virtual assistant and an internal-facing virtual assistant, named for Serena and Louis, two swans that live on the municipal campus. The team also is working to leverage AI in short-term rental analysis tools to identify properties that are maybe not registered as rental properties but being used as short term rentals, the Airbnbs and Vrbos of the world.

In Corona, Calif., CIO Chris McMasters said it starts out with governance and security, and without that in place the city wouldn't have been able to do the things it is doing today. The IT team moved early to identify all the shadow AI already in use and then built policy around what people were actually doing with the tools, and the city adjusted its licenses to support the AI tools people were actually using, and IT worked with a startup to implement a security platform. An AI agent will tee up a graffiti complaint work order with human oversight and communicate the outcomes back to the resident, taking a process that was about 20 minutes per incident down to less than three minutes per incident. The IT team also replaced its 30-year-old ERP and HR systems with Workday last year, the culmination of two years' labor. The team also embedded an agent across the city websites that can watch when people are getting frustrated, hanging too long on a page or clicking wildly, and can prompt a human to intercept.

In Virginia Beach, CIO Peter Wallace said IT is not a call center, but a value center, and the tech team needs to deliver tangible results, and faced with budget cuts, you've got to be measurable. In Schaumburg, the IT team undertook an initiative to create worst-case scenario runbooks, and that entailed a ton of sequencing and dependency analysis and operational timing, and the team worked through all of those over the span of the year. The runbooks establish responsibilities and sequencing and assignment of personnel, a whole long list of roles and responsibilities and tasks to help the team get through a catastrophic breach. As Schaumburg built a new village hall, the tech team had to disassemble its main operations area and rebuild it in a temporary facility, and this fall the team was in the midst of taking it apart again and shifting to a brand-new facility. In Corona, IT is in the midst of consolidating city data on a single platform, and the city will use that to generate profiles about the people that engage with it, so that when it puts out things, it is much more targeted.

In Normal, Gadhiraju said the town wants to make sure people truly understand the advantages of AI and the efficiencies it brings, while also recognizing where AI may not be able to deliver at scale. She said there are so many vendors now who quickly use the word AI to sell products, and a lot of these vendors are approaching the town's departments directly, and people need to ask the right questions and not be tempted by the bells and whistles. She said data and technology and innovation should always work towards solving a problem that the community is facing. In Schaumburg, Schaak said the village's focus is on operational benefits, and it is moving out of the world of funny graphics and songs and trying to be strategic in how it deploys these tools. He said the focus is to be fiscally responsible while always leaning forward, always looking to expand services, improve services, improve response times, in an environment of continuous improvement.

In Corona, McMasters said the city is being very methodical about how it engages the public, to give them the things they want, and there is this memory the city is creating so that people's experiences with their government can be persistent. He said IT played a huge role in the project management, bringing all the departments together, executing and then leading everyone through, and outside consultants helped as well, and their involvement knocks down a lot of the bureaucracy and the politics and helps to streamline things. In Normal, Gadhiraju said across departments the town all works collaboratively, and it could not do what it is doing without the type of culture that it has, and while the city's approach to data has been years in the making, it has really come together in the past year. She said the IT team has worked to build strong data pipelines, making sure that it has good back-end connections to its systems so that data can be put to work, and there is now a dashboard that shows at a glance how well the town is doing on its goal of planting more trees than it removes, and another to help manage cellphone expenses. She said the town is truly building in the measurement in every aspect of the work it does, and she is optimistic about the new AI interface, and the town does need a chatbot, and it needs to make sure people can easily ask it questions.

stories.Headline: Anthropic floats on the US stock exchange, making its seven founders multi-billionaires
stories.Summary:
Seven founders of the AI firm Anthropic will become multi-billionaires on paper very soon. These individuals left the rival company OpenAI in 2021 to start their own venture. The company announced on Wednesday that it is floating the business on the US stock exchange. This move follows five years of growth from an unknown start-up to a tech giant. The firm is now worth more than a trillion dollars.

Anthropic will sell its shares at $83 each on the US stock exchange. This price makes the founders' shareholdings worth at least $19.3bn each. Dario Amodei will have $19.7bn, while Daniela Amodei and Jack Clark will have $19.8bn. Jared Kaplan also has $19.8bn, while Chris Olah and Sam McCandlish will each have $19.9bn. Tom Brown will hold the highest amount at $20bn.

Chief executive Dario Amodei left OpenAI because he worried some people put profit before safety. President Daniela Amodei says her brother is the person who makes the company ambitious. Chief compute officer Tom Brown argued that datacentres are an enormous source of prosperity. Jack Clark serves as head of public benefit and leads the Anthropic Institute think tank. Chief science officer Jared Kaplan heads technical research and teaches at Johns Hopkins University.

Chris Olah is the interpretability research lead and is reportedly exploring morality and AI. The New York Times describes Olah as boyish with the zeal of an evangelist. Sam McCandlish is the chief architect who helps implement policy to mitigate AI risks. These seven founders will each own around 1.6 percent of the company. Their stakes will crystallise into hugely valuable assets after the shares go on sale.

Dario Amodei studied physics at Princeton and Stanford before switching to biology and biomedical sciences. Daniela Amodei studied English Literature at the University of California Santa Cruz and worked for Matt Cartwright. Tom Brown led GPT-3 engineering at OpenAI and previously worked on the Google DeepMind project. Jack Clark is a former technology journalist from Brighton who studied at the University of East Anglia. Chris Olah received a $100,000 Thiel Fellowship after leaving the University of Toronto early.

The company will now move from being a private start-up to a public entity. The founders will transition from being tech entrepreneurs to some of the world's wealthiest people. The articles do not state when the shares will officially begin trading. They do not mention the specific reactions of rival firms to this valuation. The text leaves open how the founders will use their new wealth.

stories.Headline: Jason Wei leaves Meta to become chief scientist at AI startup Mercor
stories.Summary:
Jason Wei, known as the father of Chain-of-Thought, left Meta to join the AI startup Mercor on November 18, 2026. Brendan Foody, the CEO and co-founder of Mercor, announced the hire on the X platform. Wei has officially taken the role of Chief Scientist at the company. This move follows his time at Meta's Superintelligence Lab. He previously worked at Google Brain and OpenAI.

Mercor is an AI unicorn valued at 200 billion US dollars that recently completed a 750 million dollar Series D financing. The funding involved NVIDIA, Salesforce, Benchmark, and General Catalyst. The company was founded in 2023 by Brendan Foody, Surya Midha, and Adarsh Hiremath. It provides expert data services and talent recruitment using a network of over 5 million people. The new funds will support post-training infrastructure, model evaluation, and AI agent workflows.

Brendan Foody stated that Jason Wei will help build a research team focused on data and evaluation. He noted that Wei had been a customer and a communication partner for the company for several years. Jason Wei expressed happiness about joining Mercor after spending over a year at Meta TBD Lab. He believes that data will shape the next frontier of AI development as more companies train models. His work will intersect with his previous experience in creating evaluation benchmarks.

The transition affects AI labs and enterprise customers who need specialized data for financial, legal, or software engineering tasks. Mercor's research team already includes Edward J. Hu, the first author of the LoRA paper. Other team members include Victor Barres and Minyang Tian, with researchers from Ai2 and Anthropic. The company uses the APEX benchmarks to test if AI can complete actual work requirements. They recently improved a Qwen3.5-397B model score from 16 percent to 27 percent on APEX-Agents.

Wei became famous for a 2022 paper on Chain-of-Thought Prompting that improved multi-step reasoning in large language models. While at OpenAI in 2023, he worked on Deep Research and OpenAI o1. He developed SimpleQA in 2024 to measure factual accuracy using 4326 questions. In 2025, he released BrowseComp for web search and HealthBench for medical conversations. He then joined Meta's Superintelligence Lab in July 2025.

Wei will now focus on promoting research in data and evaluation for real work scenarios. Mercor is expanding its services from providing expert data to helping customers adapt AI models. The company aims to discover tasks models cannot complete and use experts to build training data. The articles do not state the specific projects Wei will lead first. They leave open the long-term impact of his move to a data-focused startup.

stories.Headline: Lawmakers move to preserve 2026 CSAT exam papers as police investigate Lee Jin-woo for AI cheating
stories.Summary:
Lawmakers sought to preserve exam papers on November 19, 2026, to investigate AI cheating. Lee Jin-woo, 32, faces allegations of using artificial intelligence on several high stakes tests. He scored a perfect mark on the Legal Education Eligibility Test. He also took the College Scholastic Ability Test for the 2026 academic year. Police are now investigating him for fraud and obstruction of official duties.

The request covers original question booklets, OMR answer sheets, and scoring records from the 2026 CSAT. Rep. Jung Sung-kook sent letters to the Ministry of Education and provincial education offices. Rep. Park Jung-hun noted Lee's papers were kept at Younghoon High School in Seoul. The 2026 CSAT was administered on November 13 of the previous year. These materials include handover documents for each test district and site.

Rep. Jung Sung-kook said authorities should check for AI cheating on past exams. He argued that a lack of handwritten calculations might suggest AI use. He proposed reviewing score distributions and work traces for medical and dental admissions. Jung stated that these traces are circumstantial evidence to be weighed with other material. He suggested expanding the review if multiple suspicious cases are confirmed.

Lee Jin-woo is affected by these allegations and a police investigation. Some people allege he cheated on the 2024 and 2026 CSAT exams. Reporters and instructors waited for him at the IDA Admissions Research Institute. About 2,000 people joined a YouTube live stream to watch his verification. Lee failed to appear for the session and could not be reached.

Lee previously scored in the sixth to eighth grade bands on earlier CSAT exams. He entered Korea University in 2024 and Seoul National University dental school in 2026. Doubts arose after a top certified tax accountant was caught cheating with AI. The Korea Institute for Curriculum and Evaluation usually destroys booklets after one year. The retention period for the 2026 CSAT papers has already lapsed.

Police are searching for Lee after he disappeared from his Gwanak District home. He was last seen leaving lodgings in Gwangjin District on the morning of November 19. He had agreed to metal detectors and endoscopic checks for the verification session. The police investigation will now determine the facts behind the cheating allegations. It remains open whether Lee actually used AI to improve his scores.

stories.Headline: Micron President says China lags behind in high bandwidth memory development
stories.Summary:
Scott J. DeBoer, the President and Chief Technology and Products Officer of Micron, spoke about the global artificial intelligence chip race on November 18, 2026. During an interview with Deirdre Bosa on Yahoo Finance, he addressed the current competitive landscape regarding high bandwidth memory. He stated that China is currently far behind other nations in the development of this specific memory technology. This discussion highlighted the ongoing struggle for technological dominance in the semiconductor industry during a period of rapid growth.

Maintaining a lead in this sector requires a constant focus on outperforming all global competitors through superior core technology. DeBoer emphasized that Micron must partner with key customers to build products that are better than any others available in the world. This strategy involves staying significantly ahead of rivals from China, Korea, and other regions to ensure market leadership. The company believes that the only way to win is to create products that no other entity can build.

DeBoer explained that the memory business has been intensely competitive for the past 30 years without any periods of respite. He noted that there is always someone attempting to beat them, which is why the company takes this competition very seriously. When asked about political restrictions versus innovation, he replied that he can only control the ability to out innovate and compete. He mentioned that political aspects are not in his personal picture because his primary job is to deliver the products.

The context of these remarks reflects a broader international effort to secure the most advanced hardware for artificial intelligence applications. Micron intends to maintain its advantage by focusing on technical excellence rather than relying on external restrictions to hobble competitors. The company will continue to prioritize the development of high bandwidth memory to support the evolving needs of the AI chip market. Future success depends on the ability to sustain this technological gap through continuous research and strategic partnerships.

stories.Headline: UC law school launches three-day certificate lab to teach lawyers AI tool building
stories.Summary:
LexLab, which serves as the legal technology hub for the University of California College of the Law at San Francisco, is launching a new educational program. This intensive three-day course, known as the Law & AI Certificate Lab, will take place from December 1 to December 3, 2026. The program provides lawyers and organizational leaders with a condensed version of a semester-long course previously offered only to law students. Participants will engage in a deep dive into the logic of legal artificial intelligence through hands-on exploration of various systems.

The curriculum requires students to utilize the AI platform Harvey and the AI company Legora, along with the website builder Replit. Graduates of the certificate program should be able to create repeatable checklists, playbooks, and other workflows instead of simply using chat functions. The training teaches students how to evaluate different AI vendors and decide if technology should be purchased or built internally. Additionally, the course covers how to manage competence, conflicts, confidentiality, and privilege issues within an AI-augmented legal practice.

The University of California College of the Law at San Francisco is responsible for implementing this specialized training for legal professionals. The institution designed the course to help practitioners move beyond basic AI interactions toward more sophisticated tool building and management. By providing this technical foundation, the school aims to equip leaders with the skills necessary to navigate the complexities of modern legal technology. The program focuses on the practical application of AI to improve efficiency and maintain professional standards in the law.

stories.Headline: Getty appeals to the Court of Appeal over whether AI models can be infringing copies
stories.Summary:
Getty Images is appealing to the Court of Appeal in its dispute with Stability AI, the developer of the Stable Diffusion image generator. The appeal is being heard over two days, Wednesday and Thursday, in the week of 11 November 2026. The High Court gave its first instance judgment in November 2025 and largely favoured Stability AI. Getty succeeded on only a small part of its trade mark claim, and its copyright claim failed. Getty's barrister told the court that Stability "doesn't think it should have to pay" for Getty's content.

The central question is whether an AI model can be an "infringing copy" under section 27(3) of the Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988, even if the model never contained copies of the works. Stable Diffusion was trained outside the UK, so Getty dropped its primary copyright claims during the trial and kept only a secondary infringement case. That case argued that the model was an infringing copy imported into, and distributed in, the UK. The High Court accepted that an intangible AI model can be an "article", but held that an infringing copy must actually be a copy. Because the model weights had never stored Getty's images, the High Court ruled that the model could not be an infringing copy.

Getty says that "making" a model includes training it, which involves copying images, and that the finished model need not itself contain copies. In its view, if making the article in the UK would have infringed copyright, the article is an infringing copy whether or not it holds copies. Getty's barrister said Stability wants to separate what was done with the copyright works from the act of training, but can only do so by mischaracterising the facts. Stability AI argues that whether something is a copy depends on what is actually produced, not on how it was developed. It says Getty's approach would produce odd results, such as making it unlawful to import the model but lawful to copy it once it is in the UK.

The British Recorded Music Industry Limited, known as BPI, represents the UK recorded music industry and has permission to intervene in support of Getty. It warns that the High Court's approach could let developers train models offshore and bring them back into the UK, with significant consequences for the music and wider creative industries. BPI also notes that Getty accepted at trial that the versions of Stable Diffusion did not contain copies, and cites two recent German cases in which the Munich Court found that models had memorised works they were trained on. On that basis BPI says the Getty judgment has "no wider significance" on whether models contain copies, because the question depends on the facts of each model. Stability AI also argues that extending the law to models trained overseas is a matter for Parliament, not the courts, and it has cross-appealed two findings that went against it.

The High Court case was heard in June 2025, and Getty dropped one of its primary copyright infringement claims just two weeks into the trial. The claims that remained before Mrs Justice Joanna Smith were secondary infringement, trademark infringement and passing off. The court found that Getty succeeded in part on trademark infringement, but only for older models and on isolated examples. Getty had alleged that Stability copied and processed millions of copyrighted images to train Stable Diffusion in the US. Stability's directors include the filmmaker James Cameron, and Stability argues that the images were downloaded and stored in data centres outside the UK, so UK copyright law does not apply.

Stability AI is asking the Court of Appeal to overturn two findings that went against it at first instance: that an intangible model can be an "article", and that Stability itself imported or distributed the model in the UK. Getty disputes both points. If Getty succeeds, developers could face UK copyright claims over models trained abroad on unlicensed works, even where the imported model stores no copies. If Stability succeeds, where a model is trained and whether it stores copies will remain key to any claims. The judgment has not yet been handed down, and the Government continues to consider its approach to copyright and AI following its March 2026 report.

stories.Headline: LinkedIn's Sundara Raman Ramachandran details scaling a distilled LLM ranking system to 1.3 billion members
stories.Summary:
LinkedIn has implemented a scalable large language model based ranking system for its search and recommendation workloads, serving 1.3 billion members globally, TechGig reported on November 18, 2026. Sundara Raman Ramachandran, a tech lead at LinkedIn, detailed the challenges and solutions in an InfoQ presentation. The company reduced a 7 billion parameter model to 400 million parameters through multi-teacher distillation and pruning. Context compression cut job description prompt lengths from 2,000 tokens to 150 through summarisation, or to a single embedding.

These offline optimisations produced an 8x to 10x throughput improvement with less than 2 per cent quality loss. LinkedIn introduced a dedicated scoring API in the open-source SGLang engine to bypass unnecessary decode phases in ranking workloads. Inference optimisations addressed CPU bottlenecks with batch tokenisation and batch integrity across inter-process communication. GPU underutilisation was tackled by replacing synchronous blocking copies with asynchronous non-blocking copies for probabilities. A custom Item-Aware Attention Mask concatenates multiple item prompts into a single LLM input, reusing query key-value pairs.

Python-specific issues included latency spikes from garbage collection, mitigated using gc.freeze after model warm-up. The Global Interpreter Lock bottleneck in gRPC servicer and SGLang worker processes was resolved by using multiple processes. Learnings include benchmarking production traffic with Poisson distribution and ensuring absolute parity between offline and online systems. LinkedIn reported a 5 per cent to 10 per cent increase in auction metrics, such as relevance and engagement, due to LLM-based re-ranking.

stories.Headline: Siemens India showcases industrial AI and digital twins to cut engineering timelines and costs
stories.Summary:
Artificial intelligence is being integrated into India's manufacturing, infrastructure and transportation sectors in a push aimed at boosting productivity and encouraging sustainable practices, according to TechGig. The report says the move could reduce engineering timelines and costs, and it describes the integration of AI with engineering knowledge, real-time operational data, automation and digital twins as central to Siemens India Innovation Day 2026. That event, held under the theme "AI for the Real World," highlights AI deployed in industrial environments where reliability, safety, cybersecurity and measurable outcomes are critical, the article says. Applications named in the report include AI-assisted engineering, predictive maintenance, automated quality inspection and process optimisation, all of which rely on a connected foundation linking information technology and operational technology.

The article explains that digital twins are virtual representations of products, machines or infrastructure assets used to design, simulate, validate and optimise their physical counterparts, which helps find problems digitally so corrections are faster and cheaper before physical construction. Physical AI extends artificial intelligence into machines and physical systems so they can interpret objectives and respond to changing conditions autonomously, a progression from rule-based to intent-based automation. For India, the report says, this offers a chance to leapfrog older stages of industrial automation and compress technological progress that previously took many years, while companies that do not adopt Physical AI risk falling behind global competitors. Every AI model depends on physical infrastructure including computing capacity, electricity, cooling, connectivity, automation and resilient operations, and the challenge for customers is to design and operate that capacity efficiently and reliably at scale, according to the article.

Autonomous buildings use connected data and domain-specific AI to sense conditions, predict requirements and take governed action, with potential applications in energy optimisation, predictive maintenance and improved occupant comfort, the report says. Sunil Mathur, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Siemens Limited, noted that energy accounts for a significant portion of operating costs in industries like hotels and cement plants, making efficiency improvements impactful. On railways, the article says India's transformation can leverage digitalisation, automation and data to enhance infrastructure intelligence, with technologies such as Signaling X, Communications-Based Train Control and predictive maintenance applications supporting safer, more connected operations and better asset availability. The stated objective is to gain greater value from every train, signal, power system and physical asset throughout its operating life.

stories.Headline: Dell says context lifts AI agent accuracy from 60% to 94% in its testing
stories.Summary:
Dell Technologies executives said at SC26, in an interview broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media's livestreaming studio, that feeding AI agents the right context lifted accuracy in Dell's own testing from roughly 60% to about 94%, and they described new data intelligence features meant to bring enterprise AI factories into production. Srinath Alapati, senior director of product marketing for AI Data Platform at Dell, said the bottom line is that wrong data produces wrong outcomes. He appeared with Alison Biers, senior director of product marketing for compute, networking and global industries, and Adam Glick, senior director of AI solutions product marketing for compute, in a conversation with theCUBE Research's John Furrier. Dell recently extended its AI Data Platform with semantic and knowledge graph features aimed at enterprises that want the large-scale AI capabilities neocloud providers built first.

Dell's newly announced Agentic Data Gateway sits in the orchestration layer as a single point of control backed by a Model Context Protocol server, according to Alapati, because enterprises cannot give agents unfettered access to their systems. Storage intelligence tells customers what data they hold, who owns it and how large it is, while the new data intelligence capabilities track lineage and provenance, and hybrid workflows extend the model across the edge, the cloud and the data center. Alapati said other data platform providers want customers to bring all data to the platform, which is not always possible because it is expensive and data is always being generated, so Dell sends only metadata and leaves data where customers want it. On infrastructure, Dell OpenManage Rack Scale extends management beyond compute endpoints to the network fabric, power and cooling, giving operators a single operational plane from day zero through day two, Biers said. A rebuilt, intent-based Dell Fabric Manager replaces SmartFabric Manager, and PowerRack systems treat the full rack as the unit of deployment.

Biers said a rack goes from the loading dock to full production in literally six hours, work that used to take months and is now cut in half or less. Glick said more than 6,500 customers now use the Dell AI Factory, and a growing share are core enterprises asking for help putting AI to work, while validated designs built with Nvidia and other partners cover both hardware and the full software stack and Dell is expanding its labs as independent software companies join the ecosystem. He compared compute to a factory's assembly line, which does not run without a warehouse feeding it raw materials, meaning the data that goes into it. The segment was sponsored by Dell, and the disclosure states that neither Dell nor other sponsors have editorial control over content on theCUBE or SiliconANGLE.

stories.Headline: Trinity College philosophy faculty ban students from using AI in coursework
stories.Summary:
Trinity College’s philosophy department has barred students from using generative artificial intelligence on coursework, arguing the technology undermines its mission of teaching students to think, read, write, speak, reason and live ethically. The department’s faculty members, including Shane Ewegen, began deliberating on the policy with colleagues in the spring. Faculty members agreed in September on a concise three-sentence rule. The rule states that any use of AI in any capacity and for any purpose is forbidden. The department notified the campus community of the change last month.

The policy forbids students from using AI in any capacity whatsoever in preparation for classes or in the classroom for philosophy courses. It specifies that students cannot use AI for brainstorming, for writing or editing, or even to construct bibliographies. The policy states that using AI for any of those reasons undermines the core educational missions of the department. The department settled on a fairly short version of the policy after exchanging emails with different versions, some lengthy and detailed and some very short. The policy leaves any punitive repercussions for violating it entirely up to the individual professor’s discretion.

Ewegen said the philosophy department was univocal in adopting the policy and its language, though members may have differing perspectives on the reasoning behind it. He said that over the summer faculty started exchanging emails about adopting a single policy for all philosophy courses, above all to avoid confusion among students if each professor had a different policy. He said that the more they talked, the clearer it became that they were more or less in agreement in being emphatically against AI in its academic uses, really in any capacity. He said he wanted to include a sentence saying a student would fail the class if evidence of use was discovered, but it was pointed out that other members might feel differently and that a professor might in the moment feel a different outcome was warranted. Ewegen said he has tried to explain to students that the product being sold to them by billionaires’ companies promises something while in fact stealing something from them.

A Trinity College spokesperson said the college’s leaders recognize AI’s rapid expansion and remain committed to open, ongoing dialogue across the campus community. The spokesperson said that consistent with practices across higher education, faculty determine when and how AI is used in their courses based on their expertise and learning objectives. The spokesperson said the college believes students should be prepared for a world in which AI is increasingly present, including developing the knowledge and judgment to use these tools responsibly and effectively. The spokesperson said Trinity encourages faculty and students to engage thoughtfully with complex questions concerning the appropriate use of AI in an academic setting and the broader opportunities and challenges AI presents. The University of Chicago banned AI and tech in class in the social-sciences division, and Duke University’s classical-studies department expressly prohibits the use of AI on assignments.

Trinity’s collegewide AI guidance says faculty are responsible for defining the content and goals of their courses, communicating expectations, and evaluating students fairly and consistently. The guidance says students in turn make choices about their learning, from engaging in self-reflection to practicing integrity and deciding whether AI will replace their own thinking. The guidance says these practices extend to AI, shaping lifelong capacities related to purpose, resilience, and decision making. The administration devised its policies with minimal faculty input and with no faculty vote, and they are meant to apply to the college as a whole. Ewegen said he had heard students admitting to some confusion because they were not really sure, getting information from the administration and differing policies from each individual professor.

Ewegen said that in the department’s conversations, faculty agreed that really any use of AI for philosophy courses or philosophy research undermines rather than facilitates learning goals. He said the department has not seen evidence that using AI to help brainstorm, edit a paper, write a paper, or serve as an interlocutor for studying for oral finals promotes or improves students’ ability to engage in those skills. He said the department sees more and more reports about the harmful effects of AI on students’ abilities to think, read and write. He said the department was worried about ethical considerations surrounding AI, including the environmental impact of developing and using AI, such as mining massive mineral sites in the global south that contaminates water supplies. He said the department did not think the technology at this stage is redeemable in any way, at least when it comes to use in a philosophical classroom.

Ewegen said his personal hope is that the policy will provoke other departments to codify policies of their own and make those policies public. He said it is only beneficial if there is a broader conversation within the institution and across institutions about this technology and the dangers it poses. He spearheaded a faculty effort earlier this year calling on Trinity to divest from AI companies. Each faculty member now has the policy to include on their syllabi, and whether there are punitive effects and what they are will depend in each case. Ewegen said that in his case it usually means certainly failing the assignment and more likely the course if it comes to light that a student has used AI in some substantive way.

Articles.Title: Why This Philosophy Department Is Banning AI

stories.Headline: Microsoft and Salesforce launch Copilotforce to bring Salesforce context into Microsoft Copilot
stories.Summary:
Microsoft and Salesforce announced Copilotforce on Nov. 17, 2026, from Redmond, Washington, and San Francisco, unveiling it at Microsoft Ignite. The partnership brings Salesforce customer context, business processes and actions into Microsoft Copilot and other AI-powered productivity experiences. It introduces integrations across Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Teams and Microsoft Fabric, including Salesforce in Copilot, a plugin in public preview with 38 or more prebuilt sales skills. Salesforce in Copilot is available in public preview as a beta beginning today. Microsoft Work IQ, the intelligence layer powering Copilot, provides context from Teams meetings, Outlook emails and documents across SharePoint and OneDrive.

Salesforce in Copilot connects customer context with work across the business so employees can decide and act without switching applications. Through authenticated Salesforce MCP access, sellers can retrieve customer information and take supported business actions within existing Salesforce permissions. Salesforce continues to govern access and business actions, while Microsoft applies existing enterprise compliance controls to communications and documents. Supported writeback actions to the CRM require explicit user confirmation and respect existing validation rules. A two-way Zero Copy connection between Salesforce Data 360 and Microsoft Fabric lets teams work across both platforms without building pipelines or maintaining duplicate datasets.

Judson Althoff, CEO of Microsoft Commercial Business, said AI is only as powerful as the data and context that grounds it. He said bringing Salesforce customer data and sales skills together with Work IQ context in Copilot lets joint customers unlock actionable insights across core business applications. He said Copilotforce will give sales teams intelligence for faster, higher-confidence decisions while maintaining the governance and trust enterprises demand. Miguel Milano, President and Chief Operating Officer of Salesforce, said Copilotforce brings Salesforce to the largest surface in enterprise software today. He said combining the number one CRM with the number one productivity surface transforms AI from a standalone tool into a driver of productivity, smarter decisions and customer success.

Julie Sweet, Chair and CEO of Accenture, said Accenture is a Global Partner of the Year for both Salesforce and Microsoft and one of their top customers. She said the combined strengths of the three companies will reinvent sales with AI, giving sellers more time with customers while trusted intelligence and agents work alongside them. Accenture is the design and implementation partner, with expertise across 13 industries globally, and a pilot customer deploying the integrations in its own global sales organization. Accenture has scaled Copilot to more than 740,000 people and is one of the largest Salesforce users globally with 55,000 users.

Accenture is also customer zero for Copilotforce, sharing learnings to help clients turn existing Salesforce and Microsoft investments into a better way to sell. The Pipeline Review and Close Planning skills help decide which opportunities deserve attention and build a path to signature, with proposals and business cases in Word and PowerPoint. The Deal Review, Customer Health and Renewal Radar skills see beyond the recorded stage or renewal date to a customer concern in an Outlook thread, an escalation in Teams or an unresolved commitment behind a stalled deal. The Call Follow-Up skill turns customer conversations into follow-up drafts, internal recaps and proposed CRM activities.

Sales Cloud in Teams, now available in pilot, brings Salesforce customer context into conversations so sellers can see pipeline and quota progress, get deal notifications and find briefing materials. With Data Federation, now generally available, joint customers can directly query and analyze supported Microsoft Fabric OneLake data within Salesforce Data 360. A service agent can see a customer's recent purchases, a marketer can build a segment from spending behavior and an AI agent can answer from current data, all without moving source data out of Fabric. The Salesforce Data 360 shortcut, now in public preview, lets organizations share curated Data 360 customer intelligence into OneLake for analytics, reporting and AI workloads without duplicating data.

Data sharing from Data 360 into OneLake is in public preview, and Sales Cloud in Teams is in pilot with enterprise customers, with open beta coming later this year. Statements about future direction and intent are subject to change or withdrawal without notice and represent goals and objectives only. Regional availability and customer access are governed by applicable customer agreements. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Agent builders weigh browser infrastructure tools for authenticated access, stealth and scale
stories.Summary:
AI agents require specialised browser infrastructure to interact with web systems that lack clean APIs, according to TechGig. These tools provide hosted or self-hosted browsers that agents can drive programmatically, managing sessions, authentication, stealth and isolation for developers. Running browsers reliably at scale, with logins, sessions, stealth and isolation, poses a significant infrastructure challenge that these tools are designed to address. The article was published on November 18, 2026, and describes a range of tools rather than a single product launch. Agent builders weigh several needs when choosing among these tools, including authenticated access, session persistence, stealth and anti-bot capabilities, scale and isolation, and framework compatibility.

Anchor Browser focuses on authenticated enterprise access for SSO, MFA and VPN-protected applications, offering persistent session state and integration with existing agent frameworks via an SDK. Browserbase provides a general-purpose platform for hosted headless Chromium sessions and works with Playwright, Puppeteer or Selenium. Browserless offers hosted or self-hosted browser endpoints supporting Chrome, Firefox and WebKit, while Steel is an open-source, self-hostable remote browser infrastructure with built-in stealth, CAPTCHA handling and proxy options. Browser Use combines an open-source automation library with a low-cost, pay-per-minute hosted cloud, featuring built-in stealth and CAPTCHA handling. Bright Data Browser API integrates hosted Chromium with its large proxy network and excels at proxy-heavy scraping at scale, handling fingerprinting and CAPTCHA solving for tough sites.

Kernel isolates each Chromium instance in its own virtual machine, providing strong separation between browser workloads and billing by memory time for isolation-sensitive use cases. Lightpanda is an open-source headless browser built for speed and low memory use, optimising for fast page reading at scale, though it does not render graphics. The article states that the optimal tool depends on the agent's specific workload, and that prioritising authenticated access, public web data collection, control or fast content reading guides the selection process. It does not name any company or individual as responsible for these tools beyond the products described, and it does not include statements from the vendors themselves. No further steps, timelines or announcements are given beyond the guidance that selection should follow the workload.

stories.Headline: Tokenomics Foundation launches as Linux Foundation project to set open AI cost standards
stories.Summary:
The Tokenomics Foundation launched in August 2026 as a project of the Linux Foundation, working alongside the FinOps Foundation, which did the same job for cloud spending, according to a November 18, 2026 opinion piece by Raul Leite in InfoWorld. Its members include large AI buyers such as banks and retailers, plus cloud and model providers, and it does not sell a product or ship a cost-tracking tool. Instead it acts as a standards body whose working groups publish open, vendor-neutral definitions, so everyone means the same thing by input, output, reasoning and cached tokens, and standards for cost data that mainly extend FOCUS, the FinOps billing format, so AI providers report usage in the same way. The actual measuring is done by tools on the market, like AI gateways and observability platforms, and the Foundation's job is to make sure they all speak the same language.

The piece defines AI tokenomics as the practice of managing that economy and connecting the cost structure to business outcomes, noting that one token is roughly 4 characters, or 0.75 words, in English, and that the term has nothing to do with crypto, where it means the supply and incentives of a coin. Leite describes a stack mapping everything that shapes the cost of an AI answer, from energy and hardware at the bottom through infrastructure management, inference, model selection, and access and control, to demand at the top, and says its value is showing where to look before you start cutting. He also presents Big-T, an idea like Big-O notation in programming, describing how fast token use grows as more people use an app, including agent-multiplied growth where agents spawn other agents and calls pile up fast, and unbounded growth where a loop with no exit runs until someone pulls the plug. The key insight, he writes, is that the multiplier is usually invisible, since a user asks one question and the app makes five or 10 calls behind the scenes.

Leite, a principal solution architect at Red Hat who says the views are his own, writes that token prices keep falling but AI bills keep rising, because cheaper tokens lead teams to build bigger systems with longer conversations, more documents per question and agents calling agents. He says the big savings usually come from the middle and the top of the stack, using a smaller model for simple tasks, caching repeated work and sending less context, and he advises asking of every workflow how many model calls one user request really triggers. He sums up the Foundation's mission as moving AI from experimental spending to accountable operations, since most organizations cannot connect their AI spend to an outcome their CFO would accept, and says it wants to fix that by building open standards, benchmarks and a shared language. The goal, he writes, is not just about making AI cheaper but about making it worth it.

Articles.Title: Tokenomics Foundation: Making sense of what AI actually costs you

stories.Headline: Florida House speaker urges quick action on AI as Senate president prioritizes affordability
stories.Summary:
Florida’s Legislature opened its new term with the House speaker urging lawmakers to move quickly on artificial intelligence, while the Senate president put affordability at the top of his agenda. Both leaders took office with a $12 billion question hanging over local budgets after voters approved a sweeping property tax cut. The Jacksonville Business Journal reported the opening on November 18, 2026, and noted that a new Florida House panel will focus on AI and digital security. The same report pointed to related action on Amendment 3, which state leaders had delayed in special session.

The property tax cut approved by voters leaves local governments facing a $12 billion gap, and the article ties that figure directly to the budgets the new term must address. The House speaker wants fast movement on AI, and a new House panel will focus on AI and digital security. The Senate president’s priority is affordability, which the article places at the top of his agenda. The report also lists related coverage on flying cars taking another step forward in Florida, without giving further detail.

Responsibility sits with the new House speaker and the Senate president, who each set a priority as the term began. The speaker urged lawmakers to move quickly on AI, and the Senate president put affordability first. The article does not name either leader or give direct quotations beyond those paraphrased positions. It also does not say what specific AI legislation the speaker wants or what affordability measures the Senate president supports.

The context is a term opening under the weight of the voter-approved property tax cut and its $12 billion effect on local budgets. The article notes that Florida leaders had delayed a special session on Amendment 3, and that Governor DeSantis had called a special session on the property tax cut. What happens next is not detailed beyond the speaker’s call for speed on AI and the Senate president’s affordability focus. The article gives no timeline for legislation, no vote counts and no further statements from either leader.

stories.Headline: Henna Virkkunen hosts Brussels Apply AI Summit and presents first startup award
stories.Summary:
Nearly 1,000 high-level policymakers, start-ups, industry leaders and researchers will take part in the Apply AI Summit in Brussels on 17 November 2026, the European Commission has announced. They will discuss how artificial intelligence can boost Europe’s competitiveness across 10 strategic sectors and the public sector, according to the press release. The summit will also showcase concrete AI applications, European success stories and innovative projects. Henna Virkkunen, Executive Vice-President for Technological Sovereignty, Security and Democracy, will host the summit and present the first Apply AI Startup Award to three European start-ups. The award recognises innovative European startups and scaleups developing AI solutions in the strategic sectors, the Commission said.

Alongside the in-person event, an online conference platform will run from 16 to 20 November, allowing an additional 2,500 participants to join part of the summit. The Apply AI Summit marks one year since the adoption of the Apply AI Strategy, which sets out how to speed up the use of AI in Europe’s key industries and the public sector. It concludes the first European AI Innovation Month, running from 14 October to 17 November 2026, organised by the European Commission in partnership with the Irish Presidency of the Council of the European Union. Virkkunen, as Executive Vice-President for Technological Sovereignty, Security and Democracy, is responsible for hosting the summit and presenting the first Apply AI Startup Award to the three winning European start-ups. The Commission organised the European AI Innovation Month in partnership with the Irish Presidency of the Council of the European Union.

The press release does not say what the three start-ups said or name them. The articles give no further statements from the hosts or participants. The summit is tied to the Apply AI Strategy, which the Commission adopted one year before the event and which sets out how to speed up the use of AI in Europe’s key industries and the public sector. The articles do not say what happens after the summit beyond the online platform running until 20 November. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Hong Kong Monetary Authority explores agentic AI to detect crypto financial crime
stories.Summary:
The Hong Kong Monetary Authority began exploring the use of agentic AI to monitor crypto asset transactions on Tuesday, November 18, 2026. Executive Director Raymond Chan announced this initiative during a speech at a workshop hosted by the central bank to combat money laundering. This new technology aims to analyze both onchain transfers and offchain customer transactions to identify anomalies. The system would specifically flag rapid fund layering that occurs when users switch between cryptocurrency and fiat money.

This approach requires integrating blockchain analytics, scam intelligence, and customer due diligence into a single on-chain AI agent. Such a system would allow for the monitoring of suspicious wallets and the rapid freezing of illicit funds. Raymond Chan noted that illicit addresses received over 150 billion dollars in 2025, with stablecoins making up 84 percent of those transactions. He also highlighted the Virtual Asset Intelligence Taskforce, which was established in November 2025 to strengthen these efforts.

Raymond Chan stated that the central bank wants to make financial crime monitoring more effective and efficient through AI. He explained that criminal networks use digital assets for human trafficking and fraud because of their global reach and pseudonymity. Chan admitted that no single tool provides complete protection, so the city must rely on multi-layered safeguards. He noted that the primary challenge is quickly linking digital wallet activities to real-world identities to stop funds from disappearing.

The Virtual Asset Intelligence Taskforce treats crypto crime as an ecosystem issue involving regulators, law enforcement, and trading platforms. This public-private group includes the Hong Kong police, the Customs and Excise Department, and the Securities and Futures Commission. By collaborating with licensed crypto trading platforms, the task force has already improved the quality of intelligence. These agencies continue to work together to strengthen the prevention and detection of crimes across the entire digital asset landscape.

Articles.Title: Hong Kong central bank explores agentic AI to detect crypto-related financial crime

stories.Headline: Doubao Work reaches 2 billion yuan in annual recurring revenue within three months of launch
stories.Summary:
Doubao Work reached an annual recurring revenue of 2 billion yuan by November 18, 2026. The AI office application was launched only three months before hitting this financial milestone. Its daily active users have now exceeded 8 million people. Many enterprises integrated the tool into production line management and quality audits. These companies also used the AI for equipment operation and maintenance.

The system combines with Feishu collaboration to turn implicit knowledge into reusable organizational assets. In Changzhou, Ninebot uses the tool to automate 16 daily forms for attendance and overtime. This automation saves two clerks between 20 and 30 minutes of work every day. The tool also manages standard working hours and manpower data for different models. It now includes a memory function to reduce redundant data entry for line leaders.

He Yuchong, a production management specialist, used Doubao Work to polish functions based on site pain points. He described specific operation paths and expected effects to the AI to modify the system. He first troubleshot errors himself before telling the AI the phenomenon and repair logic. He then asked actual clerks and line leaders to test each updated version for convenience. He aimed to let AI take over repetitive tasks to free energy for high-value work.

Front-line engineers in Wuhan and Changzhou, and across a national supplier network, use these tools. Line leaders previously complained about redundant actions, such as selecting the same product model ten times daily. Managers formerly had to scroll through dozens of chat records or nested folders to find data. Now, managers use mobile terminals to check real-time output and efficiency while patrolling lines. Bosch China engineers also use the system to reduce time spent moving information.

TSMC faced high costs when building a wafer fab in Phoenix, Arizona, on December 6, 2022. The US plant cost 4 to 5 times more than plants in Taiwan, China. Compliance with 18,000 rules cost 35 million US dollars, and gross profit margins were only 8 percent. TSMC sent 500 engineers from Taiwan and trained 600 Arizona hires in Taiwan, China. These challenges delayed the 4-nanometer production line originally scheduled for mass production in 2024.

The AI tool now runs dashboards on large screens at the head of each production line. It automatically sends messages to responsible persons to remind them of stand-up meeting problems. The articles do not state the specific future revenue targets for Doubao Work. They leave open how other manufacturing sectors will integrate these specific AI organizational processes. The text does not detail the final results of the Bosch China implementation.

stories.Headline: AI-driven security updates overwhelm legacy systems and cause widespread outages, officials tell Congress
stories.Summary:
Over the past month, a series of major outages took down a wide range of services, including a nationwide ground halt that stopped all US airfare for hours, days without access to core Microsoft services such as Outlook and Teams, disruptions at Apple's App Store and Apple Pay, major problems at US banks, and delays and cancellations at United Airlines after a system outage. The National Security Agency's in-house communications network for classified information also went down earlier this week. According to the Washington Sun, Wall Street and NSA sources have told Congress that the outages are being triggered by system updates designed to thwart future attacks by AI. Lawmakers have been flummoxed by the outages and a spate of wide-ranging hacks, and early indications suggest that suspicions AI played a role appear to be warranted, though there is nuance in exactly how.

The updates are meant to bolster defenses as AI continues to identify glaring cybersecurity vulnerabilities that could be exploited by bad actors, and load-bearing organizations appear to have inadvertently overwhelmed their systems while pushing them through. A congressional official told the Washington Sun that the models are identifying massive vulnerabilities, which increases the urgency to patch right away, and that organizations are trying to push through a lot of patches all at once, more than the system was designed for. Department of Homeland Security secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters on Tuesday that new technology is being pushed on top of really old computer systems, which overwhelmed them, and he said he could say with 98 percent certainty that this is not a cyberattack. Officials have continued to reassure the public that the outages are not related to any cybersecurity threats.

Experts have warned for years that AI is a dangerous double-edged sword, since it can give cybersecurity researchers a major leg up in identifying possible new attacks, and earlier this year Anthropic claimed in a report that its Claude Mythos model had found more than ten thousand vulnerabilities in existing software. Hackers can use the same tools to exploit these vulnerabilities, setting the stage for an arms race as companies rush to patch the defects. Encode chief strategy officer Nathan Calvin told the Washington Sun that there is some sense in which this is reassuring, in that it means there is not an attack, but that it shows the extent to which safety critical infrastructure we rely on is based on software with large vulnerabilities on legacy systems. To Calvin, it is an arms race that will more than likely drag on as we get more advanced models.

Articles.Title: Banks and the NSA Admit That Yes, It Was AI That Caused the Massive Outages
