stories.Headline: KAIST team develops KORMo-Web AI agent that operates websites for shopping and online tasks
stories.Summary:
A research team led by Professor Lim Kyung-taek at the KAIST Graduate School of Culture Technology developed an AI agent called KORMo-Web. On November 17, the team announced that this model can watch a computer screen like a human to operate a mouse and keyboard. The AI performs various online tasks on behalf of users, such as shopping, writing emails, and creating presentation materials. It can also engage with online communities by automatically writing comments on YouTube videos.

The system requires a massive dataset of over 10 million web screen samples in English and Korean to function. To handle multi-step tasks, the researchers used more than 100,000 records of real user interactions with various websites. A compact model with 4 billion parameters achieved a 42.3% success rate on real websites in both languages. This performance surpassed previous open models by 22.1 percentage points in Korean and 9.6 percentage points in English.

Professor Lim stated that the goal was to have AI understand screens directly rather than connecting separate application programming interfaces for every service. He explained that the team wants to create an environment where small AI installed on personal computers can handle diverse web tasks. To support this goal, the team released three different models, including an in-house version and a small version for personal computers. All program code, training data, and models are provided as open source for anyone to use.

stories.Headline: Heo Seong-beom urges exam cheating countermeasures after AI scandal
stories.Summary:
Broadcaster Heo Seong-beom, a 26-year-old former AI researcher at the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology, posted a video titled "AI Was Not Made to Be Used This Way" on his YouTube channel on the 16th. In that video he said the top scorer on the Certified Public Accountant exam had admitted to cheating with a smart device, and he added that he was deeply distressed by it. He said it was painful that people who exploit AI had appeared before society had established guidelines for the technology. The video was reported by MoneyToday on 17 November 2026.

Heo Seong-beom said the biggest problem is that examinees who have studied hard are having their opportunities taken away by the minority who abuse the system. He argued it makes no sense to proceed with the CSAT as it is without any countermeasures, and he said various preventive measures must be established even if that is a bit troublesome. He cited metal detectors as an effective way to detect cheating, because cameras, communication equipment and earphones are needed to photograph questions, send them to AI and receive answers, so the response should involve detecting batteries. He said students suspected of cheating can be checked through USIM communication records and analysis of exam papers, since data exchanges leave records on the USIM and handwriting can show whether cheating occurred.

He warned those attempting to cheat that cheating will always be discovered and that if they catch them, they catch everyone. He told friends who decided to cheat because they thought they could get away with it this time that it is a matter that will ruin their lives, and he hoped they would not do it. To examinees who may feel confused, he said people like these bad actors have existed in every era, and he encouraged them not to worry and to go their own way even if they wonder why they should study in an era like this. Heo Seong-beom attended the Korea Science High School for the Gifted and the Department of Computer Science at KAIST, is currently enrolled in the AI Graduate School, and became known through CSAT explanation videos, lecturing and appearances on Coupang Play's "University War" and Wavve's "Blood Game 3."

stories.Headline: OECD study finds German media overreports autonomous vehicles and large language models in AI incident coverage
stories.Summary:
The OECD AI Policy Observatory published a paper on 17 November 2026 analysing live data from the OECD.AI Incidents and Hazards Monitor to compare how 15 thematic clusters of AI incidents and hazards appear in German-language media against global trends. The analysis found three themes overrepresented in German-language coverage, namely autonomous vehicles, intellectual property, and large language models. It found two themes underrepresented, namely synthetic media, and cyberattacks and fraud. Coverage of the remaining ten thematic clusters was broadly aligned with global media patterns. The paper says media reports of AI incidents and hazards can shape public perception and political debates, while both the level and thematic focus of media attention vary across regions.

The paper concludes that media representation of AI risks is shaped not only by the nature of AI incidents but also by language-specific and regional contexts. The OECD.AI platform says governments must track and understand AI incidents and hazards to manage risks, and that all actors must be accountable for AI risks. It also says organisations developing advanced AI systems can participate by submitting a report, and that sharing information will facilitate transparency and comparability of risk mitigation measures. The OECD.AI Index assesses countries' progress in implementing the OECD Recommendation on AI. The platform describes itself as an online interactive platform dedicated to promoting trustworthy, human-centric AI, and notes that the GPAI initiative and OECD member countries' work on AI joined forces under the GPAI brand to create an integrated partnership.

The articles do not name individual authors or officials and give no direct statements beyond the platform's general positions on accountability and risk tracking. They describe the OECD as both a regulator and investor in AI as well as a developer and user, and say experts from around the world advise GPAI and contribute to its work. The paper is available for download through the OECD.AI page, and the page invites readers to sign up for the OECD's artificial intelligence newsletter. The articles do not say what policy changes, if any, follow from the findings.

stories.Headline: Baidu and Xiaomi CEOs warn that AI investments are outpacing commercial returns
stories.Summary:
Robin Li Yanhong of Baidu and Lei Jun of Xiaomi issued warnings on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, regarding the current state of artificial intelligence. These leaders spoke during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation CEO Summit held in the city of Shenzhen. They expressed significant concern that the massive investments flowing into the technology are far outpacing the actual commercial returns. This warning comes during a period of market jitters following the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The tech leaders argued that the industry must shift its focus toward building practical applications rather than simply creating more powerful models.

They believe that the true value of artificial intelligence will be determined by how these tools are used in real-world scenarios. This shift is necessary because there is a widening gap between heavy capital expenditure and profitable adoption. Robin Li made these comments just one day after Baidu reported its sixth consecutive quarterly drop in revenue. Robin Li Yanhong stated that the most pressing task for the industry is to identify and develop high-value applications for AI models.

Both he and Lei Jun urged the tech community to prioritize utility over the hype surrounding the technology. They suggested that the current trajectory of spending could lead to an artificial intelligence bubble if returns do not materialize. The executives emphasized that the ability to generate profit depends on finding the right use cases for the existing models. More to follow.

stories.Headline: CATL searches for an AI model to accelerate battery research and scientific discovery
stories.Summary:
CATL founder and CEO Zeng Yuqun announced the search for an AI Einstein during a panel discussion at the Apec CEO Summit 2026. This event began on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, in the city of Shenzhen. The company wants to find an artificial intelligence model that can accelerate scientific research and drive growth through innovation. This initiative comes as the Chinese battery giant deals with several market setbacks and headwinds.

The project requires a specialized AI model capable of working far beyond the current applications of existing technology. Zeng Yuqun questioned Robin Li Yanhong, who is the co-founder and CEO of the AI pioneer Baidu, about the capabilities of current large language models. The goal is to determine if these existing tools are good enough to drive the necessary breakthroughs. The company believes a more advanced system is needed to speed up the pace of scientific discovery.

Zeng Yuqun is responsible for leading this search to ensure the company maintains its competitive edge in the battery market. He explained that the company is actively seeking a tool that can function like a digital genius to solve complex problems. By integrating such a model, CATL hopes to overcome current obstacles and accelerate the development of new battery technologies. The company aims to move past standard AI uses to achieve significant scientific leaps.

stories.Headline: Nscale deploys its first NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 AI supercomputers in a global rollout
stories.Summary:
Nscale has brought online its first NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, the company said on 18 November 2026, using the newest rack-scale supercomputers for artificial intelligence to begin a global rollout expected over the coming months. The systems are Dell PowerEdge XE9812 servers built on the NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 design, and the company said they give businesses that develop and run AI more of the computing power they need. Customers will use the machines to train and run large AI models that work through complex problems step by step. Each Vera Rubin NVL72 rack holds 72 NVIDIA Rubin graphics processing units, the chips that carry out the heavy maths behind AI, along with 36 NVIDIA Vera CPUs, memory and high-speed connections. The parts are built to run as a single AI supercomputer.

With the launch, Nscale became the first in the industry to deploy a new Dell networking rack that is put together and tested at the factory, complete with switches, power and liquid cooling, and shipped fully populated. That removes network rack assembly at the site and speeds up deployment. Nscale connects the GPUs with two layers of networking, NVIDIA NVLink high-speed links inside each rack and a purpose-built, standards-based version of Ethernet between racks, to keep many chips working on one job without sitting idle. The company's Fleet Operations platform manages each system from setup and burn-in testing through repairs and retirement, and watches the whole fleet in real time to catch problems early. Customers can see the signals they need on the platform, including what capacity is available and what is under maintenance.

Ihab Tarazi, chief technology officer for compute and networking at Dell Technologies' Infrastructure Solutions Group, said the deployment marks an industry first for a factory-built, fully integrated, liquid-cooled networking rack, and that Dell PowerRack validates compute, networking, power and cooling in the factory, cutting onsite work and helping Nscale reach production faster. Dion Harris, senior director of HPC and AI hyperscale infrastructure solutions at NVIDIA, said the next generation of AI factories needs tightly integrated compute and networking to support reasoning and agentic AI at scale, and that Nscale is expanding the infrastructure customers need to train more capable models and scale inference. Nidhi Chappell, president of AI infrastructure at Nscale, said demand for AI compute is carrying customers into a new age of reasoning and agentic workloads, and that the company expects to continue a global rollout over the coming months as a single production environment run by the same fleet automation as the rest of its cloud.

Demand for such systems is rising as AI changes, because the most advanced models now carry out multistep tasks on a user's behalf and need far more computing power than earlier AI applications. Nscale describes itself as a full-stack AI cloud platform that brings together software, compute and power, from a unified cloud platform for AI training and inference to the data centers and low-cost power behind it. Additional systems are expected to come online in the months ahead, and customers can contact the company to place orders or discuss timing.

stories.Headline: Lee Jin-woo skips pledged Suneung livestream as police probe AI cheating claims
stories.Summary:
Lee Jin-woo, the top scorer on this year's Legal Education Eligibility Test, failed to appear for a livestream he had pledged to hold on Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026, at the Daechi IDA Admissions Research Institute in Gangnam-gu, Seoul, where he was scheduled to arrive by 8:40 a.m. The 32-year-old first-year dentistry student at Seoul National University had planned to solve the Korean-language section of Thursday's Suneung exam in real time. Instructors from Megastudy and Daesung MyMac, as well as reporters, were to be present for the livestream. Lee failed to appear and could not be reached despite repeated attempts to contact him. An official at Daechi IDA said his phone was turned off and he had not responded to KakaoTalk messages, and that they had been trying to reach him since the previous day.

Lee had planned to answer 56 questions in just 65 minutes, covering both elective subjects, Speech and Writing as well as Language and Media, while the Korean-language section normally allows 80 minutes for 45 questions. The livestream was to run on his Instagram account from 9:30 a.m. to 12:20 p.m. Thursday at the Daechi IDA institute in Gangnam-gu, Seoul. Lee earned perfect scores in both the reading comprehension and logical reasoning sections of the LEET, administered in July for admission to law schools in 2027. The LEET was introduced in 2008 as the country transitioned from the traditional bar examination system to a law school system, and it assesses applicants' reading comprehension, logical reasoning and aptitude for legal studies rather than their knowledge of law, and also includes an essay-writing section that individual law schools may consider. Lee was not the first person to achieve a perfect score on the LEET, as a legal professional who ranked first nationwide in the 2013 exam also earned full marks, news reports said.

Lee explained that he misinterpreted the questions' requirements after losing concentration toward the end of the exam. He told a local news outlet that the livestream was intended to quickly verify his abilities using newly released exam questions that could not have been leaked in advance. He had also faced allegations of falsifying his past Suneung score reports, and the reports he posted on social media for the exams he took in 2012, 2017, 2023 and 2025 all bore his current name, Lee Jin-woo, which he adopted after legally changing his name. He had previously used a different name while attending Korea University before enrolling at Seoul National University, raising questions about whether the reports had been altered. An official from the Korea Institute for Curriculum and Evaluation, which administers the exam, told Newsis that score reports generally retain the name used at the time of registration unless formally changed through administrative procedures.

Questions about Lee's performance arose after he showed his exam booklet in an interview with YouTuber Mimiminu, known for content on college entrance exam preparation, and viewers noticed that Lee had corrected his answers to questions 25 through 29, with his original choices matching the correct answers to questions 24 through 28, fueling speculation that he had mistakenly shifted answers copied from an outside source. Some speculated that he may have mistakenly shifted the answers by one question while copying them from an external source, possibly AI, and the fact that the corrections appeared on the test booklet itself, rather than on the answer sheet where such mistakes typically occur, fueled further suspicions. The controversy gained momentum following a separate case in which the highest scorer on this year's national tax accountant qualification exam admitted to using AI to obtain answers during the tests. Lee faced similar allegations over his Suneung results, in which he got just one question wrong, and a person claiming to have tutored Lee just days before last year's college entrance exam said he lacked even basic high school-level knowledge of biology. His reported Suneung scores show a dramatic improvement over the years: in 2012, in his first Suneung, he received grades of 6 to 8 across subjects on a nine-grade scale with 1 being the highest and 9 the lowest, in his second exam in 2017 he scored 7 in Korean language, 1 in math and 4 in English with grades of 2 to 3 in the remaining subjects, by 2023 his grades had improved to grades of 1 or 2 in major subjects, and for last year's exam he earned the top grade of 1 in every subject.

Police have launched an investigation into Lee over allegations of cheating on the LEET and last year's Suneung, following a criminal complaint filed Wednesday by Bang Min-woo of Min Law Firm and Park Eun-sun of Reason Law Office on charges including obstruction of business. Nearly 552,000 students registered for the final exam under the current system, and parents braved freezing temperatures outside a Seoul testing center on the tense Suneung morning. President Lee Jae Myung on Tuesday ordered additional measures to curb AI-assisted cheating during Thursday's college entrance exam, with a proposed reward of at least 100 million won, or $75,000, for tips. A separate report addressed why phones across Korea blared emergency alerts Thursday, even on silent. The articles leave open whether Lee will reschedule the livestream and what the police investigation will find.

stories.Headline: Kenilworth residents form nonprofit and push data center bans as CoreWeave builds
stories.Summary:
A 40-megawatt data center has been under construction for a year in the Borough of Kenilworth, New Jersey, including more than 30 diesel-fueled generators that are the size of tractor-trailers, according to an ABC7 New York investigation published on Wednesday, November 18, 2026. Tiffany Haltom, who lives in a nearby town, said she did not know anything about the center until after it was under construction and found out this spring through a Facebook group for moms. She helped create and became president of a nonprofit fighting the facilities, the Union County Residents Alliance Coalition, and said the issue snowballed from there. Many Kenilworth council meetings have been tense since then, with residents from nearby towns giving public comment against the project, and the first phase is already a done deal. Under former Gov. Phil Murphy, the company behind it, CoreWeave, received up to $250 million in state tax credits.

The group is going into every town and attending meetings to push for data center bans, and it has made progress in the areas surrounding Kenilworth in just the past few months. Cranford Township and Roselle Park to the south and Union Township to the north passed bans on data centers, along with the cities of Linden and Summit, while officials in Westfield say they are considering a similar ban. A Springfield Township committee recently expressed support for a moratorium, and Scotch Plains leaders say data centers are not permitted under current zoning laws. Members of the nonprofit say they are not against data centers but do not want communities rushing to build them. New York State hit pause on building new ones for a year, while New Jersey did not.

A CoreWeave spokesperson said the company is funding approximately $150 million in electrical infrastructure upgrades, including a new substation, so grid improvement costs are not passed on to local ratepayers, and that the facility will use closed-loop cooling and sound controls designed to meet local noise standards. The spokesperson said CoreWeave is a New Jersey-based company formed by founders working in Union County and headquartered in Livingston, and that the Kenilworth project includes more than 140 data center jobs and 1,500 union construction jobs. The company said it has maintained a dialogue with neighboring communities, including multiple conversations with local leaders about power, water, sound and project plans, and will continue those conversations as the project moves into operation. Eyewitness News reached out to all of the council members in Kenilworth, who would not speak with the station, and their attorney sent a statement.

The attorney said the Mayor and Council have a responsibility to protect residents' financial interests, health and safety, and that the Borough has complied with all public notice requirements, including public hearings in 2024 and 2025, while contract negotiations and attorney-client communications remain confidential as permitted by law. The statement said the proposed data centers represent a significant tax ratable that could stabilize or reduce property taxes for residents for years to come, and that the Governing Body is retaining independent, licensed professionals with no past or present relationship with the developer to evaluate potential impacts. It said their findings will help determine whether any concerns require action, that the bipartisan Governing Body is committed to fully vetting the project, and that any claim otherwise is categorically false.

stories.Headline: COP31 observers say AI data centre growth may raise fossil fuel use and strain power grids
stories.Summary:
Observers at the COP31 UN climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, said that the expansion of data centres to power the artificial intelligence boom could increase fossil fuel use, strain power grids and raise electricity prices for ordinary people. Turkey, which is hosting the conference, launched a pledge on November 16 for countries and companies to sign that urges them to seek the technology's potential in finding climate solutions while assessing its growing environmental risks. Turkey said the pledge received 80 endorsements but did not specify who had signed, and The Straits Times understands that Singapore has not signed it. The concerns were voiced as global superpowers remain locked in a race to dominate the emerging field, and some tech leaders such as Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei have separately called for an AI slowdown on oversight grounds.

The pledge and the debate sit alongside a Turkish presidency target for countries to agree at the conference on raising the share of electricity in global energy demand from 20 per cent currently to 35 per cent by 2035 through electrification. UN climate chief Simon Stiell said at the launch that AI offers both great potential and great peril for the battle against global warming, and that people cannot be asked to accept higher bills, more planet heating pollution and deeper inequality today in exchange for promises of a better tomorrow. He called on companies to align their business plans with climate goals and to power their data centres with renewable energy. Alex de Vries-Gao, a researcher at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam who studies the environmental impacts of digital infrastructure, told the paper that AI development should be slowed if its growth cannot be accommodated without increasing fossil fuel use or putting further pressure on grids, and that building data centres first and promising to address the consequences later is not a sustainable approach.

Xueying Wu, co-lead of the Global Big Tech campaign at Greenpeace, said unchecked expansion of AI data centres threatens to derail the global energy transition, noting that an International Energy Agency report showed global data centre electricity consumption will more than double by 2030. Philip Newell, who leads the COP31 Actual Intelligence Unit at the Climate Action Against Disinformation coalition, said data centre growth would not need to slow if tech companies committed to tapping more wind and solar power backed by batteries rather than relying on fossil fuels. Nidhi Upadhyaya of the Atlantic Council's Climate Resilience Center said consumers are already seeing the strain, and that the AI infrastructure construction boom and rising electricity bills were among the main concerns for voters in the November 3 US midterm elections that saw a Democratic victory in Congress. In South-east Asia, data centres currently consume more than 13 terawatt-hours of electricity, a figure the IEA expects to nearly triple by 2035 in a November 9 report, and that current total is equivalent to about a quarter of Singapore's electricity consumption in 2024.

Kirsten Dunlop, chief executive of the independent climate innovation agency Climate-KIC, said data centre expansion should slow down to allow developers to build more sustainable infrastructure. Upadhyaya said it will be critical to ensure that the cost of building data centres is borne by the companies setting them up rather than by consumers, and that grid capacity needs to be re-evaluated and infrastructure retrofitted, upgraded or rebuilt to be more resilient. She also called for guardrails governing where data centres are built, the impacts they will have on neighbourhoods and governance of how AI is used. Hikmat Soeriatanuwijaya of Oil Change International said that with growing resistance to data centres in the US, South-east Asia will need to assess the implications of investments in these areas, while Vries-Gao said governments need to consider who benefits, who pays for the additional infrastructure and what happens to local electricity and water supplies.

stories.Headline: LinkedIn data shows Singapore firms with stronger AI capabilities record higher headcount growth across all sizes
stories.Summary:
LinkedIn released platform data on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, regarding Singaporean firms. The data shows that businesses with stronger artificial intelligence capabilities record higher headcount growth. This trend occurs across all company sizes within the city-state. The findings cover the period from September 2025 to September 2026. These results suggest AI capabilities associate with business growth for smaller companies.

AI-enabled firms have at least 5 per cent of employees with AI-related talent. Mid-market enterprises, with 201 to 1,000 employees, saw a 1.8 percentage point growth advantage. Small and medium businesses, under 201 employees, had a 1.4 percentage point advantage. Singapore ranked second for mid-market growth at 2.3 per cent, behind Germany at 3.5 per cent. Other markets included the UK, Italy, Netherlands, UAE, Australia, France, US, and Brazil.

Chua Pei Ying is the head economist for LinkedIn in the Asia-Pacific region. She stated that AI frees up resources by automating routine tasks and improving productivity. Chua noted that investing in AI skills helps smaller businesses find new ways to grow. She explained that headcount growth differs from hiring rates by measuring net workforce changes. Chua attributed mid-market success to Singapore being a connected regional business hub.

Traditional sectors like utilities, real estate, and logistics show large headcount growth advantages. Utilities recorded a 10 percentage point advantage, while real estate and equipment rental saw 7.3. Transportation and logistics followed with a 4.7 percentage point advantage for AI-enabled firms. Hiring activity softened for all, with large enterprises over 5,000 employees seeing an 11 per cent drop. Mid-market firms saw a 9.4 per cent decline, and smaller businesses saw 10.5 per cent.

Large enterprises have 25.1 per cent AI engineering skills compared to 12.5 per cent for SMBs. AI literacy is 11.4 per cent in large firms but only 3.3 per cent in SMBs. SMB AI engineering skills grew by 3.5 percentage points and literacy by 1.5 percentage points annually. Mid-market enterprises grew by 7 per cent, while smaller businesses grew by 6.7 per cent. SMB average headcount grew by a more modest 1.1 per cent between 2025 and 2026.

Hiring activity in Singapore typically peaks in May and January each year. December and February are the quietest months for recruitment according to decade-long data. Global economic uncertainty has made businesses more cautious about when they recruit new staff. The data does not establish a causal relationship between AI adoption and workforce expansion. The articles leave open how smaller firms will specifically close the AI skills gap.

stories.Headline: Palo Alto Networks beats estimates and agrees to buy Applied Compute for $4.5 billion as shares surge
stories.Summary:
Palo Alto Networks reported a beat-and-raise quarter on Wednesday evening, 18 November 2026, and its stock surged as all signs pointed to how important cybersecurity is in the AI age. Revenue in the company's fiscal 2027 first quarter increased 39% year over year to $3.45 billion, exceeding the Wall Street consensus estimate of $3.31 billion, according to LSEG. Adjusted earnings per share rose 13% to $1.05 in the quarter ended Oct. 31, ahead of the 97-cent LSEG consensus estimate. In after-hours trading shares soared 9%, after a regular Wednesday session rally that saw the stock surge nearly 10%. Palo Alto also announced an acquisition that should get the company even more deeply embedded with customers.

The quarter's next-generation security annual recurring revenue increased 66% year over year in fiscal Q1, a sequential acceleration from the 63% growth rate in the prior quarter, which was itself an acceleration from the 60% in the quarter before that. Net new NGS ARR more than doubled versus the year-ago period. Net new platformizations came in at about 170 in the quarter, more than the previous two first-quarter reports combined, a 2.5 times year-over-year increase. Total remaining performance obligation increased 35% year over year to $21 billion, also ahead of expectations. Palo Alto will acquire Applied Compute for $4.5 billion in an all-stock transaction expected to close in the fiscal 2027 third quarter.

CEO Nikesh Arora said on the call that many of the major disruptions over the last few weeks, including outages across major enterprises and governments, were partially due to unintended consequences of patching and configuration changes, as IT teams cannot patch vulnerabilities fast enough without compromising production environments. He said bad actors are using open-weight models and new frameworks to find and exploit vulnerabilities at unprecedented speed and scale. He said the increased levels of security patches needed now will continue for at least another 18 months, with the same risk of collateral damage, before the risk decreases as customers get smarter about how and when to patch. He said no patch will prevent the bad guys from trying to breach systems, and that every organization must expect and prepare for attacks. He said the most important thing is to modernize the north of $1 trillion of legacy security and IT infrastructure onto real-time platforms.

Arora said open-weight models grew from under 5% of token traffic to more than 60% over the past year, and Palo Alto expects a future with a serving opportunity in the hundreds of billions of dollars of enterprise applications driven by open-weight and open-source adoption. He said Palo Alto landed on Applied Compute because no other team matched the technical pedigree in post-training open-weight models, and expects to reach 100 researchers by year-end. He said, "We have to get in the training business to be able to build a good supervision business," and that if it works the deal could dwarf Palo Alto's cybersecurity abilities. The team expects Applied Compute to add over $1 billion of annual recurring revenue to next-gen security ARR by fiscal 2029, requiring about $3 billion, or less than half a year of free cash flow, in one hundred-plus megawatts of compute capacity over the next three to five years. CFO Dipak Golechha said Palo Alto intends to remain capital light and will maintain strong free cash flow margins through and beyond the capex cycle.

Palo Alto has been volatile with sharp ups and downs since its record-high close of almost $420 on Oct. 6. The Club reiterated its hold-equivalent 2 rating and kept its price target at $400, saying it is not its discipline to chase huge rallies. Jim Cramer's Charitable Trust is long PANW and CRWD. For fiscal 2027 Q2, revenue is expected in the range of $3.53 billion to $3.55 billion, above the consensus estimate of $3.42 billion, according to LSEG. Adjusted EPS is seen in the range of $1.01 to $1.03, which at the $1.02 midpoint beats the LSEG consensus estimate of $1.01 per share.

NGS ARR for fiscal Q2 is projected between $10.2 billion and $10.22 billion, above the FactSet consensus estimate of $9.91 billion, and RPO is expected in the range of $21.5 billion to $21.6 billion, above the consensus estimate of $21.49 billion. For the full fiscal year, total revenue is seen in the range of $14.52 billion to $14.57 billion, well ahead of the $14.17 billion expected, according to LSEG. Adjusted EPS is expected between $4.26 and $4.30, ahead of the $4.18 LSEG consensus estimate and up from the prior range of $4.16 to $4.19 per share. NGS ARR is projected between $11.48 billion and $11.53 billion, ahead of expectations of $11.13 billion and up from the previous range of $11.075 to $11.175 billion, and RPO is expected in the range of $25.3 billion to $25.5 billion versus estimates of $25.3 billion and above the prior outlook of $25.2 billion to $25.4 billion.

stories.Headline: Kyndryl CEO Martin Schroeter says companies must control AI agents and build governance into their design
stories.Summary:
Kyndryl Chairman and CEO Martin Schroeter gave adapted remarks during a fireside chat with cybersecurity expert Nuno Mateus-Coelho at the Web Summit in Lisbon on November 12, 2026. The article was published on kyndryl.com on November 18, 2026, with a read time of one minute. Schroeter said cybersecurity remains top of mind for Kyndryl's customers. He said the world now has two things to deal with: bad actors and agents that are misguided, incorrectly built or uncontrolled. He said bad actors are going to use AI to try to break into systems and that Kyndryl sees it every day.

Schroeter said the second concern is about agents, which he called the new world. He said there are examples of agents moving outside their sandbox or doing things they were not intended to do. He said Kyndryl is building agents for its customers, that they are all controlled, and that Kyndryl has visibility into them. He said Kyndryl knows what the agents are doing, what they are allowed to do and what they cannot do. He said the agents are controlled through what Kyndryl calls Kyndryl Bridge.

Schroeter said you have to create agents, control them and set their permissions the right way, as is done with many other things in infrastructure. He said that at the end of the day agents are software code, but they are relentless, goal-seeking pieces of software. He said agents need to be controlled. He said that across industries, the companies getting this right and thinking ahead have, first and foremost, a complete view of their inventory. He said Kyndryl helps its customers do this.

Schroeter said those companies have a complete view of the hardware, software, operating systems and everything in their inventory. He said they also know what patches have been applied. He said that allows Kyndryl's customers to prioritize what they need to protect specifically, because not everything is equally important. He said the first thing is to know what you have. He said the governance of agents is a top concern.

Schroeter said these companies do not build agents and then try to figure out how to govern them. He said they use tools like what Kyndryl calls policy as code. He said Kyndryl can ingest their business rules, their infrastructure and the business logic they are trying to follow. He said you can then apply the policy you already have in place to the new piece of code you are introducing into your infrastructure. He said governance cannot be an afterthought and has to be part of the design.

Schroeter said you need to be able to shut agents down or control them and make sure you have a resilient system. He said that if you know what you have, build policy governance into the design, and have a way to keep your systems resilient if something goes wrong, you are among the companies at the forefront of this in every industry. The article ends mid-sentence, asking what role industry should play in shielding customers from geopolitical risks and helpi. The article gives no further remarks, no other speakers and no additional dates or figures. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Nvidia revenue grows 103 percent as AI infrastructure demand drives third quarter gains
stories.Summary:
The American chipmaker Nvidia reported a massive surge in third-quarter revenue for fiscal 2027 on November 17. The company earned 115.8 billion U.S. dollars, which represents a 103 percent increase from the previous year and a 20 percent rise from the last quarter. This growth was primarily driven by the ongoing global demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure. The firm also recorded a net income of 65.3 billion dollars for the period ending October 25, nearly doubling its profit from the same time last year.

The data center business generated 107.6 billion dollars, accounting for about 93 percent of total revenue and increasing 110 percent year on year. Financial metrics included a GAAP gross margin of 74.8 percent and GAAP diluted earnings per share of 2.70 dollars. The company expects fourth-quarter revenue to reach approximately 130 billion dollars for fiscal 2027. Additionally, Nvidia returned 28.1 billion dollars to shareholders through cash dividends and repurchased shares during the third quarter. The board previously approved a 150 billion dollar increase to share repurchases, leaving 227.3 billion dollars remaining in that authorization.

Interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress is now responsible for the company after founder Jensen Huang stepped down from his role. Kress stated that the company's momentum is real and praised the relentless innovation of the staff. She noted that the Vera Rubin project has had an explosive start and that the company's roadmap remains on track. Kress further emphasized that the ambition of the technology leader has never been greater than it is now.

Nvidia will pay a quarterly cash dividend of 25 cents per share on December 23 to shareholders of record on December 2. This payment follows the strong financial performance reported in the first quarterly report since the change in leadership. The company continues to focus on expanding its AI infrastructure capabilities to maintain its position as a technology leader. Future growth depends on the successful execution of the current roadmap and the continued demand for high-end chips.

stories.Headline: Xinhua Institute report says AI reshapes global information ecosystem and communication power balance
stories.Summary:
A Chinese think tank has reported that artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping the global information ecosystem and the balance of power in communication, bringing both new opportunities and new challenges. The report, titled "AI Plus Media: Global Development Report 2026," was compiled by the Xinhua Institute and released during the 7th World Media Summit in Beijing. It was published on November 11, 2026, and the summit itself ran from November 5 to 9 under the theme "Media in the Intelligent Age: From Consensus to Action." Nearly 500 representatives from almost 330 media outlets, think tanks and government bodies in 112 countries and regions attended, along with the United Nations and other international organizations.

According to the report, advances in generative technology are expanding the supply of content while also making it easier than ever to fabricate it. It describes several paradoxes in AI's effect on the industry. AI platforms are opening new routes to reach audiences, yet they weaken the direct link between news outlets and their readers. AI tools are raising production efficiency, but they also place new demands on the organizational abilities and professional standards of media organizations.

The report adds that the spread of the technology is helping more people while widening the AI divide between regions. The report calls on news media worldwide to act as enablers of technological inclusiveness, pioneers in digital ethics, co-builders of rules for applications, guardians of digital rights and interests, and bridge-builders for exchange and mutual learning. It argues that global news media should work together to build a new information and communication order that is trustworthy, fair and oriented toward the common good. The authors are the Xinhua Institute, which compiled the document.

The article does not give further statements from individual officials about the report. The World Media Summit was first held in 2009 and has since become a major global platform for media exchange and cooperation. The article presents the report as a contribution to that discussion rather than as a binding measure. It does not say what follow-up steps, if any, the report's recommendations will lead to.

stories.Headline: Armenia approves seven-year program to develop physical AI and robotics
stories.Summary:
Armenia has officially approved a comprehensive seven-year program to develop physical artificial intelligence, which focuses on robotics and intelligent systems. This strategic initiative was announced on November 17 and aims to train specialists who can compete on an international level. The program targets the creation of AI systems that can interact directly with the physical world through machines. Local media reports indicate that the government intends to build a strong foundation for future technological growth.

The project requires a collaborative effort through public-private partnerships and co-financing involving three major academic institutions. Yerevan State University, the National Polytechnic University of Armenia, and the American University of Armenia will all participate in the implementation. State funding for the initial phase is set at 1.684 billion drams, which is approximately 4.3 million U.S. dollars. These funds will primarily cover the salaries of researchers and the development of necessary infrastructure, while private investors are expected to provide more money.

The government has set specific goals for the seven-year period, including the training of about 330 graduates. They aim to secure around 10 major research grants and register at least one patented invention during this time. The program also plans to organize 12 scientific conferences and establish five new startups or spin-off companies. Additionally, the participating universities intend to publish about 20 papers in academic journals that are ranked internationally.

Those responsible for the program seek to develop specialized research teams at the participating universities to ensure long-term success. They believe that strengthening cooperation with international academic networks will be essential for the growth of physical AI. The initiative focuses on creating a sustainable ecosystem where academic research translates into practical, intelligent machines. By integrating public funding with private investment, Armenia hopes to establish itself as a hub for robotics and intelligent systems.

Articles.Title: Armenia launches 7-year program to develop physical AI - Xinhua

stories.Headline: Australian Capital Equity CEO identifies growth potential in China AI and manufacturing
stories.Summary:
Yizhou He, the managing director and China CEO of Australian Capital Equity, discussed investment opportunities during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation CEO Summit 2026. This event took place on Tuesday and Wednesday in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, where he shared his views on the local economy. He explained that the combination of artificial intelligence and advanced manufacturing provides the most promising prospects for international investors. His company has already acquired equity stakes in several technology firms based in the city of Shenzhen.

He believes that the next five years must focus on growth quality by translating scientific advances into higher productivity and globally competitive businesses. This strategy requires prioritizing foundational technologies and infrastructure over standalone applications, as breakthroughs often demand years of patient capital. He evaluates frontier technologies based on their reliability, measurable value in real applications, and a credible path toward a scalable business model. He also highlighted the potential of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area to merge manufacturing strength with financial expertise and digital asset ecosystems.

Yizhou He stated that China's ability to turn innovation into industrial strength supports his confidence in the long-term economic outlook. He noted that core AI technologies and industrial applications reinforce each other, allowing innovations to reach production lines at a massive scale. Regarding international expansion, he suggested that headquarters should set clear governance expectations while giving local teams the authority to act. He also argued that closer cooperation on the mutual recognition of testing results and clearer regulatory guidance would make cross-border projects much smoother.

Articles.Title: Investor sees long-term growth potential in China‘s AI sector - China Daily Global Edition

stories.Headline: UNESCO official urges AI to serve culture while preserving human meaning
stories.Summary:
Shahbaz Khan, the director of the UNESCO Regional Office for East Asia, spoke at a forum in Changsha, Hunan province, on Monday. This event was the 2026 International Youth Forum on Creativity and Heritage along the Silk Roads. He discussed how artificial intelligence can assist people in sharing stories about their heritage through innovative methods. However, he emphasized that only human beings can provide the actual meaning to these cultural narratives.

The use of AI requires a careful balance to ensure it serves culture without causing harm. It offers new possibilities for researching, documenting, transmitting, and raising awareness regarding living heritage. These tools must not extract cultural knowledge without consent or misrepresent the traditions of various groups. Furthermore, the technology should not treat heritage as mere data that is detached from the communities sustaining it.

Shahbaz Khan explained that while AI provides helpful tools, it also poses significant risks to cultural integrity. He argued that the technology must remain a servant to human creativity and community identity. The official stressed that the human element is essential for maintaining the authenticity of historical stories. He cautioned against the dangers of stripping cultural knowledge away from its original social context.

stories.Headline: iQIYI returns to non-GAAP operating profit by using AI to increase efficiency
stories.Summary:
The online entertainment provider iQIYI reported its financial results for the third quarter of 2026 on November 17, 2026. The company achieved a return to non-GAAP operating profit by utilizing artificial intelligence to increase efficiency and implementing strict cost cuts. These strategic measures helped the firm offset the impact of a lighter content slate during the period. The company successfully narrowed its operating loss to 41.9 million yuan from 121.8 million yuan the previous year.

Revenues for the quarter fell ten percent year over year to 6.01 billion yuan, or 896.0 million dollars. Membership services revenue dropped six percent to 3.97 billion yuan, while content distribution and other revenues fell by 38 percent and 39 percent respectively. Online advertising grew three percent, and content costs decreased 13 percent to 3.52 billion yuan. The firm held 4.04 billion yuan in cash and short-term investments as of September 30, 2026, and spent 76.4 million dollars to repurchase 64.2 million ADSs.

Chief Executive Officer Gong Yu stated that the company maintained the top domestic market share for films, children's content, and long-form dramas. He noted that short-form dramas reached the top quarterly share for the first time under a new social media model. Chief Financial Officer Tian Ying explained that the company intends to improve investment efficiency through a larger portfolio of revenue-sharing content. Both executives highlighted that the integration of decentralization and artificial intelligence is producing encouraging early results for the business.

Articles.Title: iQIYI's AI-driven efficiency push pays off in Q3 - China Daily Global Edition

stories.Headline: Tencent and the China-Britain Artificial Intelligence Association host AI collaboration event in London
stories.Summary:
More than one hundred artificial intelligence researchers and professionals gathered in London on Friday, November 13, 2026, to discuss the connection between academic study and industrial innovation. The China-Britain Artificial Intelligence Association and the Chinese technology giant Tencent hosted the event to foster deeper collaboration between the two nations. Speakers at the conference included representatives from the University College London, Oxford University, and various business units within Tencent. These experts focused on the intersection of cutting-edge research and the practical application of technology in the real world.

The event required a collaborative effort to highlight how the United Kingdom and China possess highly complementary strengths in the field of intelligence. Ding Mingqin, who serves as the minister counselor and head of the science and technology section at China's Embassy in the UK, emphasized the need for international cooperation on global governance. He noted that while the UK maintains a competitive edge in frontier research, China excels in engineering, advanced manufacturing, and large-scale industrial deployment. This synergy creates a solid foundation for future collaboration because China is currently one of the largest markets for AI applications.

Ding Mingqin stated that China remains consistently committed to strengthening international partnerships to ensure the responsible development of these powerful technologies. Richard Parnes, a senior director at Tencent Games, argued that artificial intelligence cannot replace human taste or the judgment that gives meaning to creative work. He compared the rise of AI to the introduction of spreadsheets, suggesting that technology makes talented creative teams unbeatable rather than replacing them entirely. Simon Stringer from the Oxford Centre for Theoretical Neuroscience and Artificial Intelligence and Professor Peter Latham from the Gatsby Computational Neuroscience Unit also shared their specialized research.

The participants engaged in a panel discussion where they shared diverse opinions on cross-border collaboration and the implementation of real-world innovation. They explored the complex connections between the human brain and large language models to better understand how artificial intelligence can evolve. By bridging the gap between academia and industry, the attendees hoped to accelerate the pace of technological breakthroughs through shared knowledge. The conference concluded with a collective agreement that human oversight remains essential for the meaningful application of these advanced digital tools.

stories.Headline: Giovanni Carraro says open-weight AI models give enterprises more control over cost and customization
stories.Summary:
Open-weight AI models are creating new possibilities for how organizations deploy, customize and manage artificial intelligence, according to a Kyndryl article published on 18 November 2026. Unlike proprietary models, which are typically accessed through a provider, open-weight models give enterprises the option to run AI within their own infrastructure. The article says open-weight AI is expanding enterprise choice and changing how leaders evaluate cost, control and risk. Giovanni Carraro, Senior Vice President, Global Strategic Alliances at Kyndryl, discusses the trade-offs between open and closed models as more firms move from experimentation to enterprise-wide AI adoption. The article asks why open-weight AI models are gaining attention among enterprise leaders.

Carraro says organizations are moving beyond experimentation and thinking more seriously about how AI fits into their operations, infrastructure and long-term business strategies. He says cost, control and customization are driving much of the interest, and some organizations are finding that open-weight models can be a part of their enterprise tools. Open-weight models allow organizations to access, download and customize trained AI models to meet specific business needs, giving them greater control over where AI runs, how data is managed and the cost model under which it operates. He says that flexibility may become increasingly valuable as enterprises balance growing demands with operational and financial considerations. The article says the flexibility raises important questions about cost, sovereignty, security and long-term strategy.

Carraro says the choice between open-weight and closed, proprietary AI models should not be an either-or decision. He says both have advantages, and the right choice depends on an organization's needs and how it plans to use AI. He says it is helpful to think about surfaces and engines, where surfaces are where you access the tool and engines are the AI model the surface directs to. He says proprietary models are typically accessed through web, desktop and mobile applications, through APIs either directly from the developer or via managed cloud platforms, through command-line tools and IDE extensions, and increasingly through integrations embedded in enterprise software. He says the AI provider manages much of the underlying infrastructure in these instances, which can simplify deployment and ongoing maintenance for the end user.

Carraro says proprietary models can still offer choices of hosting location and capacity, and in some cases can offer fine-tuning within the model provider's available options. He says open-weight models can offer greater flexibility over where and how AI operates, and organizations can host them in private cloud or on-premises environments, or even on individual devices. He says organizations can customize certain models for specialized tasks, and some open providers offer models through cloud services, which means they would manage the infrastructure and maintenance. The article says the conversation should not be about whether open-weight or proprietary AI models are better, but about understanding which model can deliver the greatest value to an organization, including meeting its security requirements. The article says organizations may also turn to specialized models, whether open or closed, to achieve their goals.

The article says Kyndryl can help customers navigate their AI partner choices. It says the conversation about enterprise AI is evolving as organizations move beyond experimentation. The article carries a read time of 1 minute and is dated 18-Nov-2026. It says open-weight AI is expanding enterprise choice and changing how leaders evaluate cost, control and risk. The article says it is also important to distinguish open-weight models from other kinds of models.

More to follow.

stories.Headline: New AI platforms help global students and teachers practice and assess Chinese language skills
stories.Summary:
New AI-powered Chinese learning platforms were recently unveiled at the World Chinese Language Conference held in Beijing to support teachers and learners. These digital tools aim to standardize assessments and encourage more global students to practice speaking the language in their classrooms. The Yufei Smart Chinese Classroom connects lesson preparation and oral practice, and it has already been implemented in over 900 schools worldwide. These systems move the concept of artificial intelligence into actual classroom practice to help students find their voice.

The Yufei system was used in a Thai public school with 1,800 students, where 29 teachers manage 70 different classes. Over 330 days, students there generated 23,093 speaking practices and more than 65,000 pronunciation diagnostic records on the platform. In Myanmar, a school with 10,000 students used an AI oral evaluation system for levels 1 to 8 since May 2025. This specific school has held 2,127 oral exams and conducted more than 1.2 million evaluations to ensure scoring consistency. Additionally, the SureChinese 2.0 app from BlingABC now serves over 200,000 registered users and 40,000 monthly active users.

The SureChinese 2.0 platform offers 1,000 guide videos and 7,000 exercises across four HSK 3.0 levels while supporting 12 system languages. CEO Qiao Lei explained that the app evaluates accuracy and fluency while providing pronunciation guidance and automated learning reports. Xie Fei of iFLYTEK stated that the primary goal is to provide tools that do not increase the burdens placed on teachers. Principal Zhang Qiuyuan noted that AI handles repetitive scoring and initial screening, but human review remains necessary for abnormal results. Wang Zhanglong described a dual-teacher model where a virtual teacher leads while local teachers provide essential assistance.

The Yufei International Chinese Education Vertical Large Model was jointly released by iFLYTEK and the Center for Language Education and Cooperation. This model incorporates authoritative teaching materials to help teachers design exercises and explain complex language points more effectively. The technology is designed to provide a reliable content source rather than replacing the professional judgment of human educators. By using color marking to identify specific words, these tools offer targeted exercises for learners from various language backgrounds. These advancements continue to expand the reach of Chinese language education through integrated digital assessment and interactive learning.

Articles.Title: AI tools help global learners find their voice in Chinese - China Daily

stories.Headline: Amateur creators use AI to produce a viral historical short drama with 12 billion views in China
stories.Summary:
A group of six amateurs created a viral AI-generated short drama called Armed Into the Song Dynasty, which first premiered in August. The production team includes a former rideshare driver, a stay-at-home mother, an interior designer, a wholesale business owner, and a former pharmaceutical sales representative. This historical series has already reached ten seasons and consists of approximately 1,000 episodes that each last about three minutes. The show has gathered more than 12 billion views on Bilibili and Douyin, the Chinese version of TikTok.

The series is adapted from a web novel by Chagen’er that began publishing in April and follows five modern soldiers traveling back to the Northern Song dynasty. This production reflects a broader industry shift, as 490,000 micro-dramas were released in the first nine months of 2026, which is 13 times the total for 2025. An October report from the National Radio and Television Administration stated that AI-generated content now makes up over 90 percent of these dramas. The same report noted that the monthly active audience for short dramas has now exceeded 600 million viewers.

Zhang Hansheng, the 54-year-old head of the production team, told domestic media that the series cost roughly 1 million yuan, or 150,000 dollars, to produce. While Zhang declined to share the specific earnings of the team, rumors of high returns have encouraged other grassroots creators to learn AI tools. Some viewers expressed interest in making their own dramas, though others warned about scams involving AI-related courses. This success follows other historical AI dramas like Inkstone Edge Green Plum and Assuming a Noble Identity, which premiered last year.

The rise of these high-quality productions challenges the reputation of short dramas as mindless entertainment featuring formulaic characters and implausible plots. However, critics have requested more scrutiny regarding how artificial intelligence depicts the history of China. Last year, the National Radio and Television Administration began a campaign against AI videos that distort heroic, revolutionary, or historical themes. They specifically targeted content that alters classic television, film, or literary works to ensure historical accuracy is maintained.

Articles.Title: China’s Short Dramas See Quality Shift With AI-Made Historical Hit - Sixth Tone

stories.Headline: Oncologist Avishek Kumar warns that chatbot cancer answers need clinical validation
stories.Summary:
Avishek Kumar, MD, an oncologist, wrote an article published by Onco'Zine on November 18, 2026, about AI in cancer care. He described a person at almost midnight looking at blood work on a phone, with one result flagged in red. The person copied the numbers into an AI chatbot and asked what they meant. The response came back in seconds saying the findings could suggest cancer, and the person began looking up survival rates. Nobody had diagnosed the person with cancer.

Kumar wrote that AI can help detect cancer earlier, as shown by AI-assisted mammography, but findings require clinical validation and physician interpretation. In the 2026 GEMINI study, researchers examined AI-assisted mammogram reading in more than 10,000 women in the United Kingdom. The AI system flagged scans that standard human reading had not led to recall, and after additional review by clinicians, 11 more cancers were diagnosed. In a 2023 JAMA Oncology study, investigators asked an earlier version of ChatGPT for cancer treatment recommendations. Among responses that offered a recommendation, 34.3% included at least one treatment not consistent with the oncology guidelines used in the study.

Kumar said AI could be one of the most useful developments in medicine in his lifetime and is already helping identify suspicious findings on scans. He said he worries when a patient mistakes an AI-generated possibility for a medical conclusion. He said the machine has no idea what that sentence did to the person reading it. He said a dedicated mammography algorithm is not the same thing as a general-purpose chatbot and the two should not be lumped together. He said the 2023 study tested an older system, not every AI model available today, but the broader concern remains.

Kumar wrote that an elevated white blood cell count could reflect infection, inflammation, medications or a blood disorder, and a small lung nodule may need follow-up but is not automatically cancer. He said he looks at the person, their symptoms, medications, prior scans, medical history and family history, and sometimes a trend over several years tells more than one alarming result. A 2026 Nature Medicine study involving 1,298 adults found that people using large language models for medical scenarios did not make better decisions about identifying conditions or seeking appropriate care compared with a control group. Another 2026 study, in npj Digital Medicine, found potentially unsafe advice in responses from several widely used chatbots. A 2024 JAMA Oncology study found that oncologists evaluating written answers to cancer questions rated chatbot responses as more empathetic than physician responses.

Kumar wrote that two people can have the same cancer and the same stage and very different ideas about what they are willing to go through. He said AI can summarize survival curves and treatment options but cannot fully understand what it means to this particular person to miss a family wedding, to lose the ability to work, or to spend another week in the hospital. He said doctors are often rushed and could communicate better, but empathy in a paragraph is not the same as a relationship or accountability for the recommendation. He advised starting with the original result and asking whether the concern was raised by a radiologist or pathologist, by a clinically validated tool, or by a chatbot interpreting something uploaded. He advised contacting the clinician who ordered the test, especially if the finding is described as urgent or there are concerning symptoms, and being thoughtful before uploading personal medical records into an app.

Kumar wrote that patients should not ignore a real abnormality, schedule an expensive scan, assume the worst, or make treatment decisions based only on a chatbot response. He gave the question he would ask a doctor, beginning with what the actual medical evidence suggests in the case. The article ends there, and it does not say what answer a doctor would give or what happened to the person at midnight. It does not say whether any of the studies led to changes in how chatbots are regulated or used. It does not say what Kumar advises beyond contacting the clinician who ordered the test.

Articles.Title: Your AI App Says You Have Cancer. Now What?

stories.headline_source: Your AI App Says You Have Cancer. Now What?

stories.Headline: Unitree CEO warns that AI robotics breakthroughs will strain mass production capabilities
stories.Summary:
Unitree Robotics CEO Wang Xingxing discussed the potential for a technical breakthrough in general-purpose robot models on Tuesday morning. He shared these insights during his appearance at the APEC CEO Summit 2026 held in Shenzhen, Guangdong province. The leader noted that the increasing utility of large language models has created high expectations for robots to solve practical problems. He believes that while the technology is advancing, the ability to scale up production will present significant challenges.

The primary technical obstacle involves creating models that allow robots to function in homes without needing repeated retraining for every unique setting. This advancement would require robots to begin working immediately upon deployment rather than undergoing extensive site-specific adjustments. Such a shift would change how the industry approaches the deployment of general-purpose machines in domestic environments. The goal is to move beyond current limitations to achieve a more seamless integration of AI into physical robotics.

Wang Xingxing is responsible for leading the company and provided these perspectives on the current state of the industry. He explained that the success of AI in other fields has pushed the robotics sector toward similar breakthroughs. The CEO emphasized that the gap between technical possibility and mass production remains a critical point of concern. He suggested that the industry must overcome these specific hurdles before robots can be widely adopted for everyday household tasks.

stories.Headline: Ransomware groups use AI to raise global attacks as ransom payments fall
stories.Summary:
Ransomware groups used AI tools to increase global attacks during 2026, according to reports released in November of that same year. These cybercriminals used large language models to create convincing phishing emails and identify sensitive data more quickly than before. The number of groups claiming success grew from 75 in the first quarter to 111 in the third quarter. These attackers targeted various industries and regions, though the number of attacks on US companies remained fairly steady. The Gentlemen became the most active group, surpassing Qilin in the number of victims they targeted.

Halcyon reported 2,766 claimed breaches in the third quarter of 2026, which was nearly 40% higher than the previous quarter. This figure represents a 31% increase from the first quarter and a 39% increase from the second quarter of 2026. Sophos found that 62% of retail attacks succeeded in encrypting data, compared to 48% in 2025, but only 32% paid. The median ransom demand dropped to $700,000 in 2026, which is a significant decrease from $2 million in 2024. About one third of claimed successes came from groups that did not exist six months prior to the quarter end.

Cynthia Kaiser of Halcyon said AI removed language barriers for phishing, which led to more convincing messages in languages like Japanese. She noted that Japan is treating these AI driven attacks almost as a state of emergency for the country. Chester Wisniewski of Sophos stated that the efficacy of ransomware in generating money for criminals has been declining recently. He observed that local government and school districts are largely not paying ransoms regardless of whether data theft occurred. Duy-Phuc Pham of Trellix explained that AI allows small crews to do the work of large ones faster.

Retail firms were affected, but 71% recovered their data from backups, with most recovering within one week of the attack. Manufacturing remains the top target because shared platforms among partners can expose engineering data beyond the first targeted company. Victims in Europe saw an increase in attacks, while the share of US victims remained the same or decreased. Law enforcement spent the year targeting shared services that these groups depend on, including criminal VPNs and laundering services. These groups continue to broaden their campaigns against more industries and regions due to the scale AI enables.

The articles state that AI allows attackers to scan, exploit, and move through networks with very little human effort required. This technology removes historical barriers to targeting smaller populations by creating social engineering messaging in a variety of different languages. The growth in the number of groups continues to pose a threat even as the ransom payments fall. The manufacturing sector is targeted because a single compromise can expose data across a network of suppliers and partners. These trends show that ransomware is not going away despite the decline in actual money generated for crooks.

The manufacturing sector will likely remain the top targeted group in 2027 as international organizations account for a greater share. Cynthia Kaiser expects continued growth in attacks, especially in regions outside the United States, during the coming year. It remains an open question whether more attacks will actually result in more money for the ransomware groups. The articles suggest that countries newly feeling the pain may improve international cooperation to fight these AI driven threats. The reports leave open whether law enforcement can successfully dismantle the shared services these criminal groups rely upon.

stories.Headline: Varonis reveals TheMailer phishing kit that uses AI to personalize lures and evade filters
stories.Summary:
Varonis researchers revealed a new phishing kit called TheMailer on November 17, 2026. This commercial tool uses attacker supplied AI models to personalize lures and evade filters. The kit allows cybercriminals to scale their campaigns to tens of thousands of targets. It orchestrates most elements of an attack through integrated large language model functionality. The system can rewrite email lures until they successfully bypass various spam filters.

A lifetime license for the kit costs between 3,000 and 6,000 dollars in cryptocurrency. Operators must provide their own SMTP servers, proxies, target email lists, and API keys. The software supports AI models including Claude, ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Grok, Gemini, and Mistral. One campaign showed nearly 25,000 emails sent to a list of 145,000 targets. The tool personalizes the email address, body, subject line, and attachments for every recipient.

Varonis senior security researcher Daniel Kelley wrote about the kit in a blog post. He stated that the tool is built to scale against many different targets. Kelley noted that the personalization is opportunistic rather than being a true spear phishing tool. He explained that the kit removes AI writing patterns to make emails look realistic. He believes more kits will follow because buyers will start asking for these features.

The kit affects organizations that rely on content filters to block malicious email lures. Varonis suggests that defenders enforce email authentication practices like SPF, DKIM, and DMARC. They recommend monitoring for new domains and checking links through full redirect chains. Training should teach users to be wary of urgency and unexpected login prompts. Least privilege access and data monitoring can limit damage if a user clicks.

Phishing kits and phishing as a service platforms have gained popularity in recent years. Most AI functionality previously focused on reconnaissance, coding websites, and automating simple repetitive tasks. TheMailer distinguishes itself by automating the phishing process from end to end using AI. It can generate lures from a short prompt or a real brand email. This represents a degree of AI leverage hardly seen in the cybercriminal ecosystem.

Varonis assesses that TheMailer currently has a large customer base among cybercriminals. It remains unclear how successful the kit is because AI task success rates vary. The articles leave open whether other sellers have already integrated similar AI capabilities. Defenders must now adapt training because bad grammar is no longer a reliable warning sign. Future kits are expected to follow the model established by this specific tool.

Articles.Title: 'TheMailer' Phishing Kit Puts AI in the Driver's Seat - Dark Reading

stories.Headline: Civil servants submit AI and data ideas to a 2026-27 challenge run by NTT DATA with government
stories.Summary:
Civil servants across government were invited to submit ideas for using artificial intelligence and data to improve public services when the 2026-27 Civil Service AI & Data Challenge opened for applications, in a competition run by NTT DATA with the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport and the Cabinet Office. The competition is open to civil servants in all departments, roles and grades, and it asks them to identify problems they encounter in their day-to-day work that could be addressed through better use of AI and data. The strongest proposals will be developed through a Dragons' Den-style competition, and the winning project will receive £50,000 of support to help bring the idea to life. Applications are open until 10 December 2026, and civil servants can submit an idea, volunteer to join a project team, or do both through the Challenge website.

The latest competition follows last year's programme, which has seen at least seven AI and data projects taken forward by government departments and agencies. Among them is an initiative proposed by last year's winner, Marlon Woodley, a verification assurance officer at the Department for Work and Pensions, whose idea focuses on improving the tools available to benefits caseworkers to reduce errors and accelerate decision-making. Previous Challenges have also generated proposals to support peatland restoration and to improve information-sharing between the NHS and the DWP following a death. For the 2026-27 programme, eight teams of civil service volunteers will be established to develop the most promising proposals, supported by a government-wide network of data leaders, and the competition will culminate in July 2027, when a panel of senior Civil Service digital leaders will select the winning project.

Minister for digital government Stephanie Peacock said civil servants across the country see first-hand where technology could make a real difference to people's lives, whether that is speeding up decisions, reducing avoidable admin or making public services easier to use, and that the Challenge gives them the opportunity to turn that experience into action. Government chief data officer Aimee Smith said she saw last year how the Challenge enables civil servants in every role, department and grade to help improve public services, and that it is also a brilliant way for them to improve their skills and experience in digital technologies. David Filmer, head of public sector at NTT DATA UK&I, said AI and data have enormous potential to transform public services and make a tangible difference to people's lives, and that it is a privilege for the company to support civil servants in turning their ideas into reality. The Challenge is also supported by government Chief AI officer Kalbir Sohi and DCMS permanent secretary Susannah Storey.

Woodley said that winning has been a life-changing experience and that he is now involved in a project to see his idea through to implementation, improving the tools used by benefits caseworkers to reduce errors and speed up decisions. The programme is also intended to develop digital skills across the Civil Service by giving participants experience of working on technology projects alongside colleagues from other departments and disciplines.

Articles.Title: Civil servants challenged to turn AI ideas into better public services - THINK Digital Partners
